table.note: Section V Article 1 Mandatory Appendix I defines semi-automated (SAUT) and automated (AUT) examination as performed with equipment and search units mechanically mounted and guided, capable of recording response data including scanning positions via integral encoders. Hand-scanning a phased array probe fails that definition regardless of image quality on screen.

facets.q: Can PAUT be used in lieu of RT on any ASME weld?
facets.a: No. Code Case 2235-13 applies to welds in material 1/2 in. (13 mm) or greater in thickness. Below that there is no in-lieu-of route under that Case. Section VIII Division 1 uses UW-51(a)(4) instead, which routes through Section VIII Division 2 paragraph 7.5.5 and Section V Article 4 Mandatory Appendices VIII and IX. Each route carries its own acceptance philosophy.

facets.q: Is manual phased array accepted as a replacement for radiography?
facets.a: No. Across Sections I, VIII Division 1 and VIII Division 2, permitted substitute examinations are restricted to TOFD and phased array with computer-based data acquisition and analysis, using equipment mechanically mounted and guided by automatic or semi-automatic means. Manual straight beam, manual angle beam and manual phased array are excluded. Manual UT survives in specific allowances such as Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 12 closure seams.

facets.q: What does the procedure demonstration actually require?
facets.a: Under Code Case 2235-13(c), a written procedure conforming to Section V Article 4, demonstrated to perform acceptably on qualification blocks prepared by welding or hot isostatic processing and containing a minimum of three flaws: one surface flaw representing the OD, one representing the ID, and one subsurface. If the block can be flipped during examination, two flaws suffice. Flaw size cannot exceed the applicable Table 1, 2 or 3 value.

facets.q: Why does PAUT struggle on thin sections?
facets.a: Near-field length and wedge dead zone consume the wall you are trying to examine, and the geometry leaves too little path to separate the entry surface signal from a root indication. The codes reflect this: ASME Code Case 2235-13 starts at 1/2 in. (13 mm), and AWS D1.1 Annex H is reported to cover 3/16 in. to 8 in. with encoded linear scanning. Below those floors, radiography stays the practical method.

facets.q: Does an S-scan alone satisfy the code on thick welds?
facets.a: Not comfortably. The footnote to Code Case 2235-13 states that sectorial scans give good detectability from side-drilled holes because those are omnidirectional reflectors, while the beams can be misoriented for planar reflectors such as lack of fusion and cracks, particularly in thicker sections. It recommends multiple linear passes with S-scans for components greater than 1 in. (25 mm) thick, backed by enough flaws in the demonstration block.

facets.q: Who is permitted to analyse encoded PAUT data?
facets.a: Code Case 2235-13(f) requires personnel to be qualified and certified in accordance with their employer's written practice, with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 used as a guideline, and restricts analysis and interpretation to Level II or III personnel. Paragraph (h) adds that anyone who acquires or analyses data must be trained on the specific equipment and take part in the procedure demonstration. Paragraph (g) puts approval of those records with the Certificate Holder.

sections.heading: The Decision Is Made by the Construction Code, Not the Technology
paragraphs: A fabricator who has just bought a 32:128 phased array unit and a scanner still cannot substitute it for radiography on the strength of image quality. The construction code names which volumetric method is required, and swapping it requires a clause that authorises the swap. Section I calls radiography in PW-11. Section VIII Division 1 calls it in UW-11. AWS D1.1 puts radiography in Clause 8 Part E and ultrasonics in Part F. Until you cite the substitution clause, the drawing still says RT.

This is the reason the parent question of RT versus UT does not resolve into a technical comparison. Whether phased array finds a lack-of-fusion plane better than film is not in dispute, and the physics is set out in the companion piece on [RT versus UT weld inspection](/blog/rt-vs-ut-weld-inspection). What is in dispute on a live job is whether the authorised inspector, the jurisdiction and the owner's specification will accept the data package you hand over.

So the workflow runs backwards from the code. Identify the construction code and edition. Find the substitution clause it offers. Read what that clause demands of acquisition, procedure demonstration, acceptance criteria and personnel. Then decide whether the economics still work. Doing that reading before mobilising is what an [ASNT Level III consulting engagement](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) exists to shorten, and it is far cheaper than discovering the gap during a first article.

sections.heading: What ASME Permits, and the Code Case History Behind It
paragraphs: ASME approved Code Case 2235 in 1996, permitting ultrasonic examination of welds in lieu of radiography for Section VIII Division 1 and Division 2 vessels, and it was significant because it introduced fracture-mechanics accept-reject criteria rather than workmanship criteria. That single change made defect allowance considerably more tolerant of an indication a fracture-mechanics analysis showed to be harmless. The Case was revised repeatedly; revision 2235-9 was issued in October 2005 covering Sections I, VIII and XII.

Phased array techniques arrived through their own Code Cases: 2558 for manual phased array E-scan examination per Article 4 in December 2006, 2559 for linear phased array E-scan in January 2008, and 2600 for linear phased array S-scan in January 2008. Those were folded into Section V Article 4 as Mandatory Appendices in July 2010, alongside the TOFD appendix that had been published in 2004. Today Mandatory Appendix IV covers phased array manual raster techniques using linear arrays and Mandatory Appendix V covers phased array E-scan and S-scan linear scanning.

The current picture is a split. Code Case 2235-13, approved July 9, 2014, addresses Section I and Section XII, because Section VIII Division 1 absorbed the substitution into the Code itself at UW-51(a)(4). Section I offers three routes with two different acceptance philosophies: Code Cases 2235 and 2816 use fracture mechanics, while PW-52.1 routes to Section V Article 4 Mandatory Appendix VII and workmanship-based criteria. Choosing the wrong one changes which indications are rejectable.

sections.heading: Manual PAUT Does Not Count
paragraphs: This is the single most common misunderstanding on site. Across Sections I, VIII Division 1 and VIII Division 2, permitted ultrasonic examinations in lieu of radiography are restricted to TOFD and phased array with computer-based data acquisition and analysis abilities, using automatic or semi-automatic equipment that is mechanically mounted and guided on the examination surface. Manual straight beam, manual angle beam and manual phased array are all excluded as substitute techniques.

Section V Article 1 Mandatory Appendix I defines the terms precisely. Semi-automated ultrasonic examination uses equipment and search units that are mechanically mounted and guided and manually driven, recording response data including scanning positions through integral encoders so the acquired data can be imaged. Automated ultrasonic examination is the same with remote, motor-driven operation and no technician adjustment. The common requirement in both definitions is the encoder and the mechanical guide, not the beam-forming electronics.

A technician sweeping a phased array wedge by hand and reading a live sectorial image is doing genuine, useful ultrasonic testing — and is not doing anything that substitutes for required radiography. Manual UT retains specific allowances that are frequently confused with the substitution rules, such as Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 12 for a final closure seam, and Section VIII Division 2 paragraph 7.5.4 for Type 7 and Type 8 joints in some instances. Those are separate permissions with separate scopes.

sections.heading: Why PAUT Wins on Shutdown Avoidance
paragraphs: The economic case for phased array is almost never about finding more flaws. It is about not stopping the plant. Radiography needs a controlled boundary surveyed against the 10 CFR 20 dose limits, physically barriered, posted and kept under continuous direct visual surveillance. Everyone inside that boundary stops working. On a congested unit, one exposure clears a lot more real estate than the weld it examines.

Phased array carries none of that. A crew scans while pipefitters work three metres away, welders continue on the next joint, and scaffolding stays occupied. On a turnaround where the critical path passes through a small number of welds, examining them without emptying the surrounding area moves the whole schedule. That is why owners rather than inspection contractors usually drive the switch — the saving lands on the production account, not the inspection account.

The second win is immediacy. Encoded data is analysed on the spot, so a rejectable indication is known before the crew demobilises and the repair happens in the same window. Radiography introduces a processing and reading cycle between exposure and verdict. On tank and vessel work where access scaffolding is the dominant cost, that cycle time is money, which is why it shows up in [API 653 tank inspector services](/consulting/api-653-tank-inspector-services) planning as often as in weld procedure discussions.

sections.heading: Where PAUT Loses: Thin Sections and Awkward Geometry
paragraphs: The thin-wall floor is real and the codes state it. Code Case 2235-13 opens with welds in material 1/2 in. (13 mm) or greater in thickness — below that, the Case offers nothing. AWS D1.1 Annex H is reported to cover encoded PAUT from 3/16 in. to 8 in., a lower floor than ASME's because structural acceptance criteria differ, but still a floor. Physics sets both: near-field length and wedge dead zone consume the very wall you are trying to interrogate.

Geometry removes more. Nozzle-to-shell welds with compound curvature, set-through configurations, dissimilar-metal welds where the clad interface reflects, austenitic welds where grain structure scatters and steers the beam, and small-bore socket welds where there is no scanning surface all degrade coverage. A scan plan must demonstrate coverage of the required volume, and Code Case 2235-13(a) defines that volume explicitly: weld plus the lesser of 1 in. (25 mm) or t on each side for material 8 in. (200 mm) or under, or 2 in. (50 mm) each side above that.

Sectorial scanning has its own limitation, stated in the Code Case footnote. S-scans demonstrate good detectability from side-drilled holes because those are omnidirectional reflectors, but the beams can be misoriented for planar reflectors such as lack of fusion and cracks, particularly in thicker sections. The Case recommends multiple linear passes with S-scans for components greater than 1 in. (25 mm) thick. A single sectorial sweep sold as full coverage is the classic audit finding.

sections.heading: The Procedure Demonstration Burden Is the Real Barrier
paragraphs: Every substitution route ends at a demonstrated procedure, and the demonstration is where budgets break. Code Case 2235-13(c) requires the written procedure to conform to Section V Article 4 and to have been demonstrated on qualification blocks prepared by welding or the hot isostatic process, containing a minimum of three flaws oriented to simulate flaws parallel to the production weld's fusion line: one at the OD surface, one at the ID surface, one subsurface. If the block can be flipped during examination, two flaws suffice.

Acceptable performance is defined, not asserted. For amplitude-based techniques, response from the maximum allowable flaw and other flaws of interest must exceed the reference level. For techniques that do not use amplitude recording levels, every imaged flaw including the maximum allowable flaws must show an indicated length equal to or greater than the actual flaw length in the block. Flaw size in the block cannot exceed the applicable Table 1, 2 or 3 value for the thickness being examined.

Then comes documentation. Paragraph (b) requires a scan plan showing transducer placement, movement and component coverage, plus beam angles, beam directions relative to weld centreline and the volume examined for each weld, made available to the Owner/User on request. Paragraph (e) requires the complete unprocessed data set with no gating, filtering or thresholding. Building that package once, properly, is a [written practice and procedure development](/consulting/written-practice-development) exercise rather than a field improvisation.

sections.heading: Personnel: Who Is Allowed to Touch the Data
paragraphs: Code Case 2235-13(f) sets the rule plainly: personnel performing and evaluating ultrasonic examinations shall be qualified and certified in accordance with their employer's written practice, with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 used as a guideline, and only Level II or III personnel shall analyse the data or interpret the results. That is a certification requirement and an interpretation restriction in one sentence, and it is checked in audits far more often than the scan plan.

Paragraph (h) tightens it further. Personnel who acquire and analyse ultrasonic data must be trained using the specific equipment named in paragraph (d) and must participate in the demonstration under paragraph (c). A phased array analyst who joined after the procedure was qualified is not covered by that qualification. Paragraph (g) then requires contractor qualification records of certified personnel to be approved by the Certificate Holder and maintained by their employer.

There is a parallel prerequisite on the ISO 9712 side worth knowing if you work internationally: a valid UT Level 2 certification is a prerequisite for a PAUT or TOFD Level 2, and UT Level 3 for the corresponding Level 3. Either way, keeping demonstration participation, method certifications and expiry dates auditable is exactly the problem [NDT personnel certification tracking](/erp/ndt-personnel-certification-tracking) solves, because the record an inspector asks for is the one nobody filed.

sections.heading: The Equipment and Training Step Change
paragraphs: Moving from conventional UT to code-compliant encoded PAUT is a capital step, not an upgrade. The instrument is the smallest part. You add encoders, mechanical scanners or crawlers appropriate to the geometry, wedges matched to each configuration, scan plan software, demonstration blocks with embedded flaws representing the production weld, and data storage and review workstations. Every one of those is required by the acquisition definitions, not optional refinement.

Training is the second step and the one most often underfunded. Published third-party rates give a sense of scale: ASNT's own eLearning catalogue lists a Phased Array Level II course at 80 contact hours priced at $1,365 for members and $1,465 for non-members, and that covers the theory rather than procedure-specific qualification on your blocks. AWS D1.1 Annex H work is reported to require a currently certified Level II UT inspector to add 320 hours of PAUT experience plus a practical examination on two flawed samples.

Multiply that across a crew and the number stops looking like a training line item. It looks like a capability decision with a payback period, which is why fabricators tend to run it as a structured programme against their own mockups through [corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) rather than sending individuals to open-enrolment courses. If you want the transition mapped against your codes and crew before committing, [request a scoping conversation](/contact).

sections.heading: AWS D1.1 Annex H: The Structural Steel Route
paragraphs: Structural steel got its own answer in the 2020 edition of AWS D1.1 with the addition of Annex H (Normative) — Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT), retained in D1.1/D1.1M:2025, the 25th edition. It sits alongside Annex G on qualification and calibration of UT units with approved reference blocks, and Annex N, the informative guidance on UT of welds by alternative techniques. The key word is normative: Annex H is a requirement set the code owns, not commentary.

Annex H brings its own tables. Table H.1 defines essential variables for PAUT, Table H.2 gives PAUT acceptance criteria, and Table H.3 covers discontinuity classification. That replaces the amplitude-and-length judgment of Table 8.2 and Table 8.3 in Clause 8 Part F with criteria written for imaged, encoded data. Annex H is reported to apply from 3/16 in. to 8 in. using encoded linear scanning with a maximum of 1% data loss during acquisition.

For a fabricator this converts a negotiation into a citation. Before 2020, using PAUT on a D1.1 job meant seeking the Engineer's approval for alternate acceptance criteria under 8.8. After 2020, it means naming Annex H. The remaining work is calibration to Annex G or the supplemental reference blocks Annex H illustrates, and getting inspectors qualified — the same demonstration discipline ASME imposes, expressed in structural language.

sections.heading: How to Get a Client to Accept PAUT in Lieu of RT
paragraphs: Lead with their code, not your equipment. A one-page substitution request that names the construction code and edition, the authorising clause, the acceptance appendix or table, the thickness range and the personnel level restriction answers the questions an authorised inspector will ask before they are asked. A request that leads with instrument specifications and sample images invites scepticism, because it looks like a vendor pitch rather than a compliance argument.

Bring the demonstration evidence with it. Include the qualification block description with flaw locations, the demonstration results against the acceptance definition in the Case, the scan plan showing coverage of the defined examination volume, and the personnel records showing which analysts participated. That package is what makes the difference between conditional approval and a job stopped at first article, and it is reusable across every subsequent weld under the same procedure.

Then be honest about where the substitution stops. Thin wall, small bore and geometries the scan plan cannot cover stay on radiography, and saying so up front builds more credibility than claiming universal coverage. Where an owner is weighing the change across a whole facility rather than one weld, an [NDT programme audit and gap assessment](/consulting/ndt-program-audit-gap-assessment) puts numbers against both the qualification cost and the shutdown avoided.

faq.q: What is the minimum thickness for PAUT in lieu of RT under ASME?
faq.a: Code Case 2235-13 applies to all welds in material 1/2 in. (13 mm) or greater in thickness in pressure vessels and power boilers. Below that thickness the Case offers no substitution route. Section VIII Division 1 handles the substitution through UW-51(a)(4), which requires compliance with Section VIII Division 2 paragraph 7.5.5 and Section V Article 4 Mandatory Appendices VIII and IX.

faq.q: Is a Code Case still needed now that the appendices exist?
faq.a: For Section I and Section XII, yes — Code Case 2235-13 remains a live route alongside Code Case 2816 and PW-52.1. For Section VIII Division 1 the substitution moved into the Code itself at UW-51(a)(4), so the Case is no longer the vehicle. Code Cases remain available for use until annulled by the applicable Standards Committee, so confirm current status against the edition your job is built to.

faq.q: Does PAUT need to be encoded to replace radiography?
faq.a: Yes. Every ASME substitution route requires computer-based data acquisition with equipment mechanically mounted and guided on the examination surface, automatic or semi-automatic. Section V Article 1 Mandatory Appendix I defines both terms around integral encoders recording scanning positions so acquired data can be imaged. AWS D1.1 Annex H likewise works from encoded linear scanning. A live sectorial image swept by hand does not satisfy any of them.

faq.q: How many flaws does the qualification block need?
faq.a: Code Case 2235-13(c) requires a minimum of three flaws oriented to simulate flaws parallel to the production weld's fusion line: one surface flaw on the side representing the vessel OD, one on the side representing the ID, and one subsurface. If the block can be flipped during examination, one flaw represents both surfaces and two flaws suffice. Flaw size cannot exceed the applicable Table 1, 2 or 3 value.

faq.q: What does AWS D1.1 require for phased array on structural steel?
faq.a: Annex H (Normative) — Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT), added in the 2020 edition and retained in D1.1/D1.1M:2025. It supplies Table H.1 for essential variables, Table H.2 for acceptance criteria and Table H.3 for discontinuity classification, and works from encoded linear scanning. Annex G governs UT unit qualification and calibration with approved reference blocks; Annex N remains informative guidance on alternative UT techniques.

faq.q: Will a client accept PAUT if their specification names radiography?
faq.a: Only if the specification is amended or a documented substitution is approved. Code compliance and contract compliance are separate gates, and an owner's specification frequently sits tighter than the construction code. Submit the substitution against the client's named code and edition, with the authorising clause, acceptance basis, thickness limits and demonstration evidence attached, and treat approval as a document to be issued rather than a conversation to be had.

title: PCN vs ASNT: Employer Certification vs a Certificate You Own
description: ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by your employer and stops there. PCN is third-party, UKAS-accredited to ISO 9712, and portable. What US techs redo.
h1: PCN and ASNT NDT Certification, Compared for a US Technician
answer: If you work in the United States, get ASNT first. US employers certify their own people against a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, so the certificate ends at your employer's door. PCN is issued by BINDT, is UKAS-accredited to BS EN ISO 9712, and travels with you — which is why Gulf, UK and EU contracts ask for it.
expansion: The difference is not exam difficulty or syllabus depth. It is who signs the certificate. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice: the employer writes a written practice using it as a guideline, then qualifies, examines and certifies its own personnel. ASME Code Case 2235-13 states this outright, requiring personnel to be certified in accordance with their employer's written practice with SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 used as a guideline. PCN inverts that. BINDT owns and operates the scheme, holds UKAS accreditation, complies with ISO/IEC 17024 and satisfies BS EN ISO 9712, and the certificate belongs to the individual. Change employers in the US and you are re-certified by the new one. Change employers in the UK or the Gulf and your PCN card is still valid on Monday morning.
source: BINDT PCN GEN, General Requirements for Qualification and PCN Certification of NDT Personnel, Issue 19, dated 1 January 2019, clauses 13, 14, 15, 18 and 19; BINDT certification scheme pages on UKAS accreditation, ISO/IEC 17024 and BS EN ISO 9712; ASNT published pages for the ASNT NDT Level III examination, ASNT 9712 Level II and ASNT 9712 Level III; ASME BPVC Code Case 2235-13 paragraph (f).

UT: 18 days training and 180 days experience; RT: 15 days plus radiation safety and 180 days
Where it is asked for

US fabrication, refining, pipelines, power and aerospace employers

table.note: ASNT 9712 replaced the ASNT Central Certification Program (ACCP); existing ACCP certificates stayed valid to their renewal dates. PCN figures are from BINDT's PCN GEN document, Issue 19; ASNT figures are from ASNT's published scheme pages, where one training day is defined as at least seven hours.

facets.q: Which certification do US employers actually ask for?
facets.a: ASNT. US fabrication, refining, pipeline, power and aerospace employers build their written practices on SNT-TC-1A, and their customers' specifications name it. A PCN card is respected in a US interview and is not the credential the paperwork requires, so a PCN holder joining a US employer still goes through that employer's qualification and certification process before signing a report.

facets.q: Which certification do Gulf and European contracts ask for?
facets.a: PCN or another ISO 9712 certification issued by an accredited body. The reason is contractual rather than technical: ISO 9712 certification is third-party and verifiable independently of the employer, which is what a client auditing a supply chain wants. BINDT publishes online verification against a PCN number, so a client checks a technician's status without contacting the employer at all.

facets.q: Is SNT-TC-1A a standard or a recommended practice?
facets.a: A recommended practice. It supplies guidelines that an employer adapts into its own written practice, which is the document that actually governs qualification, examination and certification. ASME Code Case 2235-13(f) reflects this exactly, requiring personnel to be qualified and certified in accordance with their employer's written practice with SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 used as a guideline. The employer, not ASNT, issues the certificate.

facets.q: How long does each certificate last?
facets.a: PCN certification is normally valid for five years from the date of certification, with the wallet card normally running ten years. ASNT 9712 certificates are valid for five years. Under the SNT-TC-1A route, the interval is whatever the employer's written practice sets, because the employer owns the scheme. That is the difference in one line: a fixed published term versus a term your employer chose.

facets.q: What is the PCN pass mark?
facets.a: 70% in each examination part. For Levels 1 and 2 the 70% applies to each specimen tested and to the NDT written instruction; failure in any part fails the candidate. Candidates scoring 80% or more overall are awarded the 'D' distinction grade, and two re-tests are available to reach it. The straight 70% pass grade has applied since 1 January 2016.

facets.q: Does holding PCN reduce what you redo in the US?
facets.a: It reduces preparation, not paperwork. The syllabus overlap is large, so a PCN Level 2 walks into a US Level II examination well prepared. The employer still qualifies you against its written practice, administers its own general, specific and practical examinations, and issues its own certificate. Training and experience already documented count toward the written practice's requirements when the employer accepts the evidence.

sections.heading: The One-Line Answer for a US Technician
paragraphs: Chase ASNT first if your work is in the United States, and add PCN or another ISO 9712 certification when a contract or a move abroad requires it. That order is not a judgment about rigour. It reflects which certificate the specifications on US jobs actually name, and which one a US employer's quality system is built to issue. Reversing the order costs money and time and leaves you holding a credential the paperwork on your job does not ask for.

The reason sits in one structural fact. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, not a certifying body. An employer takes it as a guideline, writes a written practice, and then qualifies, examines and certifies its own people against that document. ASME Code Case 2235-13(f) states the arrangement in the code itself: personnel shall be qualified and certified in accordance with their employer's written practice, with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 used as a guideline.

PCN is the opposite architecture. BINDT owns and operates the scheme, holds UKAS accreditation for personnel certification, complies with ISO/IEC 17024 and satisfies BS EN ISO 9712. The certificate is issued to you by an independent body and stays valid when you change jobs. Understanding which architecture you are dealing with explains almost every downstream difference, and it is the same distinction explored between [SNT-TC-1A and CP-189](/blog/asnt-snt-tc-1a-vs-cp-189-comparison).

sections.heading: Who Issues the Certificate, and What That Changes
paragraphs: Under the US employer route, the chain runs: ASNT publishes SNT-TC-1A, your employer writes a written practice based on it, the employer's Level III designs and administers the examinations, and the employer signs your certification. Every link is inside one company. The advantage is speed and fit — the practical examination is on the specimens and equipment you actually use. The disadvantage is that the certificate has no existence outside that company.

Under PCN, the chain runs: BINDT owns the scheme under UKAS accreditation, an authorised qualifying body administers examinations to published rules, and BINDT issues a certificate in your name. BINDT publishes online verification against a PCN number, so a client confirms your status without asking your employer anything. The advantage is portability and independent verifiability. The cost is inflexibility: you sit the scheme's examinations on the scheme's specimens under the scheme's rules.

The practical consequence lands on the day you change jobs. A US technician moving between employers is re-certified by the new one, because the old certificate was the old employer's document. A PCN holder moving between employers keeps the certificate and the expiry date. Neither system is more rigorous — but only one of them survives a resignation letter, and that single fact drives most of the confusion in this comparison.

sections.heading: Recognition by Geography
paragraphs: The geographic split is not arbitrary. US industry built its NDE personnel framework around employer responsibility, and the codes reinforce it — ASME construction codes route personnel requirements to the employer's written practice rather than to a central register. Aerospace layers NAS 410 on top with its own prime-contractor expectations, a separate track examined in the comparison of [NAS 410 and SNT-TC-1A](/blog/nas-410-vs-snt-tc-1a). Everything in that ecosystem assumes the employer certifies.

Europe, the UK and much of the Gulf built around ISO 9712 and third-party certification, because their procurement model assumes a client auditing a multi-tier supply chain needs a credential it can verify without trusting the supplier. When an operator in Saudi Arabia, the UAE or Qatar writes PCN or ISO 9712 into an inspection contract, they are buying independent verification, not a different syllabus. That is why a Gulf contract asks for PCN and a Texas refinery asks for the contractor's written practice.

For a US technician the honest planning rule is: hold ASNT for the domestic market, and add PCN or ASNT 9712 when a specific contract, client or relocation requires it. Speculatively collecting international certifications ahead of demand rarely pays back, and neither certificate changes the day rate on a US job. The pay picture that does apply domestically is set out in the [NDT Level II salary guide](/ndt-level-2-salary).

sections.heading: Examination Structure Compared
paragraphs: PCN grades the general, specific and practical examinations separately. The pass mark is 70% for each examination part, and for Levels 1 and 2 that 70% applies to each specimen tested and to the NDT written instruction. Failure in any single part fails the candidate outright — there is no compensating average. Candidates achieving 80% or more overall are awarded the 'D' distinction grade, with two re-tests available to reach it, and re-examination no sooner than 30 days after the original attempt.

The ASNT NDT Level III examination is structured differently again, because it tests knowledge rather than hands-on technique. The Basic examination runs 135 multiple-choice questions over four hours. Method examinations run 135 questions over four hours for AE, ET, LT, RT and UT, and 90 questions over two hours for IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT. All are computer-based. PCN Level 3 splits into a Basic examination and a Main Method examination, where the Main Method paper is not graded until the Basic has been passed.

ASNT 9712 sits between the two worlds: a US-issued, third-party credential examined through general, specific, instruction preparation and practical components. Under the employer route, the structure is whatever the written practice specifies — which is a genuine advantage when the practical examination mirrors your production work, and a genuine weakness when nobody outside the company can evaluate what you sat. Method-by-method entry requirements are collected in the [NDT training hours guide](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method).

sections.heading: Renewal and Recertification
paragraphs: PCN draws a sharp line between two words that are used loosely elsewhere. Renewal is revalidation of a certificate without examination, available at any time up to five years after success in an initial, supplementary or recertification examination. Recertification is revalidation by examination, or by otherwise satisfying the certification body that the published criteria are met. The procedures live in separate documents — CP16 for Levels 1 and 2, CP17 for Level 3.

The consequences of failing recertification are stated plainly in PCN GEN. BINDT immediately cancels the certificate concerned, issues a replacement record that no longer shows that competence, and requires the superseded record to be returned. Cancellation does not remove eligibility for the two permitted retests within six months. Fail both retests and the route back is to apply as an initial candidate. Where recertification succeeds no later than six weeks before expiry, the new certificate expires five years after the old expiry date.

PCN also lists conditions that invalidate a certificate independently of any exam: working in an industrial sector the certificate does not cover, failing the annual visual acuity examination taken under the employer's responsibility, a significant interruption in the method, and — for industrial radiography — more than five years since success in a PCN or recognised equivalent radiation safety examination. ASNT 9712 certificates are valid five years, with recertification built on documented work records and renewal points.

sections.heading: What You Actually Redo When You Move Markets
paragraphs: Moving PCN to the United States: your PCN card does not authorise you to sign reports for a US employer. That employer qualifies you against its written practice, administers its own general, specific and practical examinations, and issues its own certificate. What your PCN buys you is preparation and evidence — documented training and industrial experience the written practice can credit, and a demonstrated pass standard the Level III can weigh. Budget for the examinations, not for the training.

Moving ASNT to the Gulf, UK or EU: this is the harder direction. An employer-issued certificate does not satisfy a contract calling for third-party ISO 9712 certification, because the objection is architectural rather than about competence. You sit the scheme's examinations. Some schemes recognise nationally recognised Level 2 certification for a reduction in required training days where it is documented on the certificate, so bring the paperwork rather than a summary.

There is one prerequisite chain worth planning around on the advanced methods. Under ISO 9712 scheme rules, a valid UT Level 2 is a prerequisite for a PAUT or TOFD Level 2, and UT Level 3 for the corresponding Level 3. You cannot enter phased array certification laterally on the strength of field experience alone. If your route runs through US method training first, that is delivered as [ASNT method training in the United States](/training-usa).

sections.heading: The ASNT 9712 Route: A US-Issued ISO 9712 Certificate
paragraphs: ASNT closed part of this gap by replacing the ASNT Central Certification Program with ASNT 9712, built to the 2021 revision of ISO 9712 and to ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023. The transition ran six months from launch, and existing ACCP certificates stayed valid until their renewal dates. The result is a third-party, US-issued credential structured on the same architecture as PCN rather than on the employer-certification model.

The requirements are published rather than employer-defined. ASNT 9712 Level II lists 18 days of training and 180 days of experience for UT, 15 days plus radiation safety training and 180 days of experience for RT, and 5 days with 60 days of experience for MT and PT, with one day defined as at least seven hours. Examinations comprise general, specific, instruction preparation and practical components. Theoretical training for initial certification remains valid for a maximum of ten years from completion.

At Level III, ASNT 9712 certificates are valid five years, practical examinations are required for the method chosen, experience runs from 180 to 540 days of Level II work depending on method and education, and Level III training runs four to five days beyond the Level II prerequisites. That is a materially different animal from the ASNT NDT Level III examination, which is knowledge-based and computer-delivered with no practical component — a distinction covered on the [ASNT certification overview](/asnt-certification).

sections.heading: Which One to Chase First
paragraphs: If you are entering NDT in the United States, the first credential is your employer's Level II in a method that gets you billable — usually UT, RT, MT or PT depending on the sector you land in. That certificate is what lets you sign reports, and it is what the specification on your job names. Everything else is a second move made from a position of employment rather than from unemployment.

If you already hold a US Level II and are looking at Gulf or European work, PCN or ASNT 9712 is the next credential, and the choice between them is about who the client recognises. Both are third-party and ISO 9712-aligned. PCN carries the longer track record in Gulf oil and gas procurement; ASNT 9712 is issued domestically and is more convenient to sit from the US. Check the actual client specification before booking anything.

If you are moving toward procedure authorship, programme ownership or an inspection-management role, Level III is the target regardless of scheme, because it is the level that writes the written practice everyone else is certified against. Employers who need that authority before they can hire it permanently cover the gap with an [outsourced ASNT Level III](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services), which is also the fastest way to get a compliant written practice in place.

sections.heading: What Employers Ask For on a Real Bid
paragraphs: Read a US inspection bid package and you will rarely find the words PCN or ISO 9712. You will find a requirement for the contractor to hold a written practice conforming to SNT-TC-1A, a requirement for Level III approval of procedures, a requirement for certification records to be available, and method-specific requirements traceable to the construction code. The credential the buyer is actually purchasing is a compliant certification system, not a card in a technician's wallet.

Read a Gulf or European package and the shape inverts. The requirement names ISO 9712 or PCN certification at a stated level and sector, often with an expiry-date cutoff and sometimes with a client-witnessed practical. The buyer is purchasing independently verifiable competence, and BINDT's online verification against a PCN number is what makes the requirement enforceable during an audit.

What both buyers punish is the same failure: expired certificates discovered mid-job. PCN invalidates certification on a failed annual visual acuity examination or a significant interruption in the method, and US written practices carry equivalent triggers. Contractors running crews across both markets manage it in [NDT personnel certification tracking](/erp/ndt-personnel-certification-tracking) rather than a spreadsheet, because the certificate an auditor asks for is always the one that lapsed last month.

faq.q: What is the actual difference between PCN and ASNT NDT courses?
faq.a: The difference is in the certification, not the course. A PCN course prepares you for examinations run to BINDT's scheme rules, leading to a certificate BINDT issues in your name and that you keep between employers. An ASNT-based course prepares you for examinations your employer administers under its own written practice, leading to a certificate your employer issues and that ends when you leave.

faq.q: Is PCN recognised in the United States?
faq.a: It is respected but it is not the credential US specifications name. A US employer still qualifies and certifies you against its own written practice before you sign reports, because SNT-TC-1A places that responsibility on the employer. Your PCN documentation supports the training and experience evidence the written practice requires, which shortens the process without removing it.

faq.q: Is ASNT certification recognised in the Gulf and Europe?
faq.a: For many roles, yes, but contracts that specify ISO 9712 or PCN certification will not accept an employer-issued certificate in its place, because the requirement is for third-party certification rather than for a different syllabus. Check whether the client specification names ISO 9712 explicitly. If it does, plan on sitting the scheme's examinations rather than presenting existing certification.

faq.q: How long is PCN certification valid?
faq.a: Normally five years from the date of certification, with the wallet card normally issued for ten years, and the expiry date shown on the certificate or card. Renewal revalidates without examination at any time up to five years after success in an initial, supplementary or recertification examination. Recertification revalidates by examination or by otherwise satisfying BINDT's published criteria.

faq.q: Does ASNT offer a third-party certification like PCN?
faq.a: Yes. ASNT 9712 replaced the ASNT Central Certification Program and is built to ISO 9712:2021 and ANSI/ASNT CP-9712 (ISO 9712:2021):2023. Certificates are valid five years, practical examinations are required, and requirements are published rather than employer-defined — 18 days training and 180 days experience for UT Level II, for example, with one day defined as at least seven hours.

faq.q: Should a technician hold both PCN and ASNT?
faq.a: Hold both when your work crosses markets. A technician who alternates between US turnarounds and Gulf projects needs the employer certification to sign US reports and the third-party certification to satisfy Gulf contracts. A technician working only in the United States gains no contractual benefit from PCN. Buy the credential the specification in front of you names, and add the second when a client requires it.

title: API 936 Is Reachable Without Inspection Time; API 653 Is Not
description: API 936 publishes no experience prerequisite. API 653 demands one to five years under an authorized inspection agency. Which one a welder can sit first.
h1: API 936 or API 653: Which Certification a Welder Can Actually Sit First
answer: API 936 has no experience or education prerequisite — API states it is open to applicants with any experience in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, as well as applicants wanting to gain industry experience. API 653 requires one to five years under an authorized inspection agency, one year of it performing inspection. A welder with no logged inspection time can sit API 936 now and API 653 later.
expansion: The two certifications sit at opposite ends of the entry problem. API's programme page for API 936 states the certification is open to applicants with any experience in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, as well as applicants wanting to gain industry experience — no diploma, no logged hours, no employer sign-off before you sit. API 653 runs on a four-tier education-and-experience table topped by a hard requirement that the experience was acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, with at least one year supervising or performing inspection activities. Tank erection time on a construction crew fails that test, because a fabrication contractor is not an authorized inspection agency. That single clause, not the exam difficulty, is what blocks a field hand from API 653 and leaves API 936 open.
source: API Individual Certification Programs pages for API 936 Refractory Personnel and API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector; API ICP published schedules and fees table; API Standard 936, Fourth Edition, June 2014; API Standard 653, Fifth Edition, November 2014, section 3 definitions; BLS 2025 wage data published via O*NET OnLine.

facets.q: Does API 936 require any prior refractory experience?
facets.a: No. API's programme page states the certification is open to applicants with any experience in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, as well as applicants wanting to gain industry experience. There is no education tier, no minimum year count and no employer verification of field time before the exam. The exam itself is the filter: 85 questions in 3.25 hours, closed book, with no reference material permitted.

facets.q: Why does tank construction time not count toward API 653?
facets.a: API 653 defines an authorized inspection agency in section 3 as one of four organization types: a jurisdictional inspection organization, an insurer's inspection organization writing AST insurance, an owner/operator maintaining an inspection organization for its own equipment, or an independent organization under contract to and directed by an owner/operator. A tank erector or fabrication contractor sits outside all four, so its payroll time earns nothing.

facets.q: What work does an API 936 card actually open?
facets.a: Refractory inspection and third-party quality surveillance on monolithic linings — FCC units, sulfur recovery units, reformers, fired heaters and CO boilers. The work is turnaround-driven, so it arrives in concentrated shutdown windows rather than steadily. Refractory contractors and inspection firms commonly require the card as a condition of field assignment during a major turnaround, which makes it a hiring key rather than a career in itself.

facets.q: Can ASNT Level II time count toward the API 653 experience requirement?
facets.a: It counts when the employer is an authorized inspection agency, because API's requirement is about who employs you and what you do, not which credential you hold. UT, MT or PT work performed on aboveground storage tanks under an independent inspection firm contracted to an owner/operator is inspection activity. The identical work performed for a fabrication shop building new tanks is not.

facets.q: Which certification is the better first step for a construction-side hand?
facets.a: API 936, because it is the only one of the two that can be sat immediately. It is not a formal stepping stone — no API 936 time converts into API 653 qualifying experience by itself. Its value is that it puts an API credential on the résumé and gets a candidate hired by the kind of organization whose employment does count toward API 653.

facets.q: Do you have to pass API 653 before proving the experience?
facets.a: The order runs the other way. API reviews the application against the education-and-experience table before an exam is scheduled, so the experience gate precedes the exam rather than following it. Studying the standard early is useful; applying early without qualifying time under an authorized inspection agency simply returns the application. Build the year first, then apply.

sections.heading: The prerequisite gap is the whole answer
paragraphs: API publishes a four-tier education-and-experience table for API 653: one year for a BS or higher in engineering or technology, two years for a two-year technical degree or certificate, three years for a high school diploma or equivalent, and five or more years for no formal education. Every tier carries the same floor beneath it — at least one year supervising or performing inspection activities as described in API 653. API 936 carries no such table at all.

For a welder or a construction-side field hand, that difference decides the order of operations. The API 653 no-education tier looks generous until you read the qualifier attached to it: the experience must have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. Five years of pipe welding at a fabrication shop earns nothing against that requirement. Five years of the same welding inside an owner-operator's inspection organization earns most of it.

So the answer to which is reachable is not close. API 936 is sittable this quarter by anyone willing to study a 49-page standard. API 653 becomes sittable only after a deliberate year inside an inspection organization. Anyone mapping that year should read the companion route in our welder-to-NDT-inspector career path for 2026, which covers the same transition from the method-certification side rather than the API side.

sections.heading: What API 653 means by an authorized inspection agency
paragraphs: Section 3 of API 653 defines an authorized inspection agency as one of four organizations that employ an API-certified aboveground storage tank inspector: the inspection organization of the jurisdiction in which the tank is operated; the inspection organization of an insurance company licensed or registered to write aboveground storage tank insurance; an owner/operator who maintains an inspection organization for activities relating only to its own equipment and not for tanks intended for sale or resale; or an independent organization or individual under contract to and under the direction of an owner/operator.

Read that list against a construction résumé and the problem becomes concrete. Tank erectors, fabrication shops, scaffolding crews, coating contractors and rigging outfits sit outside all four categories. The fourth category is the door that opens for most people making this move: an independent inspection contractor working under an owner/operator's direction. Getting hired there — as a helper, a technician, a UT hand — is what converts field time into qualifying time on the application form.

The clock matters as much as the employer. API requires the experience within the last 10 years, so a candidate who spent 2014 to 2018 inside an inspection organization and then returned to the tools has a window that closes. Anyone planning a delayed move should treat the qualifying year as perishable and apply while it is still inside the window.

sections.heading: What API 936 covers, and what it does not
paragraphs: API Standard 936, Fourth Edition, June 2014, is titled Refractory Installation Quality Control—Inspection and Testing Monolithic Refractory Linings and Materials, and runs 49 pages. It covers monolithic linings — castable, gunned, thick-layer plastic, thin-layer abrasion-resistant — and it qualifies materials, equipment and personnel by defined methods. The contents run through quality control elements, the separate responsibilities of owner, contractor, inspector and manufacturer, inspector qualifications, materials and anchors, qualification and testing, installation execution, curing, repairs and dryout.

What the card does not cover is equally important to state. It carries no authority over pressure vessels, piping, storage tanks or welding acceptance criteria. It is a narrow instrument aimed at one family of linings. That narrowness is precisely why API opens it without prerequisites: the exam tests knowledge of a single short standard, and that knowledge is learnable without a decade in the field.

Annex C of the standard is informative and is titled API Certification for Refractory Personnel, with Table C.1 listing minimum inspector competencies. Read that annex before committing money, because it states exactly what the certification asserts about the holder — installation quality control, as-installed sampling and testing, and dryout supervision, rather than fitness-for-service judgement on the equipment behind the lining.

sections.heading: The exams are not comparable in weight
paragraphs: API 936 runs 3.25 hours and 85 questions, of which 75 are scored and 10 are unscored pretest items. It is closed book throughout — no reference material is permitted in the room. Certification runs a three-year term, and API's recertification route uses an online open-book quiz of 25 questions covering code changes on a six-year cycle, with a four-hour completion window.

API 653 runs 7.5 hours and 170 questions, of which 140 are scored, split between a closed-book portion and an open-book portion that requires working from the standard and its referenced documents. The API body of knowledge for the exam pulls in API RP 571, RP 575, RP 576, RP 577, API 650, RP 651, RP 652 and ASME Sections V and IX alongside API 653 itself. Recertification runs three years and requires documented CPD hours plus continuing engagement in tank inspection work.

The fee separation follows the same shape. API's published ICP schedule puts initial certification at $450 for members and $625 for non-members on API 936, against $875 and $1,125 on API 653. Recertification runs $320 and $430 against $745 and $855. Those are API's figures, and they exclude preparatory courses, travel and the study time the open-book portion demands.

sections.heading: What each card opens on a job board
paragraphs: API 936 opens refractory inspection and third-party quality surveillance work, concentrated on FCC units, sulfur recovery units, reformers, fired heaters and CO boilers. The rhythm is turnaround-driven, arriving in shutdown windows rather than as a steady week-to-week load. Many refractory contractors and inspection firms treat the card as a condition of field assignment on a major turnaround, which is what makes it a hiring key even though its technical scope is narrow.

API 653 opens in-service external inspection, out-of-service internal inspection, repair and alteration oversight, and reconstruction work on aboveground storage tanks. The certified inspector signs the report, which is a different order of professional exposure and a different order of pay. Anyone wanting to see what that scope actually involves day to day can read our breakdown of how API 653 sets external, internal and settlement intervals, which walks the clauses an authorized inspector works to.

On earnings, BLS 2025 wage data published through O*NET puts the median for inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers and weighers at $48,570 a year against $53,750 for welders, cutters, solderers and brazers. Those national medians pool thousands of unrelated inspection roles and understate certified petrochemical work badly; our NDT inspector salary breakdown segments the bands that reflect this corner of the market.

sections.heading: The honest recommendation for a welder with no inspection time
paragraphs: Take API 936 first, and take it for the right reason. It is not a formal stepping stone to API 653 — no amount of API 936 field time converts into API 653 qualifying experience unless the employer happens to be an authorized inspection agency. What it does is put an API credential on the résumé, get a candidate onto turnaround inspection crews, and demonstrate to a hiring inspection firm that the person studies standards and passes closed-book exams.

The mistake to avoid is treating API 653 as a first purchase. API reviews the application against the qualification table before an exam is scheduled, so a candidate without the inspection year does not fail the exam — the application does not proceed to an exam at all. Money spent on API 653 preparation before the experience exists buys nothing but early familiarity with the standard.

The working sequence is: sit API 936 now, use it to get hired by an inspection organization, log the inspection year deliberately with documentation, then apply for API 653. Add ASNT method certification in parallel, because a UT or MT ticket is what makes an inspection firm want to hire a welder in the first place, and that hire is the entire bottleneck.

sections.heading: Building the API 653 experience year deliberately
paragraphs: ASNT method certification is the lever that gets the door open. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies the technician against its own written practice rather than a national body issuing the ticket, so there is no degree gate anywhere in the process — but there are documented classroom hours and documented on-the-job hours for each method, and they differ method by method. Our guide to ASNT certification levels and routes lays out how the levels stack and what each one authorises.

The on-the-job training log is what employers and auditors actually examine, and it is where most transitions come apart. Hours worked without contemporaneous records are hours that cannot be claimed later. Start the log on day one of the first inspection job, in the format described in our guide to NDT OJT hours log requirements, and keep it independent of any single employer's filing system so it survives a job change.

Run the API 653 study in the same period rather than after it. The open-book portion rewards familiarity with document navigation across API 650, RP 651, RP 652 and RP 575, and that familiarity is cheapest to build while working on tanks daily. By the time the twelfth month of inspection activity closes, the application and the exam readiness should arrive together.

sections.heading: Where Atlantis fits, and where it does not
paragraphs: Atlantis does not deliver API 510, API 570, API 653 or API 936 exam preparation, and nothing above should be read as an offer to. Those are API programmes with API's own qualification rules, and candidates apply to API directly. The guidance here exists because nobody was answering the question honestly for people coming off the tools.

What Atlantis does deliver sits upstream of the API route and is what makes a welder hireable into an inspection organization in the first place: ASNT method training across UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD and phased array through our US training programmes, and outsourced ASNT Level III consulting for employers who need a Level III to write and sign the written practice their technicians are certified under.

For tank owners on the other side of the same problem — assets that need inspecting rather than people who need certifying — our API 653 tank inspector services supply certified inspectors and the reporting that goes with them. Both sides are affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a demo or a quote available on request through contact.

faq.q: Is API 936 easier than API 653?
faq.a: API 936 is 85 questions in 3.25 hours, closed book, drawn from a single 49-page standard. API 653 is 170 questions in 7.5 hours across closed-book and open-book portions, drawn from API 653 plus API 650, RP 571, RP 575, RP 576, RP 577, RP 651, RP 652 and ASME Sections V and IX. The study load is not comparable.

faq.q: Can I sit API 653 while working for a tank construction contractor?
faq.a: No. API requires the qualifying experience to have been acquired while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency as defined in API 653. A construction contractor building tanks for sale or delivery does not meet that definition. Moving to an owner/operator's inspection organization, or to an independent inspection firm contracted to one, is the change that starts the clock.

faq.q: How long is each certification valid?
faq.a: Both API 936 and API 653 run three-year certification terms. API 936 recertification uses an online open-book quiz of 25 questions on code changes every six years. API 653 recertification requires documented CPD hours and continuing engagement in tank inspection activity, with an online quiz on the same six-year cycle.

faq.q: Does an ASNT Level II ticket help with either API certification?
faq.a: It does not substitute for either one, and API does not list it as a qualification tier. Its value is indirect and large: an ASNT method certification is what gets a welder hired by an inspection organization, and employment there is what generates the API 653 qualifying experience. Treat it as the hiring credential rather than the API credential.

faq.q: What does API 936 certification cost through API?
faq.a: API's published ICP fee schedule lists initial certification at $450 for API members and $625 for non-members, with recertification at $320 and $430. Preparatory courses, travel and study materials sit outside that. Those are API's figures for the API programme, not Atlantis pricing — Atlantis does not sell API 936 training.

title: API 510 Without a Degree: Five Years Replaces the Diploma
description: API 510 lists no formal education as a qualifying path at five years. The gate is one year of inspection activity under an authorized inspection agency.
h1: Can a Journeyman Welder Become a Certified Pressure Vessel Inspector Without a College Degree?
answer: Yes. API 510 lists no formal education as a qualifying path with five or more years of pressure vessel design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection experience. A degree only shortens the clock. The real gate is one year of supervising or performing inspection activities under an authorized inspection agency — that year cannot be logged while wrenching.
expansion: API's qualification table for API 510 runs four tiers: one year of inspection experience with a BS in engineering or technology, two years with a two-year technical degree, three years with a high school diploma, and five or more years with no formal education. The diploma changes the length of the runway, not the destination. Every tier carries the same floor — at least one year supervising or performing inspection activities as described in API 510 — and all of the experience must have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. That is the clause that keeps a journeyman welder out, not the absence of a degree. Wrenching for a mechanical contractor produces no qualifying time. The same welder inside an owner-operator's inspection organization, or an independent inspection firm under contract to one, produces qualifying time from the first week.
source: API Individual Certification Programs qualification requirements for API 510, API 570, API 577, API 936 and API 1169; API ICP published schedules and fees table; AWS QC1 eligibility paths for the Certified Welding Inspector programme; ASNT Recommended Practice No. SNT-TC-1A; BLS 2025 wage data published via O*NET OnLine.
