facets.q: Is a college degree required for API 510 in refining?
facets.a: No. API's own qualification table lists no formal education as a valid tier, requiring five or more years of pressure vessel design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection experience instead. A BS reduces the requirement to one year and a two-year technical degree to two years. The degree buys time, not eligibility, and no employer can override API's published tiers.

facets.q: What counts as inspection activity for the one-year requirement?
facets.a: API's wording is supervision or performance of inspection activities as described in API 510. In practice that means performing or directing the inspections the code calls for on in-service pressure vessels — external and internal examinations, thickness monitoring, assessment of repairs and alterations — while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Fabrication QC on new-build vessels does not satisfy it.

facets.q: Which API certification can a welder start on this year?
facets.a: API 577 is the strongest fit. API accepts any petrochemical industry experience for it, so five years on the tools with no formal education qualifies, and three years qualifies with a high school diploma. The exam runs 110 questions in 3 hours 15 minutes, closed book. API also lists holders of current API 510, 570 or 653 as automatically qualified.

facets.q: Does welding experience count toward AWS CWI?
facets.a: Directly. AWS QC1 treats welding-related experience as qualifying, and that category includes hands-on welding, welding supervision, welding instruction, quality control in a welding environment and NDT on welded products. The common path is a high school diploma plus five years of documented welding experience, reduced to two years with an associate degree in welding technology.

facets.q: How long does the whole transition realistically take?
facets.a: Roughly two to three years for someone starting from the tools. Six to twelve months to earn a hiring credential — ASNT Level II, AWS CWI or API 577 — then the move into an inspection organization, then twelve months of logged inspection activity, then the API 510 application and exam. The bottleneck is the job change, not the study.

facets.q: Can experience from years ago still be counted?
facets.a: Only if it falls inside API's ten-year recency window. API requires the qualifying experience to have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. Inspection time from twelve years ago is expired for application purposes and has to be re-earned, which is why a delayed move is more expensive than it looks.

sections.heading: The substitution rule, stated plainly
paragraphs: API publishes the same four-tier structure across API 510, API 570 and API 653. A BS or higher in engineering or technology, or three or more years of military service in a technical role, requires one year of experience. A two-year degree or certificate in engineering or technology, or two years of technical military service, requires two years. A high school diploma or equivalent requires three years. No formal education requires five or more years.

That last tier is the answer to the question everyone actually asks. A degree is not required and has never been required. What the degree does is compress the experience requirement from five years to one, which is a real advantage but a different thing from a gate. Anyone told a degree is mandatory for refinery inspection work has been told something API's own qualification table contradicts.

The substitution runs on time, and time is the one thing a journeyman welder with fifteen years in already has. The problem is that not all of that time counts, and understanding which portion counts is worth more than any exam preparation course. Our route from welder to NDT inspector for the US market covers the parallel method-certification path that most people end up using to bridge the gap.

sections.heading: The one clause that actually blocks you
paragraphs: Underneath every tier sits the same floor: at least one year of the total must be in supervision or performance of inspection activities as described in the relevant API code. A five-year no-education candidate does not need five years of inspection — four of those years can be design, fabrication, repair or operation of pressure vessels. One year must be inspection.

Layered on top is the requirement that binds hardest. API states that the experience must have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. That phrase is doing all the work. It means qualifying experience is defined by who employs you, not by what you touch. A welder repairing pressure vessels for a mechanical contractor accumulates zero qualifying years across a whole career.

This is why the honest answer to the second query — whether any API certs can be worked on while still wrenching — splits cleanly in two. The vessel, piping and tank certifications cannot, because their inspection year is unreachable from a contractor payroll. Several other API certifications can, because API does not attach an inspection-role condition to them at all.

sections.heading: What an authorized inspection agency is, and why it decides everything
paragraphs: The API codes define the authorized inspection agency narrowly. Across the family it means a jurisdictional inspection organization, an insurer's inspection organization writing the relevant coverage, an owner/operator maintaining an inspection organization for its own equipment only, or an independent organization or individual under contract to and under the direction of an owner/operator and recognised by the jurisdiction.

Three of those four are closed to a career changer in practice. The fourth is wide open and is how nearly everyone gets in: independent inspection firms contracted to refiners and terminal operators hire constantly, and they hire technicians and helpers, not only certified inspectors. A UT technician on that payroll, working on in-service vessels under an owner's direction, is generating qualifying time from the first week.

The second viable route is internal. Large refiners maintain owner-user inspection departments, and a welder already inside the plant on maintenance can transfer sideways into that department without changing employer. That transfer is the single highest-value career move available to a plant welder, and it costs nothing but the application. Both routes convert the same field skills into experience API will accept.

sections.heading: Certifications you can earn while still on the tools
paragraphs: API 936 Refractory Personnel has no published education or experience prerequisite. API states it is open to applicants with any experience in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, as well as applicants wanting to gain industry experience. A welder can apply and sit it this quarter, closed book, 85 questions in 3.25 hours.

API 577 Welding Inspection and Metallurgy is the most natural fit for someone who welds. API accepts any petrochemical industry experience against its tiers — five or more years with no formal education, three years with a high school diploma, two years with a two-year technical degree. No inspection role is required anywhere in the qualification. For a welder, this is the API credential with the shortest distance between current résumé and eligible application.

API 1169 Pipeline Construction Inspector is the third. API's qualification paths explicitly credit non-inspection pipeline work — pipeline construction, surveying and operation — and credit other heavy industry experience including welding, coating and excavation at longer year counts. Outside API, AWS CWI treats welding itself as qualifying experience under QC1, and ASNT Level II is employer-certified with no degree condition.

sections.heading: API 577 is the highest-leverage card for a welder
paragraphs: The leverage is in what it signals rather than what it authorises. API 577 covers welding processes, inspection and metallurgy — the exact knowledge a journeyman already carries in his hands but cannot prove on paper to a hiring inspection manager. Passing it converts tacit skill into a credential API recognises, and it does so without requiring the inspection year the vessel codes demand.

The economics are favourable too. API's published fee schedule puts initial certification at $380 for members and $440 for non-members, against $875 and $1,125 for API 510, 570 or 653. The exam is 110 questions in 3 hours 15 minutes, closed book, against 7.5 hours for the vessel codes. It is the cheapest and fastest API credential a welder can hold on merit.

API also lists holders of current API 510, 570 or 653 certifications as automatically qualified for API 577, which reveals how API positions it — as the welding-and-metallurgy knowledge base the inspector codes assume. Earning it first and the inspector code second runs the sequence in the order the knowledge actually builds.

sections.heading: The sequence that works, and the timeline
paragraphs: Month zero to month nine: earn a hiring credential while still on the tools. ASNT Level II in UT or MT, AWS CWI, or API 577 — any of the three makes an inspection firm interested. UT is the strongest single choice because thickness monitoring on in-service equipment is the daily work of vessel and piping inspection, so the skill maps directly onto what the employer needs done.

Month nine to month twelve: make the employer change. Move to an independent inspection firm contracted to a refiner, or transfer into an owner-user inspection department if already inside a plant. This is the step the whole plan turns on, and it is the step people postpone. Nothing before it counts toward API 510 and everything after it does.

Month twelve to month twenty-four: log the inspection year with contemporaneous records, and study the code in parallel. Keep the documentation in the format described in our guide to NDT OJT hours log requirements, because the same discipline that satisfies an ASNT audit produces the employment record API's application review wants. Apply for API 510 as the twelfth qualifying month closes.

sections.heading: What the pay change looks like
paragraphs: BLS 2025 wage data published through O*NET puts the median for welders, cutters, solderers and brazers at $53,750 a year, or $25.84 an hour. The median for inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers and weighers is $48,570, or $23.35 an hour. Read naively, that says the move is a pay cut, and that reading is wrong for a specific reason worth understanding.

The inspector occupation code pools hundreds of thousands of general manufacturing quality roles with no code certification attached. It is not a measure of certified refinery inspection work, and it does not separate an API 510 inspector on a turnaround from a parts sorter on a production line. The national median for the code tells you almost nothing about the band a certified inspector occupies.

Because the published national codes blur the distinction, segment by certification level instead. Our NDT inspector salary breakdown and the Level II band separate the roles that carry code certification from the ones that do not, which is the comparison that matters when deciding whether to spend two years on this transition.

sections.heading: Where the training and programme support come from
paragraphs: Atlantis does not deliver API 510, API 570, API 653, API 936 or API 1169 exam preparation. Those are API programmes governed by API's own qualification rules, and candidates apply to API directly. This page exists because the question was being asked at depth by people the industry was not answering.

What Atlantis delivers is the layer that makes the transition possible: ASNT method training across UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD and phased array through our US training programmes, which is the credential that gets a welder hired into an inspection organization in the first place. Our guide to ASNT certification routes explains how the levels stack and what each authorises.

On the employer side, an inspection organization cannot certify anyone without a compliant written practice and a Level III to sign it. Atlantis supplies both through written practice development and outsourced ASNT Level III consulting, which is how small inspection firms take on career changers at all. Affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a demo or quote on request.

faq.q: Do refineries actually hire inspectors without degrees?
faq.a: Routinely, because API's certification rules permit it and the certification is what the owner requires. API 510, 570 and 653 all list no formal education as a valid qualification tier at five or more years of experience. The credential the refinery checks is the API card, and API issues that card against experience regardless of schooling.

faq.q: Can I take the API 510 exam first and get the experience later?
faq.a: No. API reviews the application against the education-and-experience table before scheduling an exam, so the qualification precedes the exam rather than following it. An application submitted without the one year of inspection activity under an authorized inspection agency does not proceed. Study early if you want, but apply only when the qualifying year is complete and documented.

faq.q: Is API 577 worth taking if my goal is API 510?
faq.a: Yes, on two grounds. It is earnable now with no inspection role required, so it fills the waiting period productively, and it covers the welding and metallurgy knowledge the inspector codes assume — API treats current API 510, 570 or 653 holders as automatically qualified for it. At $380 to $440 through API it is also the cheapest API credential available.

faq.q: Does time as a welding foreman count toward API 510?
faq.a: Not as inspection activity. Supervising welders is production supervision; API's requirement is supervision or performance of inspection activities as described in API 510, performed under an authorized inspection agency. Foreman time can count within the broader four-year block of pressure vessel repair or fabrication experience at the no-education tier, but it cannot fill the one-year inspection floor.

faq.q: What is the cheapest first step from the tools?
faq.a: ASNT Level II through an employer, because there is no national exam fee and the certification is issued by the employer against its written practice. Where no employer sponsor exists, API 577 at $380 to $440 is the lowest-cost credential that carries an independent body's name and requires no inspection role to qualify.

title: API 653 Intervals: One Month, Five Years, and a 20-Year Ceiling
description: Routine at one month, external at five years or RCA/4N, internal capped at 20 years, plus API 653 Annex B settlement survey points and acceptance limits.
h1: How API 653 Sets External, Internal and Settlement Frequencies on Atmospheric Tanks
answer: API 653 governs in-service inspection of atmospheric storage tanks built to API 650 or API 12C. It sets routine in-service checks at intervals not exceeding one month, external inspection by an authorized inspector at five years or RCA/4N years — whichever is less — and internal inspection intervals capped at 20 years without a release prevention barrier.
expansion: API 653 is the in-service code. API 650 governs how an atmospheric welded steel tank is built; API 653 governs it from the day it enters service, covering the foundation, bottom, shell, structure, roof, appurtenances and nozzles to the face of the first flange. Section 6 sets four separate clocks that run in parallel rather than one master interval: a monthly routine visual by owner personnel, a five-year external inspection by an authorized inspector, an external ultrasonic thickness programme on its own corrosion-rate schedule, and an internal inspection whose interval is built from bottom thickness, corrosion rate and installed safeguards. Section 1.3 subordinates all of it to jurisdictional regulation where the two conflict, and section 6.2.3 acknowledges that jurisdictional regulations control inspection frequency where they apply. PHMSA and EPA both lean on API 653 rather than writing their own intervals.
source: API Standard 653, Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction, Fifth Edition, November 2014 — sections 1.1, 1.3, 3, 4.4.5, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 12.5 and Annex B, with Tables 4.4a/4.4b and 6.1; API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Body of Knowledge, March/July/November 2026; 49 CFR 195.432; 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6).

RCA is the difference between measured and minimum required shell thickness in mils; N is the shell corrosion rate in mils per year.

facets.q: What code governs external inspection intervals for atmospheric petroleum storage tanks?
facets.a: API 653 does, as the in-service code for tanks built to API 650 or its predecessor API 12C. It sets the external inspection at five years or RCA/4N years, whichever is less, performed by an authorized inspector with the tank in operation. Section 1.3 gives precedence to any conflicting statutory regulation, and where API 653 is more stringent than the regulation, API 653 governs.

facets.q: How do federal regulations use API 653?
facets.a: They incorporate it rather than replacing it. PHMSA's rule at 49 CFR 195.432 requires operators to inspect in-service breakout tanks according to API 653, while excluding its alternative risk-based internal inspection interval provision — so a regulated breakout tank cannot use RBI to extend the internal interval. EPA's SPCC rule at 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6) is performance-based and points to industry standards including API 653.

facets.q: What sets the out-of-service internal inspection interval?
facets.a: Two permitted routes. The corrosion-rate method uses the measured tank bottom corrosion rate and the minimum remaining thickness calculated per 4.4.5, capped at 20 years without a release prevention barrier and 30 years with one. The risk-based method under 6.4.2.2.2 uses an API RP 580 assessment of likelihood and consequence, reviewed at intervals not exceeding 10 years.

facets.q: What extends an initial internal inspection interval past 10 years?
facets.a: Table 6.1 safeguards, and they are cumulative. A thick-film reinforced product-side lining per API RP 652 adds five years, an unreinforced thin or thick film adds two, soil-side cathodic protection per API RP 651 adds five, a release prevention barrier per API 650 Annex I adds ten, and a qualifying stainless bottom adds ten. Initial bottom thickness above 6.0 mm adds a calculated credit.

facets.q: How many elevation points does a settlement survey need?
facets.a: API 653 gives the minimum as N = D/10 with D in feet, rounded up to the next higher even whole number and never fewer than eight points, uniformly distributed around the circumference. Maximum spacing between points is 10 m (32 ft). Annex B Figure B.1 adds that there must be at least four equally spaced diametrical measurement lines.

facets.q: What is the acceptance criterion for out-of-plane settlement?
facets.a: Where a rigid tilt plane fits the data, permissible out-of-plane deflection is Smax = 11L²Y/(2EH), with L the arc length between measurement points, Y the shell yield strength, E Young's modulus and H the tank height. The optimum cosine curve is only valid when R² is 0.9 or greater. Exceedance routes the tank to B.3.2.2 or a rigorous engineering assessment.

sections.heading: Which code governs, and which regulators borrow it
paragraphs: API 653 covers steel storage tanks built to API 650 and its predecessor API 12C, and it provides minimum requirements for maintaining their integrity after they have been placed in service. Its scope is limited to the tank foundation, bottom, shell, structure, roof, attached appurtenances, and nozzles to the face of the first flange, first threaded joint or first welding-end connection. Where API 653 and API 650 appear to conflict on an in-service tank, API 653 governs.

The jurisdiction question has an explicit answer in the standard. Section 1.3 states that where any provision presents a direct or implied conflict with a statutory regulation, the regulation governs — but where API 653 is more stringent than the regulation, API 653 governs. Section 6.2.3 reinforces the point, noting that jurisdictional regulations control the frequency and interval of inspections where they apply, and that knowledge of those regulations is necessary for compliant scheduling.

In the United States the two regulators that matter most both borrow rather than write. PHMSA's 49 CFR 195.432 requires operators to inspect in-service breakout tanks according to API 653, with the alternative risk-based internal inspection interval provision carved out. EPA's SPCC rule at 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6) requires integrity testing to industry standards without prescribing a frequency, and requires visual inspection to be combined with another technique such as hydrostatic, radiographic, ultrasonic or acoustic emission testing.

sections.heading: Routine in-service inspection: the one-month clock
paragraphs: The most frequent requirement in API 653 is also the one most often missed in programme audits. Clause 6.3.1.1 requires that the external condition of the tank be monitored by close visual inspection from the ground on a routine basis. This inspection may be done by owner/operator personnel and by people who are not authorized inspectors, provided they are knowledgeable about the storage facility operations, the tank, and the characteristics of the product stored.

Clause 6.3.1.2 sets the interval: consistent with conditions at the particular site, but not to exceed one month. That is a hard ceiling, not a target. A tank on a quarterly walk-down schedule is non-compliant regardless of how thorough the quarterly walk-down is, and no corrosion argument extends it.

Clause 6.3.1.3 defines the content. The routine inspection covers the tank's exterior surfaces, and evidence of leaks, shell distortions, signs of settlement, corrosion, and the condition of the foundation, paint coatings, insulation systems and appurtenances should be documented for follow-up by an authorized inspector. The monthly walk is the detection layer that decides whether the five-year external inspection finds a surprise. Programmes that struggle to evidence twelve records a year per tank usually have a records problem rather than an inspection problem, which is what our NDT program audit and gap assessment is built to surface.

sections.heading: The five-year external inspection and the RCA/4N test
paragraphs: Clause 6.3.2.1 requires that all tanks be given a visual external inspection by an authorized inspector, conducted at least every five years or RCA/4N years, whichever is less. RCA is the remaining corrosion allowance — the difference between the measured shell thickness and the minimum required thickness, expressed in mils. N is the shell corrosion rate in mils per year. Tanks may be in operation during this inspection.

The formula is the part that gets skipped. Five years is a ceiling, not a default, and a tank with a thin shell and an active corrosion rate falls below it arithmetically. A shell with 40 mils of remaining corrosion allowance corroding at 4 mils per year yields RCA/4N = 40/16 = 2.5 years, and the external inspection is due at 2.5 years, not five. Every external interval decision should show that calculation on the face of the report.

Two supporting requirements travel with the external inspection. Clause 6.3.2.2 permits insulation to be removed only to the extent necessary to determine the condition of the exterior wall or roof, which keeps insulated-tank inspections proportionate. Clause 6.3.2.3 requires that grounding system components such as shunts and mechanical cable connections be visually checked, referencing API 2003 for hydrocarbon ignition prevention.

sections.heading: External UT of the shell: five years, or RCA/2N to a 15-year ceiling
paragraphs: Clause 6.3.3.1 describes external ultrasonic thickness measurement of the shell as a means of determining a rate of uniform general corrosion while the tank is in service, with the extent of measurement determined by the owner/operator. It is optional in the sense that the standard says when used — but once a programme relies on it, clause 6.3.3.2 fixes the intervals.

Where the corrosion rate is not known, the maximum interval is five years, and the standard permits rates to be estimated from tanks in similar service based on thickness measurements taken at an interval not exceeding five years. Where the corrosion rate is known, the maximum interval is the smaller of RCA/2N years or 15 years. Note the difference from the external visual: the UT formula divides by 2N, the visual by 4N, so the visual always falls due first on the same tank data.

Clause 6.3.3.3 provides the substitution most owners want. Internal inspection of the tank shell, performed when the tank is out of service, can be substituted for a programme of external ultrasonic thickness measurement if the internal inspection interval is equal to or less than the interval that 6.3.3.2 b) would require. That is the clause that lets a tank on a tight internal cycle avoid running a parallel external UT programme.

sections.heading: The initial internal interval: 10 years plus Table 6.1 credits
paragraphs: Clause 6.4.2.1.1 sets the interval from initial service date to first internal inspection at not more than 10 years, unless the tank carries one or more of the leak prevention, detection, corrosion mitigation or containment safeguards listed in Table 6.1. The maximum initial interval is 10 years plus incremental credits for those safeguards, and the credits are cumulative.

Table 6.1 prices each safeguard. A thick-film reinforced lining on the product side installed per API RP 652 adds five years. A thin-film or thick-film unreinforced lining per API RP 652 adds two. Cathodic protection of the soil side installed, maintained and inspected per API RP 651 adds five. A release prevention barrier installed per API 650 Annex I adds ten. A qualifying stainless steel bottom per API 650 Annex SC with Annex S or X adds ten. Initial bottom thickness above 6.0 mm (0.25 in.) adds a calculated credit using 0.375 mm per year (15 mpy) or a rate from Annex H.

The standard's own worked example makes the arithmetic concrete: an 8 mm bottom with a release prevention barrier and a fibreglass-reinforced lining earns 10 years initial, plus 5 for the lining, plus 10 for the RPB, plus 4.2 for the thickness credit, giving 29.2 years. Two ceilings bind that result — 20 years without a release prevention barrier, 30 years with one. Clause 6.4.2.1.1 also states that the limits of Table 4.4 do not apply when establishing the initial interval this way.

sections.heading: Subsequent internal intervals: minimum remaining thickness drives the date
paragraphs: Clause 6.4.2.2.1 sets the subsequent interval using the measured tank bottom corrosion rate and the minimum remaining thickness in accordance with 4.4.5, with a maximum of 20 years without a release prevention barrier and 30 years with one. The interval is an output of the thickness calculation, not an input chosen first and justified afterwards.

The governing equation in 4.4.5.1 is MRT = (minimum of RTbc or RTip) − Or(StPr + UPr), where Or is the in-service interval of operation in years to the next internal inspection, RTbc and RTip are minimum remaining thicknesses from bottom-side and internal corrosion after repairs, and StPr and UPr are the top-side and bottom-side corrosion rates not repaired. StPr is zero for coated areas where the coating life equals or exceeds Or; UPr is zero for areas with effective cathodic protection.

The result is tested against Table 4.4. In USC units the minimum bottom plate thickness at next inspection is 0.10 in. for a tank bottom and foundation design with no means for detection and containment of a bottom leak, and 0.05 in. where such means exist or where a reinforced lining thicker than 0.05 in. is applied per API 652. Clause 4.4.5.3 states the consequence directly: if the projected thickness falls short, the bottom is lined, repaired or replaced, or the interval is shortened. In the critical zone, 4.4.5.4 sets a separate floor and prohibits thickness averaging.

sections.heading: The risk-based route and its guardrails
paragraphs: Clause 6.4.2.2.2 permits an owner/operator to set the subsequent internal interval using risk-based inspection procedures in accordance with API RP 580. The assessment must be a systematic evaluation of both the likelihood and the consequence of failure, thoroughly documented, and it must produce an inspection strategy defining methods, frequencies for internal, external and in-service inspections, and mitigation steps.

The guardrails are stricter than most programmes expect. The assessment must be performed by a team with inspection and engineering expertise in API RP 580 principles, tank design, construction and deterioration modes, and that team must review and approve it at intervals not exceeding 10 years, or sooner where process, equipment or consequence changes warrant. The methodology itself requires a documented validation review, and API recommends that validation be performed by an entity external to the assessment team.

One requirement disqualifies a great deal of existing data: corrosion rates derived from prior inspections must come from high or medium inspection effectiveness as defined in the owner's procedures, with API RP 581 given as the reference for those categories. Rates from low inspection effectiveness, spot UT explicitly named, must not be used. Programmes building this capability from scratch should start with our RBI program design service rather than retrofitting a spreadsheet, and remember that PHMSA excludes this route for regulated breakout tanks.

sections.heading: Settlement surveys: how many points, and where
paragraphs: The point count comes from clause 12.5.2. The tank is surveyed with an even number of elevation measurement points, N, uniformly distributed around the circumference, with the minimum given by N = D/10 where D is the tank diameter in feet. All values of N round up to the next higher even whole number, N is never fewer than eight, and the maximum spacing between measurement points is 10 m (32 ft). Annex B Figures B.1 and B.2 reference that method and add that there must be at least four equally spaced diametrical measurement lines.

Clause 12.5.1 requires a settlement survey for all existing tanks undergoing a hydrostatic test, except tanks with a documented service history of acceptable settlement values where no settlement is anticipated during the hydrotest. An initial survey with the tank empty provides the baseline; in its absence, the standard directs that the tank be assumed initially level, which is a conservative and often expensive assumption.

Annex B adds measurement discipline that changes results. Where bottom distortion or corrosion extends beyond the shell, readings taken near bottom lap welds can produce significant elevation errors, and surveying the weld between the first and second shell courses gives more consistent results. Where measured settlement approaches the allowable, Annex B directs repeating the measurement with the bottom forced into contact with the soil, because a bottom not bearing on the foundation over- or under-states settlement.

sections.heading: Acceptance criteria for differential settlement on a ringwall
paragraphs: Annex B separates settlement into three components: uniform settlement, rigid body tilt in a plane, and out-of-plane settlement. Only the third threatens shell and bottom integrity, so the evaluation subtracts the first two. The uniform component is the lowest point on the plotted curve; the rigid tilt plane is represented by an optimum cosine curve of the form Elevpred = a + b·cos(θ + c), fitted by least squares.

The validity test is explicit and is where most evaluations fail quietly. The optimum cosine curve is only considered valid — meaning it accurately fits the measured data — if R² is greater than or equal to 0.9. Where out-of-plane settlement concentrates in one or two areas, the least-squares fit under-predicts the local settlement and is not conservative, and R² typically falls below 0.9. That result routes the tank to the B.2.2.5 and B.3.2.2 procedure, which uses a K factor indexed by tank diameter and roof type, or to a more rigorous engineering assessment.

Where the cosine fit is valid, permissible out-of-plane deflection follows Smax = 11L²Y/(2EH). In USC units Smax and L and H are in feet, with L the arc length between measurement points, Y the shell yield strength in psi, E Young's modulus in psi and H the tank height. Annex B credits the equation to Marr, Ramos and Lambe, Criteria for Settlement of Tanks, ASCE Journal of the Geotechnical Engineering Division, Volume 108, August 1982.

sections.heading: Bottom depressions, edge settlement and what triggers NDE
paragraphs: Annex B contains a trap worth knowing before the survey is commissioned. Taking more measurement points improves the cosine fit but shrinks the arc length L, and because Smax scales with L², using every point in the Smax equation produces a very small allowable settlement. The standard's resolution is to compute the optimum cosine curve using all measurements, then calculate Si and Smax from a subset spaced no further apart than 10 m (32 ft), minimum eight points, with the subset required to include the points furthest from the optimum cosine curve.

For depressions and bulges away from the shell, clause B.3.3 gives the permissible value as BB = 0.37R in USC units, where BB is the maximum bulge height or depression depth in inches and R is the radius of the inscribed circle in the affected area in feet. In SI units the relationship is BB = 0.031R with both terms in millimetres. Those limits apply to bottoms with single-pass lap-welded joints.

Edge settlement is evaluated against allowable values Bew and Be read from Figures B.11 and B.12, with Bew the more conservative and the sensible first screen for all settled areas. Locating the breakover point takes a straight edge laid on the unsettled bottom, and on a cone-up or cone-down bottom the settlement B is measured from a projection of the unsettled bottom rather than from level. Clause B.3.4.2 sets the NDE trigger: where measured settlement exceeds 75 % of Bew, welds within 300 mm (12 in.) of either side of the breakover area are examined visually, and suspect areas by magnetic particle or liquid penetrant examination.

sections.heading: Turning the clauses into a programme that survives an audit
paragraphs: Every interval above is defensible only if the evidence behind it is retrievable — the thickness data feeding RCA and N, the Table 6.1 credits claimed and the installation records supporting them, the MRT calculation with its assumed Or, the settlement point count against N = D/10, and the certification status of the inspector who signed. Programmes fail audits on retrieval far more often than on technical judgement.

Two structural weaknesses recur. The first is inspector certification lapsing mid-cycle, which puts a signature on a report that the code does not recognise; tracking expiry alongside CPD evidence is what our NDT personnel certification tracking module in the Atlantis ERP exists to automate. The second is a monthly routine inspection performed diligently and recorded informally, which produces a compliant tank and a non-compliant record set.

Where the interval calculations themselves need independent review, or where a tank has failed its thickness or settlement criteria and the question becomes whether it can stay in service, our API 653 tank inspector services provide certified inspectors and our fitness-for-service assessment under API 579 handles the evaluation that follows. For sites where the tank programme sits inside a wider PSM obligation, our OSHA PSM mechanical integrity support ties the inspection evidence to the mechanical integrity element. Affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a demo or quote on request via contact.

faq.q: Is the five-year external inspection interval a maximum or a target?
faq.a: A maximum. Clause 6.3.2.1 requires the external inspection at least every five years or RCA/4N years, whichever is less, so a tank with low remaining corrosion allowance and an active shell corrosion rate falls due sooner. A tank with 40 mils remaining corroding at 4 mils per year is due at 2.5 years. Show the calculation on the report.

faq.q: Can a tank ever go 30 years between internal inspections?
faq.a: Only with a release prevention barrier. Both the initial interval under 6.4.2.1.1 and the subsequent corrosion-rate interval under 6.4.2.2.1 cap at 20 years without an RPB and 30 years with one. PHMSA's 49 CFR 195.432 additionally excludes the alternative risk-based internal interval provision for regulated breakout tanks, so RBI cannot be used to extend those assets.

faq.q: Does the internal inspection have to be done with the tank out of service?
faq.a: Not always. Clause 6.4.1.2 permits the internal inspection to be accomplished in service where it is required solely to determine tank bottom condition and integrity, using robotic ultrasonic thickness measurement and other on-stream methods, supplemented by electromagnetic methods. The data collected must be sufficient to evaluate thickness, corrosion rate and bottom integrity and to establish the next interval.

faq.q: How does API 653 treat a ringwall showing differential settlement?
faq.a: It separates uniform settlement and rigid tilt from the out-of-plane component, evaluates the out-of-plane deflection against Smax = 11L²Y/(2EH) where a cosine fit with R² of 0.9 or better exists, and routes non-conforming or poorly fitted profiles to the B.3.2.2 K-factor procedure or a rigorous engineering assessment by an engineer experienced in tank settlement analysis.

faq.q: What corrosion rate data is disallowed in an RBI assessment?
faq.a: Rates derived from low inspection effectiveness. Clause 6.4.2.2.2 requires corrosion rates based on prior inspections to come from high or medium inspection effectiveness as defined in the owner/operator's procedures, with API RP 581 cited for examples, and states explicitly that rates from low effectiveness such as spot UT must not be used in the RBI process.

faq.q: Which edition of API 653 should a programme be written to?
faq.a: The edition your jurisdiction and your owner specification name. Clause numbers here follow the Fifth Edition, November 2014, and subsequent addenda renumber some subclauses without changing the substance of the intervals. Verify clause references against the edition on the API Publications Effectivity Sheet before citing them in a written procedure or an inspection report.

title: NDT Techs Make $78,350 Median, Not the $48,570 BLS Number
description: US NDT technicians earn a $78,350 median under SOC 17-3029, not the $48,570 quality-inspector figure. Pay decomposed by level, method, industry and state.
h1: What NDT Technicians Actually Take Home in the US, by Level and Method
answer: NDT technicians in the US earn a median of $78,350 a year, or $37.67 an hour, under the federal occupation that actually covers them. Level I trainees start near $40,000. Level II runs $55,000 to $80,000, with phased-array and TOFD hands pushing $110,000. Level III salaries reach $130,000. Gulf Coast turnaround work adds per diem and overtime on top of all of it.
expansion: Four things move an NDT paycheck, and only one is the certification level printed on the card. Method comes first: an MT and PT hand and a phased-array hand hold the same Level II, and the phased-array hand earns forty to seventy percent more. Industry comes second, because aerospace and nuclear pay a documentation premium while refinery turnaround work pays an availability premium. Geography comes third, and the Gulf Coast leads because the shutdown work sits there. Schedule comes fourth, and it is the one people forget: a six-day, twelve-hour rotation with per diem turns a $75,000 base into a six-figure year without a raise. Federal wage tables report annual salary for the surveyed position only, so they capture none of that. Read them as a floor for the staff half of the trade, then add method premium, overtime and per diem on top.
source: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025, for SOC 17-3029 and SOC 51-9061 via O*NET OnLine; Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter and Salary.com US aggregates retrieved 2026; GSA FY2026 CONUS per diem schedule.

table.note: The last two rows are the same government survey read two ways. O*NET maps Non-Destructive Testing Specialists, code 17-3029.01, to the engineering technician wage series at a $78,350 median. SOC 51-9061 lumps inspection in with quality control inspectors, QA auditors and weighers at $48,570. Quoting 51-9061 understates a working Level II by roughly $30,000, which is more than the entire gap between Level I and Level II.

facets.q: How much do NDT techs make an hour?
facets.a: The federal median for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists is $37.67 an hour as of May 2025, against an annual median of $78,350. The tenth percentile of the occupation earns $47,030 a year and the ninetieth $118,330. A Level I trainee bills $19 to $26, a general Level II $26 to $34, and a phased-array Level II $38 to $53. Gulf Coast contract inspectors see $50 and above before overtime.

facets.q: Does NDT pay more than welding?
facets.a: Yes at Level II and above. A certified welder moving into NDT starts near the Level I band of $40,000 to $55,000 and passes journeyman welder pay once a second and third method are certified. The federal median for NDT specialists is $78,350. Welders crossing over keep their code and joint-configuration knowledge, which shortens the ramp on weld-focused UT and RT work.

facets.q: How much does an NDT Level II make in Texas?
facets.a: The Texas median for NDT specialists is $73,860, with a tenth percentile of $38,720 and a ninetieth of $113,050. Houston Level II roles advertise $75,000 to $105,000 because refinery density and offshore access keep the bidding competitive. Those figures are base only. Per diem on travel work and turnaround overtime push the actual annual number well past the state ninetieth percentile.

facets.q: What is the highest-paying NDT method?
facets.a: Phased-array ultrasonics. A Level II holding PAUT earns $80,000 to $110,000 against an MT and PT baseline near $60,000, a premium of forty to seventy percent on the same certification level. TOFD sits just below at $75,000 to $100,000. Both premiums exist because the equipment is expensive, the scan plans are technical, and few people produce a defensible weld map unsupervised.

facets.q: Do NDT technicians get per diem on top of salary?
facets.a: On travel and turnaround work, yes. Under an accountable plan a per diem paid at or below the federal rate is reimbursement rather than wages, so it stays off the W-2. The GSA schedule for fiscal 2026 sets the standard rate at $178 a day and Houston at $208. Market per diem on onshore US assignments runs $75 to $150 a day.

facets.q: How long does it take to go from Level I to Level III pay?
facets.a: Four to eight years for most technicians, and the driver is method count rather than calendar time. Each method carries its own training-hour and experience-hour requirement before certification, and Level III adds a basic examination plus a method examination. Technicians who log hours deliberately across UT, RT and phased array reach the top of the Level II band before others finish a second method.

sections.heading: The number, in plain language
paragraphs: An NDT technician in the United States earns a median of $78,350 a year, which is $37.67 an hour, under SOC 17-3029, the federal wage series that O*NET maps Non-Destructive Testing Specialists to. The occupation runs from $47,030 at the tenth percentile to $118,330 at the ninetieth. That spread is not survey noise. It is the distance between a first-year trainee shooting film on a fabrication shop floor and a phased-array hand on a refinery turnaround, and the rest of this page decomposes it.

Certification level tells you less than people expect. The card sets what a technician is allowed to sign; the method, the schedule and the plant set what the technician is paid. A Level II holding magnetic particle and penetrant sits near $60,000. The same Level II card with phased-array ultrasonics on it clears $100,000. Our [Level II salary breakdown](/ndt-level-2-salary) splits that by method and employer type, and the [Level I salary page](/ndt-level-1-salary) shows where the ladder starts and what a first card is worth.

Three numbers anchor the ladder: roughly $40,000 to $55,000 at Level I, $55,000 to $80,000 at Level II, and $80,000 to $130,000 at Level III. Add per diem and turnaround overtime and the top of each band moves up by a third. The [Level III salary page](/ndt-level-3-salary) covers the split between staff Level IIIs who run one written practice and contract Level IIIs carrying several client programmes, which is where the range widens most sharply.

sections.heading: Why $48,570 keeps showing up, and why it is the wrong code
paragraphs: Search for NDT pay and you will hit $48,570, the May 2025 median for SOC 51-9061, Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers and Weighers. That code is real government data. It is also the wrong occupation. Its own published sample job titles are Inspector, QA Auditor, Quality Control Inspector, Quality Technician and Test Technician. Nothing in that list requires a radiation badge, an employer written practice, a UT thickness log or a method certification of any kind.

The code that maps to the trade is 17-3029.01, Non-Destructive Testing Specialists, which draws its wages from Engineering Technologists and Technicians, Except Drafters, All Other. Its May 2025 median is $78,350. The gap between the two codes is $29,780, larger than the gap between a Level I and a Level II. Quoting 51-9061 to a working technician is how a salary article loses its reader in the first paragraph, and it happens constantly across the sites that rank for these queries.

Neither code captures schedule. BLS reports annual wage for the position as surveyed, so rotation premiums, call-out pay and per diem land outside the number entirely. A technician on a six-day, twelve-hour turnaround schedule earns a year that no federal table shows. Use 17-3029 as the floor for staff positions and treat everything on top as separate, which is exactly how the [2026 global NDT salary guide](/blog/ndt-salary-guide-2026-global) structures its regional and method tables.

sections.heading: Level I, II and III: what each rung actually pays
paragraphs: Level I runs $40,000 to $55,000. The card permits performing calibrations and tests under a Level II procedure without independent evaluation, so employers price it as an apprenticeship. Most Level I hires in the US sit inside a company programme rather than paying their own way, because certification is granted by the employer under a written practice. The technicians who move fastest treat method hours as the asset and log them deliberately from the first week on the job.

Level II runs $55,000 to $80,000 across the general population and $80,000 to $110,000 for advanced methods. This is the rung where pay stops tracking seniority and starts tracking capability. Two technicians hired the same week diverge by $40,000 inside four years purely on which methods their employer certified them in. Glassdoor's US aggregate for NDT Technician Level II sits at $77,064 average with a $61,981 to $97,044 interquartile range, which brackets the same story from a different dataset.

Level III runs $80,000 to $130,000 and splits into two populations. Staff Level IIIs write and own the written practice and qualify personnel inside one employer. Contract and outsourced Level IIIs carry several client programmes at once and earn on the higher half of the band. Glassdoor's ASNT NDT Level III aggregate reports a $100,205 average with a $77,507 to $131,287 quartile spread, which is what two distinct populations look like when a site averages them into one figure.

sections.heading: Method premium: PAUT and TOFD are where the money is
paragraphs: The single largest lever on an NDT paycheck is method, not years served. Phased-array ultrasonics at Level II pays $80,000 to $110,000 against a magnetic particle and penetrant baseline near $60,000, a forty to seventy percent premium on the same certification level. Time-of-flight diffraction sits just under it at $75,000 to $100,000. Both premiums encode a scarcity: the equipment costs real money, the scan plans are technical, and few technicians produce a defensible weld map without supervision.

Radiography carries a differently shaped premium. RT pays above MT and PT because of the radiation card, the night work and the exclusion zones, not because interpretation is harder. Digital and computed radiography shift the picture again by cutting shot time and raising throughput per technician, which employers price into the contract rate rather than into the base salary. A technician holding both RT and phased array is the most portable person on a Gulf Coast crew and gets priced accordingly.

The practical implication is boring and reliable: the fastest raise available to a Level II is another method, not another year. Employers fund that when the method sits on their scope of work, because adding phased array across an existing crew costs a fraction of hiring phased-array hands at market rate, and the crew keeps the client relationships it already has. That arithmetic is why method expansion beats recruitment in almost every NDT service business.

sections.heading: Industry: the same card pays differently across sectors
paragraphs: Aerospace and nuclear pay a documentation premium. The inspection is not harder; the traceability, the personnel qualification records and the audit exposure are. Technicians in those sectors sit at the top of the staff band with modest overtime and heavy paperwork. Aerospace personnel qualification runs under NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, which changes the examination and eligibility requirements an employer has to meet before it can certify anyone onto a method.

Refinery and petrochemical work pays an availability premium instead. The base looks ordinary and the year does not, because turnarounds compress twelve months of work into six weeks of twelve-hour days. Fabrication and structural shops pay the lowest bands with the most predictable hours. Pipeline construction sits between them and swings hardest with capital spending. Power generation outage work behaves like refinery turnaround work on a shorter and more predictable cycle.

Sector choice therefore sets the shape of the income, not only its size. A fabrication shop Level II on $68,000 with no travel and a turnaround Level II on $68,000 base with eighteen weeks of shutdown work do not take home the same money, and the difference runs to five figures. Compare offers on annualised all-in, and read the [NDT inspector salary page](/ndt-inspector-salary) for how inspection-titled roles price the same underlying skills differently.

sections.heading: Region: Texas leads, Louisiana lags, and the federal data shows it
paragraphs: State wage data for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists puts Texas at a $73,860 median with a $38,720 to $113,050 spread, and Louisiana at a $58,960 median with a $38,160 to $103,810 spread. Both sit under the $78,350 national median, which surprises people who assume the Gulf Coast pays the most. It does pay the most, but through per diem, call-out and overtime, none of which the annual wage series captures.

Houston Level II roles advertise $75,000 to $105,000 because the density of refineries, offshore access and turnaround contractors keeps the bidding competitive. Offshore Gulf of Mexico packages run on day rates instead, at $500 to $800 per twelve-hour day on rotation, which produces annual figures that no state median resembles. Onshore travel work adds market per diem of $75 to $150 a day on top of whatever the base salary line says.

Outside the Gulf Coast, the strongest US markets are the aerospace corridors, the operating nuclear fleet and pipeline capital projects. Cost of living erases part of the nominal advantage in the Northeast and California. The certification that pays in Wichita is not the one that pays in Baytown, which is why [corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) programmes get scoped against the client base a crew actually serves rather than against a generic method list.

sections.heading: Base is not take-home: per diem, overtime and rotation
paragraphs: Per diem is the most misread line on an NDT offer. Under an accountable plan, a per diem paid at or under the applicable federal rate is reimbursement rather than wages, so it does not appear on a W-2 as income. The GSA schedule for federal fiscal year 2026 sets the standard continental US rate at $110 lodging plus $68 meals and incidentals, which is $178 a day, and Houston at $128 plus $80, which is $208 a day.

Overtime is the second line. A non-exempt technician earns one and a half times the regular rate for hours over forty in a workweek under the Fair Labor Standards Act. On a six-day, twelve-hour turnaround schedule that is thirty-two overtime hours a week, billing as eighty-eight straight-time-equivalent hours. Six weeks of that pattern moves an annual figure by five digits, which is why turnaround technicians rarely accept staff positions at the same nominal base salary.

The third line is rotation. Offshore and remote assignments trade weeks at home for day rates and travel allowances, and the all-in figure stops resembling a salary at all. When you compare two offers, annualise all four components: base, expected overtime hours, per diem days actually worked, and rotation allowance. The [NDT technician salary page](/ndt-technician-salary) sets out that arithmetic with worked examples for both staff and contract patterns.

sections.heading: How to move your number inside twelve months
paragraphs: Add a method. That is the entire answer for a Level I or Level II, and the numbers support it: the phased-array premium at Level II is larger than the whole gap between Level I and Level II. Log the on-the-job hours properly while you do it, because an incomplete experience record is the most common reason a certification stalls at the employer review stage rather than at the examination stage, and it costs months.

Then decide between the code-inspector track and the Level III track. Code inspection covering pressure vessels, piping and storage tanks pays on a different curve and rewards a different credential set, and we compare the two branches in [Gulf Coast code inspector pay against CWI pay](/blog/code-inspector-vs-cwi-salary-gulf-coast). The Level III track pays on method breadth and programme ownership instead, and it leads toward writing the written practice rather than working under one.

Employers hold most of the leverage in this trade, because method certification is granted by an employer under a written practice rather than bought from a school. If your programme is not certifying people onto new methods, that is the constraint worth attacking first. [Corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) exists for exactly that situation: expanding an existing crew onto the methods the client base is already asking your schedulers about.

faq.q: How much do NDT technicians make in the US?
faq.a: The federal median is $78,350 a year, or $37.67 an hour, for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists under SOC 17-3029 in the May 2025 wage survey. The tenth percentile is $47,030 and the ninetieth is $118,330. By certification level, Level I runs $40,000 to $55,000, Level II runs $55,000 to $80,000, and Level III runs $80,000 to $130,000 before overtime and per diem.

faq.q: Why do salary sites give such different NDT numbers?
faq.a: Because they measure different populations. Federal SOC 51-9061 includes sorters, samplers and weighers and reports $48,570. SOC 17-3029 filters to NDT specialists and reports $78,350. Glassdoor reports $77,064 for NDT Technician Level II, ZipRecruiter $61,725, and Salary.com $64,000. Title-based aggregators include trainees and uncertified assistants under the same job title, which pulls the average down.

faq.q: Is NDT a good career in 2026?
faq.a: The federal projection for NDT specialists is one to two percent employment growth from 2024 to 2034, with 5,700 annual openings against 67,300 people employed. Growth is slow but replacement demand is steady, and the advanced-method half of the trade is short of people. Pay concentrates in phased array, radiography and code inspection rather than in the entry-level methods.

faq.q: What does an NDT Level II earn with phased array?
faq.a: Between $80,000 and $110,000 in the US, against $55,000 to $70,000 for the same Level II card holding only magnetic particle and penetrant. That is a forty to seventy percent premium for one additional method. Time-of-flight diffraction pays $75,000 to $100,000. Both figures are base salary and exclude turnaround overtime and travel per diem.

faq.q: Do you need a degree to earn six figures in NDT?
faq.a: No. The route to six figures runs through method certification, not education. A Level II holding phased array and radiography on Gulf Coast turnaround work clears $100,000 with overtime and per diem. A degree shortens the eligibility clock for code inspection certifications later, which is where it pays back, but it is not required for the technician ladder.

title: Gulf Coast API Inspectors Out-Earn CWIs by $46k on Cert Data
description: Gulf Coast pressure vessel and piping inspector pay against AWS CWI pay: base, GSA FY2026 per diem, and what turnaround overtime at 1.5x actually adds.
h1: Pressure Vessel and Piping Inspector Pay vs CWI Pay on the Gulf Coast
answer: On the Gulf Coast, API 510 and 570 code inspectors bill $50 to $59 an hour against CWI rates near $30. Certification-filtered data puts API 510 holders at $131,000 average versus $85,000 for CWIs. Per diem adds $178 to $208 a day untaxed on travel work, and turnaround overtime at one and a half times over forty adds more than the base gap does.
expansion: The comparison breaks the moment you line up two quoted base salaries, because the two roles are paid on different instruments. A plant staff CWI is salaried and exempt, priced against a local labour market: Salary.com puts the US CWI average at $57,736 and ZipRecruiter puts Houston at $63,498. A contract code inspector on turnaround is hourly and non-exempt, priced against scarcity inside a six-week window, with postings for combined API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors showing $50 to $59 an hour. At sixty hours a week with time and a half over forty, that hourly rate produces a weekly gross the salaried figure cannot reach. Add a non-taxable per diem of $178 to $208 a day and the gap widens again. Certification-based survey data captures this better than title-based aggregates: Payscale reports $131,000 average for API 510 holders against $85,000 for CWI holders.

table.note: The $131,000 and $85,000 rows are certification-filtered self-reported survey data on small samples, 74 and 287 respondents. The $57,736 and $62,807 rows are title-based aggregates that include uncertified people holding the same job title. Both are useful and neither is a rate card. Comparing a certification-filtered figure against a title-based one is how the Gulf Coast pay question gets answered wrongly, and it is why a page ranking first on this query still fails to satisfy the person asking.

facets.q: Is an API 510 worth more than a CWI on the Gulf Coast?
facets.a: Payscale's certification data puts API 510 holders at $131,000 average against $85,000 for CWI holders, a $46,000 gap. That gap reflects role as much as credential: API code inspectors work owner-user and contract turnaround scopes priced on shutdown scarcity, while most CWIs sit in fabrication shops and project QA on steady salaried hours. Holding both is the best-paid combination on the coast.

facets.q: How much per diem do Gulf Coast turnaround inspectors get?
facets.a: The GSA federal rate for fiscal 2026 sets Houston at $128 lodging plus $80 meals and incidentals, $208 a day. Lake Charles and most other Gulf Coast towns fall to the standard rate of $110 plus $68, $178 a day. Contractors pay at or near those numbers because anything above the federal rate becomes taxable wages. Over a six-week turnaround that is $7,476 to $8,736.

facets.q: Is per diem taxable income on an inspection job?
facets.a: Per diem paid under an accountable plan at or below the federal rate is reimbursement, not wages, and does not appear as taxable income. IRS Notice 2025-54 sets the high-low substantiation rates effective 1 October 2025 at $319 for high-cost localities and $225 for the rest of the continental US. Anything paid above the applicable rate is wages and gets taxed and reported normally.

facets.q: Why do quoted CWI salaries on the Gulf Coast look so low?
facets.a: Because title-based aggregators pull from postings and self-reports filed under the title welding inspector, which sweeps in uncertified inspection assistants and shop QC clerks. Salary.com's US CWI average is $57,736 with a $68,113 ninetieth percentile. Payscale's certification-filtered figure for people who actually hold the card is $85,000. The credential filter alone accounts for roughly $27,000 of apparent difference.

facets.q: Do plant staff inspectors earn more than contract field inspectors?
facets.a: On base, plant staff usually win. On annual all-in, contract field inspectors win in a heavy turnaround year and lose in a light one. Staff roles are exempt and salaried, so extra outage hours are unpaid. Contract roles are non-exempt at one and a half times over forty with per diem on top. The trade is variance: staff pay is flat, field pay tracks the outage calendar.

facets.q: What does turnaround overtime add to an inspector's year?
facets.a: A six-day, twelve-hour schedule is seventy-two hours a week: forty straight plus thirty-two at time and a half, billing as eighty-eight straight-time hours. At $55 an hour that is $4,840 a week against $2,200 for a normal forty-hour week. Six weeks grosses $29,040 where six ordinary weeks gross $13,200, a $15,840 premium before per diem adds another $7,476 to $8,736.

sections.heading: The question as asked: base first, then all-in
paragraphs: Base salaries on the Gulf Coast put an AWS CWI in the high fifties to low sixties and a certified code inspector, API 510 for pressure vessels and API 570 for piping, well above it. Salary.com's US CWI average is $57,736 as of August 2026. ZipRecruiter's Houston CWI figure is $63,498 with an $84,515 ninetieth percentile. Payscale's certification-filtered figure for people holding API 510 is $131,000 average across seventy-four respondents.

All-in changes the shape rather than only the size. Contract code inspectors work turnarounds as non-exempt hourly staff, so thirty-two hours of every seventy-two-hour week bill at one and a half times, and per diem of $178 to $208 a day arrives untaxed on top of that. A CWI on a plant staff payroll is exempt and salaried, so the extra hours worked during the same outage cost the employer nothing.

The short answer, then: the two credentials cost roughly the same to obtain and pay very differently, and most of the distance comes from the employment structure each one leads into rather than from the examination itself. Our [comparison of AWS CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II](/compare/aws-cwi-vs-api-577-vs-asnt-level-ii) sets out what each credential authorises a holder to sign before you try to price any of them.

sections.heading: Why the published base numbers disagree by $70,000
paragraphs: Two kinds of salary data circulate and they measure different populations. Title-based aggregates from Salary.com, ZipRecruiter and Indeed scrape postings and self-reports filed under a job title. Certification-based surveys, such as Payscale's credential pages, filter to people who hold the card. For CWI the two disagree by $27,000: $57,736 against $85,000. For pressure vessel inspection they disagree by $68,000: $62,807 against $131,000.

Neither number is wrong. The title series includes inspection assistants, uncertified shop QC and trainees carrying the same title. The certification series includes senior people who volunteer their pay to a salary site, which skews high and rests on small samples, seventy-four respondents for API 510 and 287 for CWI. Read them as a bracket rather than a rate. The honest Gulf Coast reading sits nearer the certification figure for contract turnaround roles and nearer the title figure for salaried plant positions.

Federal data supplies a third bracket and excludes everything interesting. The May 2025 wage survey for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists puts Texas at a $73,860 median and Louisiana at $58,960, both reported as annual wage only. Per diem, rotation allowances and call-out pay sit outside the survey entirely, which is why the state medians read lower than the market feels to anyone actually working a spring turnaround season.

sections.heading: The per diem line: what GSA sets and what contractors pay
paragraphs: GSA publishes the federal per diem schedule for fiscal 2026, running 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2026. Houston, covering Harris, Fort Bend and Montgomery counties, is $128 lodging plus $80 meals and incidentals, $208 a day, with $60 on first and last travel days. Lake Charles falls to the standard continental rate of $110 plus $68, which is $178 a day. Alexandria and Natchitoches sit at $112 plus $68.

Contractors anchor to these numbers for a tax reason rather than a generous one. Under an accountable plan, per diem paid at or below the applicable federal rate is reimbursement and stays off the W-2. IRS Notice 2025-54 sets the high-low substantiation alternative at $319 for high-cost localities and $225 for the rest of the continental United States from 1 October 2025. Pay above the applicable rate and the excess becomes taxable wages immediately.

The effect on any comparison is large. A six-week turnaround at the Houston rate is $8,736 of untaxed reimbursement; at the standard rate it is $7,476. Against a salaried CWI who sleeps at home, that is a straight addition to the year. Our [2026 NDT salary guide](/blog/ndt-salary-guide-2026-global) records market per diem on onshore US travel work at $75 to $150 a day, which sits below the federal ceiling.

sections.heading: Turnaround overtime is the real multiplier
paragraphs: Federal overtime law does the heavy lifting here. A non-exempt employee earns one and a half times the regular rate for hours over forty in a workweek. The salary threshold that determines exemption is $684 a week, or $35,568 a year, the 2019 level restored after a federal court in the Eastern District of Texas vacated the 2024 Department of Labor rule nationwide on 15 November 2024. Almost no field inspector clears exemption on duties anyway.

Contract inspectors are hourly and non-exempt, so a six-day, twelve-hour turnaround schedule pays forty straight hours plus thirty-two at one and a half times, billing as eighty-eight straight-time-equivalent hours a week. At $55 an hour that grosses $4,840 a week. Six weeks grosses $29,040 where six ordinary forty-hour weeks gross $13,200. The $15,840 difference is earned inside six weeks and is the single largest swing in a Gulf Coast inspector's year.

Plant staff inspectors classified as exempt see none of that. Their outage is longer days at the same salary, sometimes softened by a fixed turnaround bonus. This is precisely why two offers with identical base numbers produce different years, and why the base-against-base comparison is the wrong comparison to make. Ask for the outage and overtime policy in writing before you compare anything else on the two offer letters.

sections.heading: Which credential commands which band
paragraphs: CWI authorises weld inspection to AWS D1.1, API 1104 and the other structural and pipeline codes, and it is the entry credential for fabrication quality assurance. AWS prices initial certification at $1,255 for members and $1,520 for non-members effective 1 January 2026, with the two-week seminar and examination package at $3,935 for members and $4,200 for non-members. Renewal at years three and six by work experience runs $650 for members.

API 510 and 570 authorise in-service inspection of pressure vessels and piping under owner-user programmes, which is a different legal position: the certificate underwrites a fitness decision on operating equipment. API charges $875 for members and $1,125 for non-members. The examination is a seven-and-a-half-hour day at a Prometric centre with 170 questions, 140 of them scored, split 110 closed-book and 60 open-book. Eligibility starts at one year of experience with an engineering degree.

ASNT Level II and Level III sit alongside both rather than beneath them, because NDT method certification is granted by an employer under a written practice rather than by an examination body. The best-paid people on a Gulf Coast crew hold a stack: an ASNT Level III in the methods, an API code certification and a CWI. Our [Level III salary page](/ndt-level-3-salary) shows what the top of that stack earns in the US market.

sections.heading: Plant staff against contract field: why base comparisons mislead
paragraphs: A plant staff inspector's offer is built for retention: salary, benefits, a retirement match, predictable hours and a home bed. A contract field inspector's offer is built for mobilisation: an hourly rate, overtime, per diem, travel days and no guarantee past the outage. Quoting the two base figures side by side compares a twelve-month instrument against a six-week one. The two only become comparable after both are annualised on the same assumptions.

Annualise honestly. Take the contract rate, multiply by realistic billed hours including overtime, add the per diem days actually worked, then subtract the unbilled weeks between jobs and the cost of self-funded benefits. Take the staff salary, add the bonus, and value the benefits at replacement cost. In a heavy turnaround year the contract number wins by a wide margin. In a light year, with two outages cancelled, it loses badly.

This is why career moves on the Gulf Coast run in both directions rather than one. Field inspectors take staff jobs when they want the schedule back; staff inspectors go contract when the outage calendar is full. The [NDT inspector salary page](/ndt-inspector-salary) breaks the two employment structures out separately rather than averaging them, because averaging them produces the figure nobody in the trade recognises.

sections.heading: Stacking credentials is where the Gulf Coast money is
paragraphs: The highest bands on the coast belong to people who can sign more than one kind of document. An inspector holding API 510, a CWI and an ASNT Level II in ultrasonics can accept a vessel inspection scope, evaluate the repair welds and take the thickness readings without a second body on site. Contractors pay a premium for that because it removes an entire mobilisation from the job cost.

Order matters more than people expect. Method certification comes first, because ultrasonics and radiography open the field work that funds everything else. CWI comes second, because weld inspection sits on the critical path in fabrication and repair. Code certification comes last, because its eligibility clock counts inspection experience acquired under an authorised inspection agency, and the first two credentials are what generate that experience. Reversing the order stalls the API application.

Employers fund this progression when the scope requires it, which is why the [welder to NDT inspector career path](/blog/welder-to-ndt-inspector-us-career-path-2026) starts on a shop floor rather than in a classroom. Each addition moves the pay curve, and the largest single step on the Gulf Coast is the code certification, because it changes the category of contract the holder can be assigned to rather than merely the rate.

sections.heading: How to read a Gulf Coast offer
paragraphs: Ask five questions before comparing anything. Is the role exempt or non-exempt? What is the per diem, and is it paid on days off during a hitch? What billed-hours pattern does the contractor expect? Who pays for travel days and mobilisation? What happens between outages? Four of those five move the annual number more than the base does, and the fifth decides whether there is a reliable annual number at all.

Then check the credential against the scope. An API 510 on a job that never touches in-service pressure vessels earns nothing extra, and a CWI on a turnaround that is entirely thickness surveys earns nothing extra either. The premium attaches to the document you are asked to sign, not to the card in your wallet. Match the certification to the work the contract actually specifies before you value it.

For the level-by-level US picture underneath these Gulf Coast numbers, read [what NDT technicians actually make](/blog/how-much-do-ndt-technicians-make), which decomposes the same federal wage series by certification level and method. If you run the programme rather than work in it, our [API 510 pressure vessel inspector services](/consulting/api-510-pressure-vessel-inspector-services) and [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) cover the two positions clients most often outsource when the outage calendar outruns the certified headcount already on the roster.

faq.q: What does a code inspector earn on the Gulf Coast compared with a CWI?
faq.a: Certification-filtered survey data puts API 510 holders at $131,000 average against $85,000 for CWI holders. Field postings for combined API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors show $50 to $59 an hour against roughly $30 an hour for CWI work. Add per diem of $178 to $208 a day and turnaround overtime, and the contract code inspector's year separates further.

faq.q: Does per diem count toward salary when comparing two offers?
faq.a: It counts toward take-home but not toward taxable wages. A per diem paid at or below the federal rate under an accountable plan is reimbursement, so it never appears on a W-2. Annualise it separately: per diem days actually worked multiplied by the daily rate. Six weeks of Houston turnaround work adds $8,736 that no salary figure will show.

faq.q: Which pays more over a career, CWI or API 510?
faq.a: API 510, on the published data, and by roughly $46,000 a year on Payscale's certification averages. The CWI is cheaper and faster to obtain and opens fabrication and construction work. API 510 requires documented inspection experience under an authorised inspection agency first, which most people accumulate while holding a CWI or an ASNT Level II.

faq.q: Are Gulf Coast inspector rates falling in 2026?
faq.a: Federal projections for NDT specialists show one to two percent employment growth from 2024 to 2034 with 5,700 annual openings, so the labour market is replacement-driven rather than expanding. Rates on the Gulf Coast track the turnaround calendar rather than the growth rate, and the scarce credential stack still clears the top of every published band.

faq.q: Should a fabrication shop hire a CWI or an API inspector?
faq.a: A CWI. New construction sits under the fabrication codes and the inspection authority for the pressure boundary is the Authorized Inspector, not an API 510 holder. API code certifications pay for themselves on in-service scopes: operating vessels, piping circuits and storage tanks, where the certificate authorises inspection intervals and repair sign-off.

title: API 510 All-In Runs $2,082 to $6,283; Holders Average $131k
description: Every published 2026 cost line for sponsoring an API 510: the $875 and $1,125 exam fees, $999 to $4,950 prep, Prometric travel and the three-year recert cycle.
h1: The Honest All-In Cost of an API 510 in 2026, and What It Returns
answer: Yes, and the sponsorship cost is bounded. All-in runs $2,082 to $6,283 per candidate. API charges $875 for members and $1,125 for non-members. Prep courses run $999 self-paced online to $4,950 instructor-led. Payscale puts API 510 holders at $131,000 average against $62,807 for the generic pressure vessel inspector title. Recertification costs $745 every three years.
expansion: Two numbers decide this. The cost side is published and bounded: API charges $875 for members and $1,125 for non-members for initial certification, prep courses run from $999 for a self-paced online programme to $4,950 for a five-day instructor-led course, and the examination is in person only at a Prometric centre, which adds a travel day at the federal per diem rate of $178 to $208. The return side is a role change rather than a raise. API 510 is what an owner-user programme requires before a person can authorise inspection intervals and sign off repairs on in-service pressure vessels, and that signature is a bid qualification on refinery and petrochemical work. Payscale's certification-filtered data puts holders at $131,000 average against $62,807 for the generic pressure vessel inspector title. One sponsored field technician returns the outlay inside a single turnaround season.
source: API Individual Certification Programs, Schedules and Fees and the API 510 programme page, 2026 and 2027 windows; API ICP-PD-102-Inspector recertification requirements, revision 15 September 2025; API and Prometric exam delivery notices; Atlas API Training and PetroKnowledge published course prices; GSA FY2026 per diem schedule; Payscale February 2026 and Salary.com December 2025.
