table.note: NASA-STD-5009 is an NDE capability requirement, not a personnel qualification standard. It tells you what flaw size your procedure has to find with what reliability. A supplier still needs a NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A written practice underneath it to certify the people running those procedures — the two documents answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other.

facets.q: Does Nadcap accreditation satisfy NASA-STD-5009?
facets.a: No. Nadcap AC7114 accredits your special process against industry baseline criteria. NASA-STD-5009 sets the flaw-size detection capability a procedure must demonstrate for fracture-critical metallic components, which is a capability demonstration on representative hardware with representative flaws. A Nadcap-accredited supplier can still fail a Marshall fracture-control review because its procedure was never demonstrated to the required capability.

facets.q: Who certifies NDT personnel on an Army missile subcontract in Huntsville?
facets.a: You do. The purchase order cites the inspection standard — commonly ASTM E1417 for penetrant or E1444 for magnetic particle — and AS9100 requires special process validation, but neither certifies your people. Personnel certification runs through your own written practice, administered by a qualified Level III who writes it, examines the technicians and signs the certification records. DCMA can review those records on site.

facets.q: What does a Level III do about additively manufactured engine hardware?
facets.a: Writes procedures for hardware whose defect population does not match wrought or cast experience. AM parts carry lack-of-fusion, porosity and unfused powder in internal geometries penetrant cannot reach, which pushes inspection toward computed tomography and radiography, with surface methods after machining. The Level III sets the technique, defines what counts as an indication in that geometry, and qualifies operators to interpret it.

facets.q: We inspect friction stir welds for launch vehicle structure. What has to be documented?
facets.a: A procedure and a technique sheet for each joint configuration and thickness, not one procedure for all welds. Friction stir joints produce characteristic defect types — root flaws, wormholes, lack of penetration — at depths and orientations that dictate the probe, wedge, scan plan and reference standard. The reference standard has to contain representative flaws in representative material, and its control has to be documented.

facets.q: Our contract cites ASTM E1417 rather than a customer process spec. Does that change the written practice?
facets.a: It changes what the written practice must reference. ASTM E1417 carries its own process control, system performance verification, lighting and documentation requirements, and they are revision-specific. Your written practice and procedures both have to name the revision the purchase order cites, and your change control has to catch it when the customer moves to a newer revision mid-contract.

facets.q: Can a Huntsville small business win propulsion subcontract work without a staff Level III?
facets.a: Yes, with an outsourced one named in the written practice. Prime supplier questionnaires ask who your Responsible Level 3 is and what methods that person is qualified in. A named contracted Level III with a documented scope and real site presence answers the question. A blank field or a quality manager listed with no NDT qualification ends the evaluation.

sections.heading: What Rocket City actually sends out for inspection
paragraphs: Redstone Arsenal is the gravity well. Roughly 38,000 acres, more than 35,000 people, over sixty tenant agencies and more than $50 billion in annual federal budget flowing through Army Materiel Command, Aviation and Missile Command, Space and Missile Defense Command, the Program Executive Offices for Aviation and for Missiles and Space, and Redstone Test Center. NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center sits inside the same perimeter, and Cummings Research Park next door holds over three hundred companies and thirty thousand employees.

The hardware that comes out of that ecosystem is unforgiving. Solid rocket motor cases and nozzles. Liquid engine turbomachinery and combustion chambers. Missile airframes and launcher structure. Welded launch vehicle barrels and domes. Pressure vessels. Almost none of it can be inspected after it flies, and almost all of it is fracture-critical in the sense NASA uses the term — a failure of one component causes loss of the vehicle or the mission.

That drives NDT upstream into the supply base. L3Harris runs autoclaves, tape-wrap systems, hydraulic presses and composite machining in Huntsville. United Launch Alliance welds and machines in Decatur. Blue Origin builds engines. Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Raytheon, Dynetics, Moog, PPG Aerospace and Sierra Nevada all have Huntsville operations. Behind each of them is a layer of machine shops, composites houses and welding firms in Madison and Morgan counties carrying the inspection obligation.

sections.heading: Three authorities over one supplier
paragraphs: A Huntsville tier-two shop with three customers frequently has three different governing regimes on its shop floor at once. NASA Marshall work brings NASA-STD-5009 and the fracture control requirements of NASA-STD-5019. Army missile work brings ASTM standards cited directly on the purchase order under an AS9100 quality system. Commercial propulsion work for L3Harris, ULA or Blue Origin brings Nadcap AC7114 and customer process specifications. The methods are the same. The documentation obligations are not.

Suppliers try to resolve this by writing one procedure per method and hoping it satisfies everyone. It does not, because the three regimes ask different questions. NASA asks what flaw size the procedure reliably finds. The ASTM-cited contract asks whether the process control and system performance checks specified in that revision were performed and recorded. Nadcap asks whether the process meets baseline criteria and whether the people running it were qualified against a written practice.

The resolution is architectural. One written practice covering personnel qualification for all work, with method procedures written per customer specification and technique sheets written per part family. [Building the written practice from the customer flowdowns backwards](/consulting/written-practice-development) is the only structure that survives three auditors, because it keeps the common material common and makes the customer-specific requirements visible rather than buried.

sections.heading: NASA-STD-5009 is a capability requirement, not a certification
paragraphs: This is the misunderstanding that costs Huntsville suppliers contracts. NASA-STD-5009 sets nondestructive evaluation requirements for fracture-critical metallic components — it defines the flaw sizes a procedure has to detect and the confidence with which it has to detect them. It is about the demonstrated capability of a technique on representative hardware. It says nothing about how you certify the person operating the equipment.

Personnel certification comes from somewhere else entirely: a written practice built on NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A, administered by a qualified Level III who writes the practice, sets the training and experience requirements, administers general, specific and practical examinations, and signs the certification records. NAS 410 Revision 5 requires the specific examination after 75% of the experience hours and the practical after 100%, and it requires a named Responsible Level 3 to own the programme.

Suppliers who read a Marshall requirement and conclude they need a capability demonstration are half right. They also need the personnel layer underneath it, because a demonstrated procedure operated by an uncertified technician produces data nobody can accept. [The Responsible Level 3 role NAS 410 defines](/consulting/nas-410-responsible-level-3) is what closes that gap, and it is the role most Huntsville shops of thirty to a hundred people have never filled.

sections.heading: Solid rocket motor work is the fastest-growing NDT demand in Madison County
paragraphs: L3Harris, which absorbed Aerojet Rocketdyne, opened a 379,000-square-foot Advanced Manufacturing Facility South in Huntsville producing inert solid rocket motor components — cases, nozzles, exit cones and aft closures — supporting Standard Missile, Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System and Javelin. It joins a 136,000-square-foot northern facility opened in 2019. More than $20 million went into renovating the southern site, funded in part through a Defense Production Act Title III cooperative agreement, with forty jobs created and over a hundred more projected.

That hardware is composite and it is bonded, which sets the technical agenda for the local supply base. Tape-wrapped and autoclave-cured structure requires ultrasonic inspection of bondlines and insulation, radiography of assembled configurations, and careful discrimination between acceptable manufacturing signatures and rejectable disbonds. Ablative liners in nozzles and exit cones have their own inspection criteria. None of that is covered by a generic ultrasonic procedure written for plate stock.

For a Huntsville subcontractor moving into this work, the requirement is method-specific Level III scope and part-family-specific procedures. [Method procedures written to the customer's process specification](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) with technique sheets naming the reference standard, scan plan and equipment configuration are what a customer source inspector will ask to see before the first shipment, not after.

sections.heading: Decatur, friction stir welds and launch vehicle structure
paragraphs: United Launch Alliance's Decatur plant runs 1.5 million square feet forty minutes west of Huntsville, producing Atlas V, Delta and Vulcan structures. Large-diameter aluminium barrels and domes for launch vehicles are joined by friction stir welding, a solid-state process that produces a defect population unlike fusion welding — root flaws, wormholes and lack of penetration at depths and orientations that a fusion weld procedure was never designed to find.

Inspecting those joints demands a procedure per joint configuration and thickness, with a probe, wedge, scan plan and reference standard chosen for the specific geometry. The reference standard has to carry representative flaws in representative material and be under documented control. Suppliers who submit one ultrasonic procedure covering all weld types discover the gap when a customer engineer asks which flaw orientations the technique was proven against.

The Level III's contribution here is technical rather than administrative. Someone has to select the technique, prove it against a standard containing the flaws that actually occur, write it down in a form a technician can execute repeatably, and then qualify that technician against the written procedure. When a supplier's Level III departs mid-programme, that entire chain stalls — the situation covered in [what to do when your NDT Level 3 resigns](/consulting/ndt-level-3-resigned-what-to-do).

sections.heading: Additive manufacturing has moved NDT from final inspection to process control
paragraphs: Huntsville's propulsion sector adopted additive manufacturing faster than most of American aerospace, because engine components with internal cooling channels and complex manifolds are exactly what the process is good at. Blue Origin's BE-4 production, NASA Marshall's propulsion development work and the missile supply base all now build parts that no conventional inspection method was designed around.

The defect population changed with the process. Lack of fusion between layers, trapped porosity, unfused powder in internal passages and residual stress cracking occur in geometries that penetrant cannot reach and conventional radiography cannot resolve. Computed tomography has moved from a laboratory technique to a production one, and surface methods run after machining rather than instead of volumetric inspection. The acceptance criteria that governed castings do not transfer.

This puts an unusual demand on the Level III: writing procedures for a defect population without decades of field experience behind it, defining what constitutes a rejectable indication in a given geometry, and qualifying operators to interpret CT data rather than film. It is the part of the work that most benefits from a Level III who has seen the same problem at multiple companies, which is one practical argument for [an outsourced ASNT Level III arrangement](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) over a single in-house hire.

sections.heading: Huntsville's Level III labour market, and why the seat stays empty
paragraphs: Huntsville has more engineers per capita than almost any American city and a documented shortage of certified NDT Level IIIs specifically. The people who hold the qualification are absorbed by the organisations that can pay for method breadth and stability — L3Harris, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Dynetics, ULA, Blue Origin and the Marshall contractor base. Small suppliers train someone toward the qualification and lose them.

The consequence is structural rather than occasional. A supplier lands a subcontract from a Redstone prime, receives a supplier quality questionnaire asking who the Responsible Level 3 is and which methods that person is qualified in, and has nothing to write. The evaluation stops there — not because the shop cannot do the work, but because it cannot show a qualified technical authority over the inspection process.

Contracting the role converts an unfillable requisition into a service agreement with a defined method scope. The named Level III does not leave for a prime, the written practice does not go stale between hires, and audit continuity stops depending on one person's career decisions. Firms serving both the missile base here and the fighter and rotorcraft base in Texas often run one programme across both, as described on our [Fort Worth and DFW aerospace NDT page](/consulting/aerospace-ndt-consulting-fort-worth).

sections.heading: What the engagement covers, and where its authority ends
paragraphs: An Atlantis engagement in Huntsville starts with the customer documents: which programmes, which primes, which standards on which purchase orders, at which revisions. From that we author or rebuild the written practice, write and approve method procedures and technique sheets per part family, build the examination programme, complete the personnel files, and be present when a Nadcap auditor, a customer source inspector or a DCMA representative arrives.

The boundaries matter and are worth stating before anyone signs. An outside Level III cannot certify technicians he has not examined, cannot approve procedures in methods he is not qualified in, and cannot create experience hours that were never logged. Responsibility for the programme stays with the employer under NAS 410. Someone on site controls documents, calibration records and reference standards day to day. A capability demonstration under NASA-STD-5009 requires representative hardware the supplier has to provide.

What we do supply is the qualified signatory, the technical documents that signatory stands behind, an examination programme that makes your certifications defensible under scrutiny, and attendance at the audit. Affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the specific mix of NASA, Army and commercial propulsion obligations a given Madison County supplier carries. [Tell us your programmes and your next audit date](/contact) — quote on request.

faq.q: We just won our first subcontract from a Redstone prime. What do we need before first article?
faq.a: A written practice naming a qualified Responsible Level 3, method procedures written to the standard and revision the purchase order cites, technique sheets for the specific part family, and personnel certification records for every technician who will touch the work. If the contract is NASA fracture-critical, you also need a demonstration that the procedure finds the required flaw size. Assemble those before first article, not after a rejection.

faq.q: Does an ASNT NDT Level III certificate mean our technicians are certified?
faq.a: No. The ASNT certificate qualifies one individual by third-party examination. Your technicians are certified by your employer under your own written practice, which the Level III writes and administers. That employer-based route under SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 is exactly why an outsourced Level III has commercial value: the firm needs someone qualified to sign the written practice and administer the examinations, and most Huntsville shops under a hundred people do not have that person on staff.

faq.q: How does DCMA involvement change what we need to keep on file?
faq.a: It changes when the records have to be right rather than what they contain. A DCMA representative can review the quality system on site, and personnel certification records have to reconcile with the written practice on that day. Files reconstructed after a request are a finding in themselves. The practical requirement is that certification records, examination packages, experience logs and vision tests stay current continuously, not before scheduled events.

faq.q: Can one Level III cover both our Huntsville facility and a Decatur operation?
faq.a: Yes, with a single written practice and site-specific annexes covering the equipment, reference standards and customer specifications unique to each location. The Responsible Level 3 scope has to name both sites and the methods at each. Two entirely separate programmes double the maintenance burden and drift apart within a year, which shows up as inconsistent certification records across sites.

faq.q: Do you also handle the ERP and record-keeping side of certification tracking?
faq.a: Yes, where a client wants it. Certification expiry dates, examination records, experience hours, calibration intervals and equipment records are the things that quietly go out of date between audits. Our [Odoo-based ERP configured for NDT companies](/erp) tracks technician certification and equipment calibration alongside project and invoicing data, so the audit evidence is a report rather than a filing exercise. It is optional and separate from the Level III engagement.

title: Charlotte Nuclear NDT Consulting: Pass an NQA-1 Supplier Audit
description: Outsourced ASNT Level III consulting for Charlotte NDT firms facing 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, NQA-1 and NUPIC supplier audits on Duke Energy nuclear contracts.
h1: Getting a Charlotte Inspection Firm Through a Duke Energy or NUPIC Supplier Audit
answer: Duke Energy's nuclear fleet and its Charlotte-area supply chain audit NDT vendors against 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and ASME NQA-1, not ISO 9001. An outsourced ASNT Level III writes your written practice, approves procedures to ASME Section V and XI, administers CP-189 examinations, and stands with you through the NUPIC audit.

Duke Energy runs its six-plant Carolinas fleet from a Charlotte headquarters; McGuire sits seventeen miles northwest in Huntersville and Catawba about thirty-five miles south at Lake Wylie. facets.q: Does an ISO 9001 certificate qualify us for Duke Energy nuclear work?
facets.a: No. ISO 9001 addresses a management system; Duke's nuclear procurement audits against 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, implemented through ASME NQA-1. The two overlap on document control and corrective action but Appendix B adds design control, commercial grade dedication and 10 CFR 21 reporting that ISO 9001 never touches. Keep the certificate, then build the Appendix B programme underneath it.

facets.q: Why does ASME Section XI reference CP-189 instead of SNT-TC-1A?
facets.a: ANSI/ASNT CP-189 was published in 1991 and incorporated into ASME Section XI in the mid-1990s — the only sector adoption of that standard. IWA-2300 governs qualification of personnel performing inservice examination, and Appendix VI reaches CP-189 for VT-1, VT-2 and VT-3 visual examiners. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended guideline; CP-189 is a standard with mandatory requirements, and audits treat that difference literally.

facets.q: What is NUPIC and why does one audit matter so much?
facets.a: The Nuclear Procurement Issues Committee runs joint audits on behalf of subscribing utilities so a supplier is audited once rather than by every plant. That efficiency cuts both ways: a single finding propagates across the whole subscriber list. NUPIC audits confirm the quality programme satisfies 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, 10 CFR 21, NQA-1 and ANSI N45.2, and Regulatory Guide 1.28 points to a triennial cycle.

facets.q: We have no Level III on staff. Can an outsourced one sign our written practice?
facets.a: Yes. SNT-TC-1A explicitly contemplates an outside Level III engaged by the employer to write and approve the written practice, approve procedures, and administer and grade examinations. The certification itself remains the employer's — you certify your own people. Our [outsourced ASNT Level III service](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) names a method-specific Level III who signs and attends the audit with you.

facets.q: What does Appendix VIII performance demonstration change about our UT procedure?
facets.a: Appendix VIII qualifies the whole examination system — procedure, equipment and personnel together — because the industry and the NRC doubted the reliability of inservice ultrasonic testing. Utilities funded the Performance Demonstration Initiative with EPRI to implement it. Your procedure must sit inside the qualified essential-variable envelope. Drift outside it on scan plan, frequency or wedge and the examination is not creditable.

facets.q: Which Charlotte employers are competing for the Level III we would otherwise hire?
facets.a: Duke Energy, EPRI's NDE Center on W.T. Harris Boulevard, Siemens Energy's Charlotte Energy Hub and Terrestrial Energy's new Tyvola Road headquarters all recruit from the same pool, alongside 240-plus energy organisations across the sixteen-county region. UNC Charlotte's EPIC graduates roughly 150 energy-discipline students a year against regional demand well above 400 new entrants.

sections.heading: Charlotte Is Four Audit Doors, Not One Customer
paragraphs: Duke Energy runs its regulated business from Charlotte, serving more than seven million customers and owning roughly 58,200 MW of generation. The nuclear share of that — six plants and eleven units — supplied more than half of Carolinas customers' electricity in 2024. Two of those plants are commuting distance from uptown: McGuire, seventeen miles northwest at Huntersville on Lake Norman, and Catawba, about thirty-five miles south at York, South Carolina. Oconee at Seneca, Robinson at Hartsville, Harris at New Hill and Brunswick at Southport are day trips.

Duke is only the first door. EPRI operates its Nondestructive Evaluation Center at 1300 West W.T. Harris Boulevard, a laboratory built to evaluate inspection systems and move research into plant use. Siemens Energy's Charlotte Energy Hub on Westinghouse Boulevard has been the company's worldwide base for 60 Hz power generating equipment since 1969 and sits inside a $421 million North Carolina expansion. Terrestrial Energy opened its US corporate headquarters on West Tyvola Road in September 2025 to build an American supply chain for its molten salt reactor.

That density is why the Charlotte region counts more than 240 energy organisations and over 26,000 energy employees across sixteen counties, and why UNC Charlotte's Energy Production and Infrastructure Center draws more than 250 participating energy corporations. For an inspection company the consequence is uncomfortable: four different buyers, four procurement organisations, and one shared expectation that you already hold a nuclear quality programme before you are permitted to quote at all.

sections.heading: The Regime: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, Implemented Through NQA-1
paragraphs: Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50 is the NRC's binding list of eighteen quality assurance criteria that every US nuclear plant must satisfy. ASME NQA-1 is the consensus standard that says how to implement them, and NRC Regulatory Guide 1.28, Revision 5, endorses it as an acceptable means of compliance. The eighteen NQA-1 requirements and the eighteen Appendix B criteria map to one another almost exactly, which is why a utility auditor moves between the two documents without pausing.

When a Charlotte inspection firm becomes a supplier of safety-related services, the utility must qualify it. The most rigorous method is an on-site audit of your facility, QA manual, procedures and records, and Regulatory Guide 1.28 points to a triennial cycle for supplier programme audits. NUPIC exists so that one audit serves many subscribing utilities. The efficiency is real, and so is the exposure — a single adverse finding reaches every subscriber at once.

The first document opened in that audit is almost always the written practice, because it is the one artefact that binds everything else together: the methods you claim, the levels you certify, the training hours, the examination structure and the Level III who signs. If it was downloaded, adapted from a previous employer or written for a scope you no longer perform, the audit turns into a document review you cannot win. Our [written practice development service](/consulting/written-practice-development) rebuilds it against your actual scope.

sections.heading: Section XI Runs on CP-189, and Firms Get This Backwards
paragraphs: ANSI/ASNT CP-189 was published in 1991 and taken into ASME Section XI in the mid-1990s — the only adoption of that standard by an industry sector and its governing code. IWA-2300 sets the qualification provisions for personnel performing nondestructive examination during inservice inspection, and paragraph IWA-2312(c) drives visual examination personnel to Appendix VI, which in turn reaches CP-189. The current edition of CP-189 is 2024.

Most inspection firms arrive with an SNT-TC-1A programme, because SNT-TC-1A is what governs fabrication, construction and virtually every non-nuclear code contract. That programme is not wrong; it is simply not sufficient for Section XI scope. A Charlotte firm doing McGuire outage work and Siemens Energy component examination in the same year needs both branches in one written practice, with the boundary between them stated explicitly so an auditor can see which examiner is certified under which standard on which job.

The Level III does three things here that no one else in the company can. They decide which method and level applies to each scope, they author or approve the general, specific and practical examinations, and they sign the certification. Where a firm needs an independent hand on the examination process itself, our [Level III examination oversight service](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) administers and grades to the written practice so the records survive scrutiny.

sections.heading: Appendix VIII, PDI, and Why the Charlotte Address Matters
paragraphs: Appendix VIII to ASME Section XI exists because the US nuclear industry and its regulator were not satisfied that inservice ultrasonic examination reliably found the flaws it was supposed to find. Rather than qualify procedures on paper, Appendix VIII qualifies the examination system by performance — the procedure, the equipment and the examiner demonstrated together on specimens with known flaws. Utilities funded the Performance Demonstration Initiative through EPRI and implemented it by the late 1990s.

Charlotte matters because EPRI's NDE Center is here. The laboratory on W.T. Harris Boulevard holds facilities for evaluating components and materials and for developing inspection, welding, fabrication and repair techniques. For a local firm that means the qualification infrastructure is not a flight away — but it also means the buyer next door knows exactly what a qualified technique looks like and will notice when yours is not one.

The practical failure mode is drift. A procedure is written inside a qualified envelope, then a scan plan changes, a wedge angle is substituted, a frequency moves, and the examination silently falls outside the essential variables it was qualified against. Indications reported from an unqualified technique are not creditable, and the finding lands on the firm rather than the utility. Our [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) work maps every essential variable back to the code and the qualification record.

sections.heading: Commercial Grade Dedication: When Your Service Becomes Safety-Related
paragraphs: Commercial grade dedication is the controlled process by which an item or service procured outside the nuclear quality supply chain is evaluated and accepted for safety-related use. NQA-1 Part II, Subpart 2.14 defines the process; EPRI TR-102260 is the industry guideline behind it; and 10 CFR Part 21 imposes the reporting obligation if a dedicated item is later found defective. Failure to dedicate properly is an Appendix B violation, not a paperwork observation.

Four acceptance methods are recognised: special tests and inspections, a commercial grade survey of the supplier's processes, source verification at the manufacturer before shipment, and acceptable supplier performance history. Every one of them turns on identifying the critical characteristics on which the safety function depends and then verifying them. For an NDE service the critical characteristics are rarely obvious — they include examiner qualification, calibration block traceability, technique parameters and reporting thresholds.

This is precisely where a Level III earns the engagement. Defining critical characteristics for an inspection service, and writing them so a utility engineer can accept them, is a technical judgement call that a quality manager without method-level depth cannot make defensibly. It is also the item most often flagged when a firm's first Appendix B audit goes badly, because the dedication records exist but do not tie to anything measurable.

sections.heading: The Level III of Record Problem for a Twenty-Person Charlotte Shop
paragraphs: The Charlotte labour market makes the staffing answer expensive. Duke Energy's workforce plan calls for 1,200 new skilled trades positions and 400 engineering roles by the end of 2026. UNC Charlotte's EPIC graduates roughly 150 students a year in relevant energy disciplines against regional demand for more than 400 new entrants. EPRI, Siemens Energy and Terrestrial Energy recruit from the same shortlist. A nuclear-experienced Level III in this metro is not a hire you win on salary alone.

An outsourced arrangement inverts the problem. A named, method-specific Level III becomes your Level III of record: they author or approve the written practice, approve procedures and technique sheets, administer and grade certification examinations, and sit on your side of the table when the auditor arrives. You carry the certification authority as the employer, which is what SNT-TC-1A contemplates, without carrying a full-time salary against utilisation you cannot yet guarantee.

The scenario that generates most of the urgent calls is a resignation. A firm with an audit scheduled and no Level III has no one who can approve a procedure or sign a certification, and every certification issued after that date is exposed. If that is where you are, [what to do when your NDT Level III resigns](/consulting/ndt-level-3-resigned-what-to-do) sets out the sequence for keeping the programme valid while cover is established.

sections.heading: What the Same Written Practice Has to Cover Between Outages
paragraphs: No inspection firm survives on refuelling outages alone. Between them the crews work Siemens Energy component scope on Westinghouse Boulevard, Duke's gas and hydro fleet, transmission structures, and the general fabrication base that a metro of this size supports. That work runs on ASME Section V for methods, Section VIII and B31.1 for pressure boundary, and AWS D1.1 for structural welds — all of it certified through an SNT-TC-1A written practice rather than CP-189.

One written practice has to carry both. The document needs a method-by-level matrix, a clear statement of which sector standard governs which scope, training and experience hours for each combination, and named examination arrangements. Auditors do not object to a firm holding two branches. They object to a firm that cannot show, for a given examiner on a given job, which branch applied and what evidence supports it. Our [energy and utilities NDT consulting](/consulting/energy-utilities-ndt-consulting) work builds that structure once so it covers the full order book.

If the same shop also chases aerospace or defence work, a third door opens: Nadcap accreditation under AC7114, which audits the NDT process itself rather than the corporate quality system and which imposes its own responsible Level III expectations. That is a separate readiness programme — see [Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness](/consulting/nadcap-ac7114-audit-readiness) — but it should be scoped at the same time so the written practice is authored once rather than three times.

sections.heading: The Eight Weeks Before Your Audit Date
paragraphs: A workable sequence starts with a gap assessment against the specific regime the customer named — Appendix B, NQA-1, Section XI, or a Nadcap supplement — because the corrective actions differ sharply. Week one produces a findings list ranked by what an auditor opens first. Weeks two and three rebuild the written practice against actual scope and get it signed. Weeks four and five rebuild procedures and technique sheets with code citation and essential variables traceable.

Weeks six and seven close the personnel file gap: training hours, examination records, vision tests, practical demonstrations, and certification letters that match what the written practice promised. Commercial grade dedication records and 10 CFR 21 procedures are drafted in parallel. The final week is a mock audit run by the Level III who signed the documents, which is the only rehearsal that tests whether the programme holds together under questioning rather than on paper.

The same architecture, with different buyers and different code emphasis, applies in the other US nuclear metros — see our pages on [nuclear NDT consulting in Pittsburgh](/consulting/nuclear-ndt-consulting-pittsburgh) and [power generation NDT consulting in Chattanooga](/consulting/power-generation-ndt-consulting-chattanooga). Atlantis works remotely and on site across all three, and support is affordable, accessible and fully customisable to your scope. Tell us the audit date and the customer, and we will scope it from there — [request a quote or a demo](/contact).

faq.q: How long does it take to get an inspection firm ready for a NUPIC or Duke Energy supplier audit?
faq.a: Eight weeks is a realistic floor if the firm already performs the work competently and the gap is documentary. The long poles are the written practice signature, procedure rewrites with traceable essential variables, and personnel files that have to be reconstructed rather than corrected. Firms starting with no Appendix B programme at all should plan on a longer runway, because commercial grade dedication and 10 CFR 21 procedures have to be written from scratch.

faq.q: Do we need CP-189 certification for every technician or only for Section XI scope?
faq.a: Only for the scope the code demands it. ASME Section XI IWA-2300 governs personnel performing inservice examination, so examiners on McGuire or Catawba outage scope fall under CP-189. Technicians working Siemens Energy component fabrication, Duke's gas fleet or general shop work remain under your SNT-TC-1A written practice. The written practice must state the boundary explicitly so an auditor can trace any examiner to the right standard.

faq.q: Can Atlantis act as our Level III of record for nuclear work in Charlotte?
faq.a: Yes. A named, method-specific ASNT Level III signs as your responsible Level III for written practice approval, procedure and technique approval, certification examination administration, and audit defence. Cover is available across UT including phased array and TOFD, RT including digital and computed radiography, MT, PT, VT and ET. Engagements are structured against your actual scope rather than a fixed package.

faq.q: What is the difference between the NRC regulating Duke and the NRC regulating us?
faq.a: The NRC does not licence your inspection company. It licences Duke Energy, and Region II in Atlanta oversees the Carolinas plants. Your obligations reach you through the licensee's Appendix B programme as contractual flow-down, plus 10 CFR Part 21, which applies directly to suppliers of basic components. That is why the audit comes from the utility or NUPIC rather than from a federal inspector.

faq.q: We already hold ISO 9001 and ISO 17020. What still has to be built?
faq.a: Design control, commercial grade dedication under NQA-1 Part II Subpart 2.14, a 10 CFR Part 21 evaluation and reporting procedure, and CP-189-compliant personnel records for Section XI scope. Document control, corrective action, internal audit and records retention largely carry over with mapping. The efficient route is a crosswalk that reuses what the existing certificates already prove and builds only the delta.

facets.q: Does our 10 CFR 50 Appendix B programme cover naval nuclear work at Cheswick or Bettis?
facets.a: No. Naval Reactors and NAVSEA impose their own nondestructive testing requirements through the contract, outside the NRC framework entirely. An ASNT Level II certificate does not, on its own, constitute acceptance for naval scope. The customer's requirement documents govern personnel qualification, procedure approval and record handling, and your written practice needs a distinct branch that points at them.

facets.q: Why is Beaver Valley audited differently from Westinghouse?
facets.a: Beaver Valley is an operating licensee, so its examination scope is inservice inspection under ASME Section XI, with personnel qualified to ANSI/ASNT CP-189 through IWA-2300 and ultrasonic systems performance-demonstrated under Appendix VIII. Westinghouse is a component supplier and new-build vendor, so its scope is largely ASME Section III and Section V with SNT-TC-1A employer certification flowed down through NQA-1.

facets.q: Can one written practice really cover nuclear, naval and pipeline work?
facets.a: Yes, and it is cheaper and more defensible than three. The document needs a method-by-level matrix, an explicit sector column, and annexes that state which customer requirement applies to which scope. Auditors accept multiple branches. They reject a document that cannot show, for one named examiner on one named job, which branch applied and what evidence supports it.

facets.q: What does 49 CFR Part 192 require of the NDT contractor on Marcellus gathering and transmission lines?
facets.a: Part 192 sets minimum federal safety standards for gas pipelines and reaches nondestructive examination through welding and inspection requirements, typically implemented via API 1104 and the operator's own specification. The practical exposure for a contractor is records: qualified interpreters, retained radiographs or digital images, and a traceable link from each weld number to the examiner who accepted it.

facets.q: Is Pittsburgh under NRC Region I or Region II?
facets.a: Region I, whose office is at King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, covers the northeastern states including Pennsylvania — so Beaver Valley oversight sits there. Region II in Atlanta covers the southeast. The distinction rarely touches a supplier directly, because the NRC does not licence inspection companies; obligations reach you through the licensee's Appendix B flow-down and through 10 CFR Part 21.

facets.q: How much work is there outside nuclear if the outage schedule slips?
facets.a: Substantial. US Steel's Mon Valley Works is spending up to $2.5 billion including a new hot strip mill at Edgar Thomson in Braddock, Shell's Potter Township complex produces 1.6 million tonnes of polyethylene a year, EQT is the largest Appalachian Basin gas producer, and Elliott Group employs around 900 people building turbomachinery at Jeannette.

sections.heading: Three Nuclear Economies Share One Pittsburgh Labour Pool
paragraphs: Westinghouse Electric runs its global headquarters at 1000 Westinghouse Drive in Cranberry Township, Butler County — the design authority behind the AP1000 and, more recently, the AP300 small modular reactor and the APX platform, which in August 2026 drew supporting agreements with Amentum for fleet-scale deployment. Whatever happens to the US nuclear build rate is decided, in engineering terms, about twenty miles north of downtown Pittsburgh.

Curtiss-Wright's Electro-Mechanical Systems campus at Cheswick, in Allegheny County, has occupied the same 118 acres since 1952, building canned motor pumps, motors, generators, control rod drive mechanisms and ship propulsion equipment. The site traces its commercial nuclear lineage to Shippingport and its naval lineage to USS Nautilus, and it is currently adding roughly 150 jobs under an $80 million multi-year expansion on top of more than 860 existing positions.

Bettis Atomic Power Laboratory sits at West Mifflin, founded in 1949 and working exclusively on nuclear propulsion for the US Navy as part of the Naval Nuclear Laboratory, operated by Fluor Marine Propulsion under NNSA's Naval Reactors office. Twenty-seven miles northwest, Vistra's Beaver Valley Power Station runs two Westinghouse pressurised water reactors at Shippingport in Beaver County, commissioned in 1976 and 1987, and has since committed capacity under a twenty-year agreement supporting Meta's operations.

sections.heading: The Commercial Nuclear Branch: Appendix B and NQA-1
paragraphs: Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50 sets eighteen quality assurance criteria that bind every US nuclear licensee. ASME NQA-1 is the consensus standard the NRC endorses, through Regulatory Guide 1.28 Revision 5, as an acceptable way of implementing them. Westinghouse and Vistra both flow that architecture down to subcontractors. Suppliers are qualified by on-site audit of the facility, QA manual, procedures and records, on a cycle Regulatory Guide 1.28 places at three years.

Being qualified for one scope does not qualify a firm for another. A supplier approved to provide one type of safety-related service is not automatically approved for a different one, which is the trap for an inspection company that wins a magnetic particle scope and then quotes phased array ultrasonics on the assumption the approval travels. The written practice, the procedures and the personnel records must all extend to the new method before the purchase order is accepted.

At Beaver Valley the scope is inservice inspection, and that changes the personnel standard. ASME Section XI IWA-2300 governs qualification of examination personnel, reaching ANSI/ASNT CP-189 — the standard incorporated into Section XI in the mid-1990s. Ultrasonic examination of piping welds additionally falls under Appendix VIII performance demonstration, implemented by the utilities and EPRI through the Performance Demonstration Initiative. Our [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) work ties every essential variable back to that qualification.

sections.heading: Naval Nuclear Is a Different Rulebook Entirely
paragraphs: The most expensive assumption a Pittsburgh inspection firm can make is that a working commercial nuclear programme transfers to naval scope. It does not. Naval Reactors and NAVSEA impose their own nondestructive testing requirements through the contract, outside the NRC framework, and they specify personnel qualification, procedure approval routes and record handling in terms that an ASNT certificate does not satisfy by itself.

In practice that means a second branch inside your quality system rather than a footnote. Procedures are written to the customer's requirement documents, not to ASME Section V alone. Personnel qualification records have to demonstrate what the customer asked for, in the form the customer asked for. Controlled document handling, marking and destruction, and site access constraints at facilities like Bettis are programme requirements, not administrative preferences, and auditors treat sloppiness there as a systemic failure.

This is where an outsourced Level III is most useful and where the limits of the role need stating plainly. The Level III can author and approve the technical content, administer examinations and defend the programme in audit. They cannot become the responsible party for customer contract compliance or hold clearances on your behalf. Our page on [what an outside NDT Level III can and cannot do](/consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do) draws that boundary before an engagement starts.

sections.heading: The Third Economy: Marcellus Gas and Beaver County Petrochemicals
paragraphs: EQT Corporation runs the largest natural gas production business in the Appalachian Basin from EQT Plaza in downtown Pittsburgh, and its July 2024 acquisition of Canonsburg-based Equitrans Midstream folded a major gathering, transmission and storage network — including an interest in the 303-mile Mountain Valley Pipeline — back into the same company. That is a standing volume of weld inspection, in-service examination and integrity work inside a ninety-minute radius.

The regime is federal but it is not the NRC. Gas transmission and gathering fall under 49 CFR Part 192, implemented in practice through API 1104 for welding and inspection and ASME B31.8 for the piping itself, layered with each operator's own specification. Exposure for a contractor is concentrated in records: qualified radiographic interpreters, retained images, and an unbroken trace from weld number to accepting examiner. Our [oil and gas NDT consulting](/consulting/oil-gas-ndt-consulting) work builds that record architecture.

Twenty-five miles northwest, Shell's Pennsylvania Petrochemicals Complex occupies 386 acres at Potter Township in Beaver County, producing 1.6 million tonnes of polyethylene a year since operations began in November 2022 after roughly $14 billion of construction. Turnaround scope there runs on ASME B31.3 and owner specification. The failure mode is mobilisation speed — crews arrive faster than their certification records can be verified, and the contractor is stood down at the gate.

sections.heading: Mon Valley Steel and Turbomachinery: Where the Volume Is
paragraphs: US Steel's Mon Valley Works is three plants strung along the river: coke at Clairton, steelmaking at Edgar Thomson in Braddock, and finishing at Irvin in West Mifflin. Under Nippon Steel ownership the complex is receiving up to $2.5 billion, centred on a new hot strip mill at Edgar Thomson that will replace an 87-year-old facility at Irvin and lift capacity from about 2.2 million to 3.5 million tons of sheet steel, preserving roughly 3,000 jobs.

A capital project of that size is a structural and pressure inspection programme in its own right — AWS D1.1 on structural steel, ASME Section VIII on vessels, owner specification on everything else, and a construction schedule that punishes any contractor whose examiner records are not audit-clean on day one. It is also the most reliable non-nuclear revenue in the metro for a firm whose nuclear work is outage-cyclical.

Elliott Group adds a different flavour of the same requirement. The Jeannette plant in Westmoreland County employs around 900 people building steam turbines, centrifugal compressors, power recovery turbines and control systems as part of Ebara. Rotating equipment inspection — rotor bore examination, blade root inspection, weld overlay evaluation — demands technique depth that a general written practice rarely covers, and the customer will ask which Level III approved the technique.

sections.heading: One Written Practice, Not Three Programmes
paragraphs: The instinct when three regimes collide is to run three quality systems. It is the wrong answer: three systems mean three sets of personnel records, three corrective action logs, three revision cycles, and a guarantee that one of them is out of date when an auditor asks. The right answer is one written practice with an explicit sector structure and customer-specific annexes that reference the governing document for each branch.

Structurally, that means a method-by-level matrix covering UT including phased array and TOFD, RT including digital and computed radiography, MT, PT, VT and ET; a sector column naming the applicable standard — CP-189 for Section XI, SNT-TC-1A for construction and industrial scope, customer requirement documents for naval; training and experience hours for each combination; and named examination arrangements. Our [written practice development service](/consulting/written-practice-development) builds it in that shape.

The test an auditor applies is simple and firms consistently fail it. Take one named examiner, one named job, one named weld. Show which standard governed the examiner's certification, which procedure applied, what revision was current on that date, who approved it, and what training and examination record supports the level claimed. If the answer requires cross-referencing three binders and a spreadsheet, the finding is written before the question finishes.

sections.heading: Who Signs, and What Happens When They Leave
paragraphs: Every branch of that written practice needs a signature from someone qualified to give it. SNT-TC-1A contemplates an outside Level III engaged by the employer to write and approve the written practice, approve procedures and technique sheets, and administer, grade and record certification examinations. The certification itself remains yours — you certify your own people — which is exactly the arrangement Westinghouse's and Vistra's supply chains are accustomed to seeing.

In a metro where Westinghouse, Curtiss-Wright, Bettis and Beaver Valley all recruit method-qualified people, keeping a Level III on payroll against uneven utilisation is a hard commercial case for a firm under fifty heads. An outsourced arrangement carries the same signature authority without the fixed cost, and it scales method by method as scope grows. Our [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) names the individual who signs for each method.

Naval and marine propulsion scope has one further wrinkle worth planning for: the technique library that serves shipboard and submarine components overlaps heavily with commercial marine survey work, which is why firms in this market often carry both. Our [maritime NDT consulting](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting) page covers that side. Where the fleet nuclear work and the commercial marine work share examiners, the written practice must keep the certification records separable.

sections.heading: Sequencing an Audit-Readiness Programme in Pittsburgh
paragraphs: Start by naming the customer and the regime, because the corrective actions diverge immediately. A Westinghouse purchase order and a Beaver Valley outage contract are both nuclear and require almost nothing in common at the personnel-standard level. A Cheswick naval subcontract shares even less. Scoping this correctly in week one saves the four weeks that firms routinely lose rewriting a written practice against the wrong standard.

From there the sequence is stable: gap assessment against the named regime; written practice rebuild and signature; procedure and technique sheet rebuild with traceable code citation and essential variables; personnel file reconstruction covering training hours, examinations, vision tests and practical demonstrations; commercial grade dedication and 10 CFR 21 procedures where safety-related scope is involved; then a mock audit run by the Level III who signed the documents.

Atlantis works remotely and on site across the Pittsburgh market, and support is affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the scope you actually hold. The same structure applied to a different buyer mix is set out in our [Charlotte nuclear NDT consulting](/consulting/nuclear-ndt-consulting-charlotte) page, where Duke Energy and EPRI dominate instead. Tell us the customer, the methods and the audit date, and we will scope it — [request a quote or a demo](/contact).

faq.q: We supply Westinghouse today and want to add Beaver Valley outage work. What has to change?
faq.a: The personnel standard changes first. Westinghouse component scope runs on ASME Section III and Section V with SNT-TC-1A employer certification; Beaver Valley inservice inspection runs on ASME Section XI IWA-2300 with ANSI/ASNT CP-189 qualification, and ultrasonic examination of piping welds additionally requires Appendix VIII performance demonstration. That means a new branch in the written practice, new procedures written inside the qualified envelope, and new certification records for the examiners you intend to deploy.

faq.q: Do naval nuclear customers accept an ASNT Level III signature on our procedures?
faq.a: Only where the contract says so. Naval Reactors and NAVSEA impose their own requirement documents, and personnel qualification, procedure approval and record handling follow those documents rather than SNT-TC-1A by default. A qualified Level III still adds the technical authorship and defensibility, but the acceptance route must be read out of the customer's own requirements before any procedure is issued.

faq.q: How often will we be audited once we are on an approved supplier list?
faq.a: Regulatory Guide 1.28 points to a triennial cycle for supplier quality programme audits, and NUPIC-style joint audits are structured around that rhythm so one audit serves multiple subscribing utilities. Re-evaluation also triggers on ownership change, key personnel departure, facility relocation or process change. A Level III resignation is one of those triggers, which is why cover matters more than the calendar.

faq.q: Is a Level III needed for Marcellus pipeline work, or only for nuclear?
faq.a: Needed for both, for different reasons. Nuclear customers audit the Level III signature directly. Pipeline operators working under 49 CFR Part 192 and API 1104 rely on the contractor's own written practice for interpreter qualification, and that written practice is only valid if a Level III authored or approved it. The scrutiny is lighter until an integrity incident, at which point the records are examined as closely as any nuclear audit.

faq.q: Can Atlantis attend the audit with us rather than just writing the documents?
faq.a: Yes. The named Level III sits on your side of the table for pre-audit gap closure, on-site attendance and corrective action close-out. Defending a procedure in the room is a different exercise from writing one, and firms that outsource only the authorship routinely lose findings they could have answered. Engagements are structured around your audit date and scope.

facets.q: Does TVA use NQA-1, and which edition?
facets.a: Yes. TVA's Fleet Nuclear Quality Assurance Plan is the quality assurance programme description controlling activities affecting safety-related structures, systems and components, and it is built on the requirements and guidance of ASME NQA-1-2015, Parts I and II. That is what a supplier's own programme is measured against during qualification, alongside 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and 10 CFR Part 21.

facets.q: Can our nuclear-qualified crew work Raccoon Mountain without extra paperwork?
facets.a: They can work it, but not on the same certification record. Hydro examination sits outside the NRC framework entirely — TVA's dam safety programme and contract specification govern, with ASME Section V methods and AWS D1.1 for structural welds, certified through an SNT-TC-1A written practice. The written practice must keep the two branches separable so an auditor can trace any examiner to the right standard.

facets.q: What makes Watts Bar different from Sequoyah for an inspection contractor?
facets.a: Watts Bar Unit 2 entered commercial operation in October 2016, making it the first US reactor to do so since Unit 1 in 1996, so the plant carries a mix of new and mature systems. It also holds NRC authorisation to irradiate tritium-producing burnable absorber rods for the National Nuclear Security Administration, which adds access, scheduling and record controls that Sequoyah scope does not impose.

facets.q: Why does Browns Ferry need different procedures if it is the same utility?
facets.a: Because it is a boiling water reactor fleet — three General Electric BWR-4 units with Mark I containment, totalling around 3,775 MWe near Athens, Alabama. Component geometry, material and access differ from Sequoyah's Westinghouse pressurised water reactors with ice condenser containment. Browns Ferry also carries the Appendix R fire protection legacy that followed the 1975 cable fire, which shapes examination scope on cable and barrier systems.

facets.q: How does the Clinch River SMR project change what suppliers need?
facets.a: It shifts the work from Section XI inservice inspection to Section III construction examination. TVA has filed the first US construction permit application for a GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 at Oak Ridge, supported by a $400 million Department of Energy award in December 2025. New build means SNT-TC-1A employer certification, heavy commercial grade dedication under NQA-1 Part II Subpart 2.14, and construction NDE procedures rather than ISI.

facets.q: Is there still turbine inspection expertise in Chattanooga after Alstom closed?
facets.a: Yes, and it is a real local asset. The Riverfront Parkway plant opened in June 2010 on roughly $300 million of investment, held the world's largest rotor balancing facility, and built Arabelle nuclear steam turbines before GE announced closure of the operations in June 2016. The rotor, blade and generator examination skills built there stayed in the metro and remain hirable.

sections.heading: One Utility, Four Rulebooks: The Chattanooga Vendor's Problem
paragraphs: TVA is the largest public utility in the United States and its sixth-largest power supplier, delivering electricity to roughly ten million people across all of Tennessee and parts of Alabama, Mississippi, Kentucky, Georgia, North Carolina and Virginia. Its corporate headquarters is in Knoxville, but Chattanooga carries the nuclear organisation — TVA's licensing correspondence to the NRC goes out on 1101 Market Street letterhead, and the Nuclear Fleet Center sits in the city.

The generating fleet behind that is unusually mixed for a single buyer: twenty-nine hydroelectric dams, four coal plants, seven nuclear units across three sites, nine simple-cycle gas turbine plants, nine combined-cycle plants, one pumped-storage station, a wind site and fourteen solar sites. A Chattanooga inspection company with the right crew can bid across all of it without leaving the service area, which is a commercial advantage almost no other US metro offers.

It is also the specific reason those firms fail supplier qualification. The same technician, doing the same ultrasonic examination, is governed by ASME Section XI and ANSI/ASNT CP-189 at Sequoyah on Monday and by TVA specification and an SNT-TC-1A written practice at Chickamauga Dam on Thursday. If the quality system cannot show which standard applied to which job, the audit finding is written against the whole programme, not against one record.

sections.heading: The Nuclear Door: Sequoyah, Watts Bar and Browns Ferry
paragraphs: Sequoyah is the closest — seven miles east of Soddy-Daisy and twenty miles north of Chattanooga in Hamilton County. Two Westinghouse pressurised water reactors with ice condenser containment produce about 2,440 MW winter net dependable capacity. Unit 1 entered commercial operation in July 1981 and Unit 2 in June 1982, and the plant holds the distinction of being the first new nuclear station licensed after Three Mile Island. Licences renewed in 2015 run to 2040 and 2041.

Watts Bar sits in Rhea County near Spring City. Unit 1 entered commercial operation in May 1996; Unit 2 followed on 19 October 2016, making it the first US reactor to enter commercial operation since Unit 1, ahead of Vogtle 3 and 4. The site also holds NRC authorisation, granted by licence amendment in 2002, to irradiate tritium-producing burnable absorber rods for the National Nuclear Security Administration — scope that carries its own access, scheduling and record controls.

Browns Ferry, near Athens and Decatur in Limestone County, Alabama, runs three General Electric BWR-4 units with Mark I containment totalling roughly 3,775 MWe, with licences renewed in 2006 running to 2033, 2034 and 2036. It is also the plant where a 1975 fire, started by a worker using a candle to check air leaks, damaged reactor control cabling and led directly to the NRC's Appendix R fire protection requirements now imposed across the industry.

sections.heading: TVA's Fleet Plan Is NQA-1-2015, Parts I and II
paragraphs: TVA's Fleet Nuclear Quality Assurance Plan is the quality assurance programme description that controls activities affecting the quality of safety-related structures, systems and components. It is built on the requirements and guidance of ASME NQA-1-2015, Parts I and II. That is not a detail for the licensing team — it is the document a supplier's own programme is compared against when TVA or a joint utility audit qualifies you.

Qualification methods available to the buyer include an on-site survey of your facility, manual, procedures and records; source inspection during fabrication; documented performance history; acceptance of third-party accreditation; and commercial grade dedication. The on-site audit is the most rigorous and is the default for safety-significant scope. NRC Regulatory Guide 1.28, Revision 5, points to a triennial cycle for supplier quality programme audits, and re-evaluation triggers on ownership change, facility relocation or key personnel departure.

Approval is scope-bound. A supplier qualified to provide one type of safety-related service is not automatically qualified for a different one. Firms lose money here routinely, quoting a method the approval does not cover and discovering it after the purchase order is issued. Our [written practice development service](/consulting/written-practice-development) sets the method-by-level matrix so the approved scope and the quoted scope are the same document.

sections.heading: Section XI Personnel: CP-189, Appendix VI and Appendix VIII
paragraphs: Inservice examination personnel at all three TVA nuclear sites are qualified under ASME Section XI IWA-2300, which reaches ANSI/ASNT CP-189 — the standard published in 1991 and incorporated into Section XI in the mid-1990s, the only sector adoption of it. Paragraph IWA-2312(c) drives VT-1, VT-2 and VT-3 visual examination personnel to Appendix VI and from there to CP-189. The current edition of CP-189 is 2024.

Ultrasonic examination of piping welds carries an additional layer. Appendix VIII to Section XI was developed because the industry and its regulators doubted the reliability of inservice ultrasonic inspection, so the whole examination system — procedure, equipment and examiner — is qualified by demonstration on specimens with known flaws. US utilities funded and implemented that through the EPRI-supported Performance Demonstration Initiative by the late 1990s.

The consequence for a procedure author is that the essential-variable envelope is not negotiable. Change the scan plan, the transducer frequency, the wedge or the coverage assumption, and the examination no longer sits inside what was qualified. Our [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) work ties each variable back to the qualification record and the code paragraph, and [Level III examination oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) keeps the personnel side matching.

sections.heading: The Hydro Door: Raccoon Mountain, Chickamauga and Twenty-Nine Dams
paragraphs: Raccoon Mountain is TVA's only pumped-storage plant and sits on the ridge above Nickajack Reservoir west of downtown Chattanooga. Four units give it 1,700 MW of summer net dependable capacity, and the upper reservoir takes about twenty-eight hours to fill when the units run in pump mode. It generates roughly fourteen times the output of nearby Chickamauga Dam, whose four units contribute 142 MW inside the city itself.

No NRC requirement touches any of it. TVA is a federal agency, its dams are federally owned, and the examination requirements come from TVA's own dam safety programme and from contract specification. Method work is performed to ASME Section V, structural welds to AWS D1.1, and personnel are certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. The technical content is demanding in a different way — penstock weld ultrasonics, spiral case and scroll case examination, turbine runner and shaft inspection, gate and headcover fastener evaluation.

What catches firms out is the operational envelope rather than the code. Penstock and draft tube access is confined-space work on a dewatering window that cannot slip, often with rope access, and the procedure has to be written for those conditions rather than adapted from a shop document. The written practice must carry a hydro branch with its own technique sheets, and our [energy and utilities NDT consulting](/consulting/energy-utilities-ndt-consulting) work builds that alongside the nuclear branch rather than after it.

sections.heading: The Fossil and Gas Door, and the Skills Chattanooga Already Has
paragraphs: TVA's four remaining coal plants and eighteen gas turbine and combined-cycle stations generate a steady non-outage workload: boiler tube examination on waterwalls, superheaters and reheaters; heat recovery steam generator and header inspection; and steam and feedwater piping to ASME B31.1. Vessels fall under Section VIII. None of it requires CP-189, all of it requires an SNT-TC-1A written practice that actually names the methods and the sector.

The metro has a deeper turbine skills base than its current employer list suggests. Alstom opened a turbine manufacturing plant at 1119 and 1201 Riverfront Parkway in June 2010 on roughly $300 million of investment, with an on-site barge dock rated to 1,000 tons and what was then the world's largest rotor balancing facility. It built the Arabelle nuclear steam turbine there. GE acquired Alstom's power business in a $10.6 billion transaction and announced closure of the Chattanooga operations in June 2016.

Those people did not all leave. Rotor bore examination, blade root inspection, generator retaining ring evaluation and weld overlay assessment are techniques a Chattanooga firm can staff locally and that TVA's own fleet needs on a rolling basis. The gap is almost never capability. It is a written practice that never got extended to cover the techniques the crew can already perform, so the firm cannot legitimately quote them.

sections.heading: Clinch River and What New Build Changes
paragraphs: TVA has submitted a construction permit application to the NRC for a GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at the Clinch River site in Oak Ridge — the first construction permit application for that design in the United States. The Department of Energy awarded TVA $400 million in December 2025 toward advanced light-water SMR deployment, on top of TVA's own funding lines carrying planning, design and regulatory work through fiscal year 2026.

For an inspection supplier this is a different business from outage work. Construction examination falls under ASME Section III with Section V methods, personnel are certified through an SNT-TC-1A written practice rather than CP-189, and the volume is front-loaded rather than cyclical. It also makes commercial grade dedication central: NQA-1 Part II Subpart 2.14 and EPRI TR-102260 govern the process, and 10 CFR Part 21 imposes the reporting obligation if a dedicated item later proves defective.

Firms that want that scope should build the dedication capability now rather than when the purchase orders appear. Defining critical characteristics for an examination service — examiner qualification, calibration block traceability, technique parameters, reporting thresholds — is a Level III judgement that a quality manager cannot make defensibly alone. It is consistently the item flagged when a supplier's first NQA-1 audit goes badly, because dedication records exist but tie to nothing measurable.

sections.heading: Getting a Chattanooga Firm Through TVA Supplier Qualification
paragraphs: The efficient sequence starts by naming every TVA asset class you intend to bid, because that decides how many branches the written practice needs. A firm chasing Sequoyah and Watts Bar inservice work plus Raccoon Mountain penstock scope plus combined-cycle header inspection needs three, structured in one document with an explicit sector column so any examiner on any job traces to one governing standard.

From there: gap assessment against NQA-1-2015 Parts I and II and 10 CFR 50 Appendix B; written practice rebuild and Level III signature; procedure and technique sheet rebuild with traceable code citation and essential variables; personnel file reconstruction covering training hours, examinations, vision tests and practical demonstrations; commercial grade dedication and 10 CFR Part 21 procedures for safety-related scope; then a mock audit run by the Level III who signed. Where technicians need to be brought up to level, [corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) runs against your own written practice rather than a generic syllabus.

Atlantis provides a named, method-specific [outsourced ASNT Level III](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) who signs, administers examinations and attends the audit with you — affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the asset classes you actually bid. The same architecture applied to different utilities is set out in our [Charlotte nuclear NDT consulting](/consulting/nuclear-ndt-consulting-charlotte) and [Pittsburgh nuclear NDT consulting](/consulting/nuclear-ndt-consulting-pittsburgh) pages. Tell us the scope and the date — [request a quote or a demo](/contact).

faq.q: Do we need a separate quality programme for TVA hydro work and TVA nuclear work?
faq.a: No — one programme with two clearly separated branches. Nuclear scope is governed by 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, TVA's Fleet NQAP built on ASME NQA-1-2015 Parts I and II, and ASME Section XI with CP-189 personnel. Hydro scope is governed by TVA's dam safety programme and contract specification with SNT-TC-1A certification. Running two full systems doubles the records and guarantees one is stale at audit.

faq.q: How far are the TVA nuclear plants from Chattanooga?
faq.a: Sequoyah is the closest, seven miles east of Soddy-Daisy and about twenty miles north of the city in Hamilton County. Watts Bar is near Spring City in Rhea County, between Chattanooga and Knoxville. Browns Ferry is near Athens and Decatur in Limestone County, Alabama. Raccoon Mountain and Chickamauga Dam are inside the metro, which makes a Chattanooga base unusually efficient for a fleet-wide inspection contract.

faq.q: Does TVA accept ISO 9001 or ISO 17020 in place of an NQA-1 programme?
faq.a: Not for safety-related nuclear scope. Those certificates cover management system and inspection body competence and carry over usefully on document control, records and corrective action, but they do not address design control, commercial grade dedication under NQA-1 Part II Subpart 2.14, or 10 CFR Part 21 reporting. The efficient route is a crosswalk that reuses what the certificates prove and builds only the missing elements.

faq.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign our written practice for TVA work?
faq.a: Yes. SNT-TC-1A contemplates an outside Level III engaged by the employer to author and approve the written practice, approve procedures and technique sheets, and administer, grade and record certification examinations. Certification authority stays with you as the employer. For Section XI scope the Level III must also hold qualification consistent with ANSI/ASNT CP-189 as invoked through IWA-2300.

faq.q: What does Appendix VIII qualification mean for our ultrasonic procedures at Sequoyah?
faq.a: It means the procedure, equipment and examiner are qualified as one system by demonstration on specimens with known flaws, through the EPRI-supported Performance Demonstration Initiative, rather than by document review. Your written procedure must sit inside the qualified essential-variable envelope. Substituting a wedge, changing frequency or altering the scan plan takes the examination outside that envelope and the results are not creditable.

faq.q: We only want the fossil, gas and hydro work — is a Level III still required?
faq.a: Yes. Every SNT-TC-1A written practice requires a Level III to author or approve it, approve procedures, and administer certification examinations, regardless of whether nuclear scope is involved. TVA specification work at Chickamauga, Raccoon Mountain or a combined-cycle station relies on that written practice being valid. Without a signing Level III, every certification issued is exposed the moment a contract audit opens the file.

title: Jacksonville NDT: One Written Practice Cannot Cover Mayport and Class
description: Jacksonville yards work Mayport warships under NAVSEA T9074-271 and classed tonnage under IACS rules. How an outsourced ASNT Level III covers both regimes.
h1: Outsourced ASNT Level III Support for Jacksonville Shipyards, Terminals and Marine Fabricators
answer: Jacksonville inspection firms serve two incompatible regimes at once. Mayport availabilities invoke NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which turns SNT-TC-1A into mandatory minimums and bars recertification by continued performance. Class work on Crowley and TOTE tonnage runs under IACS Z17 and W35. An outsourced ASNT Level III writes both written practices, qualifies the procedures, and administers the examinations.
expansion: Jacksonville is unusual among US maritime metros because one inspection crew often works both sides of the fence inside a single week. BAE Systems Jacksonville Ship Repair runs a 25,000-ton shiplift, marine railways rated at 4,000 and 1,000 tons, and 1,630 feet of pier, and takes everything from Mayport destroyers to tankers and megayachts. Naval Station Mayport homeports Arleigh Burke destroyers and Freedom-variant littoral combat ships. Across the St. Johns, JAXPORT's Blount Island, Talleyrand and Dames Point terminals carry Crowley's and TOTE's LNG-fuelled Puerto Rico trades. Warship work is governed by NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271. Classed commercial tonnage is governed by IACS Unified Requirements Z17 and W35. The two regimes disagree on who may certify a technician, how often, and on what evidence. A firm running one written practice against both will fail an audit on one side.
source: Verified against NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Revision 1 (11 September 2014), Chapter 1 sections 1.5 through 1.8; NAVSEA Standard Item 009-04; IACS UR Z17 Rev.21 (2025), sections 4 to 8 and Annex 1; IACS UR W35 Rev.1 (October 2023, uniformly implemented from 1 January 2025), sections 1.1 to 2.9; BAE Systems' published Jacksonville Ship Repair facility specifications; JAXPORT terminal data for Blount Island, Talleyrand and Dames Point; USNI News fleet tracker entries for Mayport-homeported hulls; NAVSEA Master Ship Repair Agreement application guidance.
