A Z17 certificate does not qualify a Seattle firm for the Bering Sea fleet, and fleet work builds nothing toward one.

facets.q: Does an outsourced Level III satisfy NAVSEA Tech Pub 271 at a Puget Sound yard?
facets.a: Paragraph 1.5.5 defines the Examiner as the individual to whom the activity delegates authority to examine and certify NDT personnel and to approve procedures and workmanship standards. It does not require that person to sit on the payroll. The activity remains responsible for the adequacy of its own programme under paragraph 1.6.3, so the delegation belongs in the written practice, in writing.

facets.q: Can a Seattle firm reuse NDT procedures it already ran at another shipyard?
facets.a: No. Paragraph 1.7.4 states procedures shall not be transferred from one activity to another without the specific approval of NAVSEA. Paragraph 1.6.9 sets the same bar on people: transfer of NDT certifications to other activities is prohibited except as authorized by NAVSEA. A new yard, a new subsidiary or a new legal entity starts from a fresh written practice.

facets.q: When is the worst time to start a Puget Sound qualification project?
facets.a: November. Bering Sea pollock A season opened 20 January in 2026 and runs to mid-April, so the catcher-processor fleet crowds Lake Union Dry Dock, Pacific Fishermen, Everett Ship Repair and Vigor from late autumn until the boats sail. Practical examinations, procedure demonstrations and technical performance evaluations then compete with production for the same senior technicians.

facets.q: Do Washington State Ferries dry-dockings require ASNT-certified inspectors?
facets.a: The 21-vessel WSDOT fleet is Coast Guard inspected and dry-docked under contract, and bidders supply method procedures and inspector qualification records inside the package. Three replacement hybrid-electric ferries are contracted to Eastern Shipbuilding Group with first delivery scheduled for 2030, so the existing hulls absorb steel renewal and weld inspection across the rest of this decade.

facets.q: Does a class thickness-measurement approval cover the Alaska fishing fleet?
facets.a: No. IACS UR Z17 Annex 1 paragraph 1.1 places two exclusions on the thickness-measurement category by name: non-ESP ships under 500 gross tonnage, and all fishing vessels. Work on the Terminal 91 fleet is accepted against class survey scope and the owner specification instead. The two credentials build separately and neither substitutes for the other.

facets.q: What does ASNT charge for the Level III examinations behind this?
facets.a: ASNT's published schedule lists the NDT Basic examination and the AE, ET, LT, RT and UT method examinations at $545 for members and $625 for non-members, with IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT at $525 and $605. Retake fees run lower. Level III certification renews every five years. Those fees are paid to ASNT, not to a consultant.

sections.heading: Puget Sound is three industries wearing one coastline
paragraphs: The Navy end of the Sound is Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility at Bremerton: roughly 15,000 people on 179 acres, six dry docks running from 638 to 1,151 feet, and the only facility in the United States certified to recycle nuclear-powered ships. Across the water, Vigor's Harbor Island yard occupies 27 acres with three large dry docks and holds a Master Ship Repair agreement, which places it in the same contracting category as HII Newport News, Everett Ship Repair and General Dynamics NASSCO on the Puget Sound Ship Repair Association roster.

Thirty minutes north, Salmon Bay and Lake Union hold a different industry. Pacific Fishermen Shipyard, founded in Ballard in 1946 by fishermen who wanted a yard of their own, and Lake Union Dry Dock, operating since 1919 across twelve acres, service the North Pacific catcher-processor fleet berthed at Terminal 91 and Fishermen's Terminal. Those vessels run from 250 feet up to the 376-foot Alaska Ocean, owned by Glacier Fish Company and the largest factory trawler in the United States fleet.

A third stream cuts through both. Washington State Ferries, a division of WSDOT, runs 21 auto-passenger vessels across 20 terminals with close to 2,000 employees and 16 unions, making it the largest ferry system in the United States. Vigor dry-docks those boats alongside Navy and Coast Guard hulls at Harbor Island, and Nichols Brothers Boat Builders at Freeland on Whidbey Island built the car ferry Samish. One inspection firm here quotes all three streams inside a single quarter.

sections.heading: Bremerton and Harbor Island both answer to Tech Pub 271
paragraphs: Navy NDT in Puget Sound is governed by NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271. Paragraph 1.6 carries the sentence that catches commercial firms out: personnel shall be certified in accordance with the activity's written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and SNT-TC-1A as modified shall be invoked as mandatory minimum requirements and shall not be considered as recommendations or guidelines. The recommended practice a commercial shop treats as flexible becomes a contract floor the moment a Bremerton or SUPSHIP job order lands.

Paragraph 1.5.5 names the person who carries it. The Level III NDT Examiner is the individual to whom the activity delegates responsibility and authority to examine and certify NDT personnel, and the individual to whom the activity assigns responsibility for approving NDT procedures and workmanship standards. The document states plainly that the Examiner is equivalent to the Level III in ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Without that person on the org chart, a Puget Sound firm has nobody who can sign a certification or release a procedure.

This is precisely the gap that [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting services](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) fill. Tech Pub 271 never requires the Examiner to be an employee; it requires the activity to delegate the role, record the delegation, and stay responsible for programme adequacy under paragraph 1.6.3. [Written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) is the first deliverable, because every other requirement in Chapter 1 points back at it, including the limited-scope certifications that paragraph 1.6.1.1 permits for technicians performing one operation of a method.

sections.heading: Nothing you certified at the last yard travels with you
paragraphs: Two paragraphs kill the most common shortcut in the Sound. Paragraph 1.6.9 states that transfer of NDT certifications to other activities is prohibited except as authorized by NAVSEA. Paragraph 1.7.4 states that procedures shall not be transferred from one activity to another without the specific approval of NAVSEA. Hiring a certified ultrasonic inspector away from a Bremerton contractor does not import that certification, and copying a proven magnetic particle procedure from a previous employer does not import its approval.

An activity is defined in paragraph 1.5.3 as all sites of an organisation under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan. Open a second shop in Everett under separate QA management and it becomes a separate activity. Acquire a competitor and leave its QA system intact and you now operate two activities. Each one needs its own written practice, its own certified people and its own approved procedures before it touches Navy steel.

Procedures also carry a physical burden. Paragraph 1.7.2 requires each procedure to be qualified by proving that known discontinuities, natural or artificial, can be reliably detected and evaluated, with those discontinuities sized near the threshold of acceptance and rejection. That is bench work on real specimens, not a document review, and it is the part of [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) that Seattle shops consistently underbudget in calendar time.

sections.heading: Washington State Ferries: 21 hulls carrying the load until 2030
paragraphs: The WSF fleet is the second-largest vehicle ferry operation in the world, carrying more than nine million vehicles in 2024. In July 2025 the state contracted Eastern Shipbuilding Group in Panama City, Florida, to build three new 160-car hybrid-electric ferries, with first delivery scheduled for 2030 and the second and third following in 2031 and 2032. That is the first out-of-state ferry build Washington has ordered in more than fifty years, and the total programme is budgeted at $1.15 billion.

The scheduling consequence matters more to an inspection firm than the contract award does. The existing 21 vessels carry the entire service through the rest of this decade, which pushes steel renewal, shell plating replacement, tank work and structural weld inspection into every dry-docking window Vigor can open at Harbor Island. Weld inspection volume on an ageing fleet climbs while replacements are under construction elsewhere; it does not fall away.

Ferry work sits under Coast Guard inspection rather than NAVSEA, so the procedures, acceptance criteria and record formats differ from the Navy package filed in the same cabinet. A firm bidding both writes one written practice carrying two procedure sets, and the Examiner who signs the certification statement on each procedure under paragraph 1.7.1 has to be fluent in both. Bidders hand over inspector qualification records with the package, which means those records have to be current on bid day.

sections.heading: The Alaska fleet does not schedule around your audit
paragraphs: The North Pacific fleet works a fixed calendar. Bering Sea pollock A season opened on 20 January in 2026 and runs to mid-April; hake follows from mid-May to late June; pollock B season runs June to October, with C and D seasons across August to October and hake again from September to November. The North Pacific Fishery Management Council held the 2026 Bering Sea pollock total allowable catch at 1.375 million metric tons, so the fleet that has to be maintained is stable in size.

Back that calendar out and the yard window compresses to roughly November through the second week of January. Every catcher-processor needing shaft work, tank steel, hull plating or a class survey competes for the same berths at Vigor, Lake Union Dry Dock, Pacific Fishermen and Everett Ship Repair inside the same eight weeks. Technicians are on the boats rather than in a classroom, and test blocks are in the field rather than on a bench.

A qualification programme therefore belongs in spring or late summer, well away from the surge. Practical examinations, the procedure demonstrations required by paragraph 1.7.2 and the annual oversight required by paragraph 1.6.10 all draw on the same senior people that production needs in December. Scheduling [NDT Level 3 exam oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) in the off-season is the difference between a programme that stays current and one that expires while the fleet is at sea.

sections.heading: Why a class thickness-measurement certificate skips the fishing fleet
paragraphs: IACS Unified Requirement Z17 sets the approval scheme for firms whose results a class surveyor relies on when making decisions affecting classification or statutory certification. Annex 1 section 1 covers thickness measurement of structural material, and paragraph 1.1 carves out two exclusions by name: non-ESP ships under 500 gross tonnage, and all fishing vessels. A Seattle firm that earns a Z17 thickness-measurement certificate has not, by that act, qualified itself for the Terminal 91 fleet.

The Z17 requirements still matter, because cargo work in the Sound does sit under them. The responsible supervisor is to be qualified to a recognised national or international NDT standard such as ISO 9712 Level II. Operators are to be certified at Level I and to know ship structure well enough to select representative measurement positions. The surveyor countersigns each separate job. Certificates for thickness-measurement firms renew at intervals not exceeding three years, shorter than the five-year general rule.

Z17 also names ASNT directly in places. In the membrane cargo containment sections, supervisors and operators can be certified to ISO 9712 or to SNT-TC-1A, subject to one condition: SNT-TC-1A personnel must show that training was administered by an independent training body centrally certified to ASNT. Employer-based certification is accepted at sea. The condition attached to it is that somebody credible ran the training and somebody qualified signed the certificate.

sections.heading: The dated obligations an Examiner carries after the audit passes
paragraphs: Certification is a calendar, not an event. Under paragraph 1.6.4, NDT personnel other than Examiners are recertified at intervals not greater than three years and Examiners at intervals not greater than five, and a certification expires on the last day of the month in which recertification falls due. Recertification by evidence of continuing satisfactory technical performance is not permitted, and neither is recertification on the basis of ASNT certifications granted without examination.

Paragraph 1.6.10.1 adds annual surveillance: witnessing in-process inspections, reinspecting previously inspected product, or conducting a technical performance evaluation. At least one of the three, documented every twelve months, by the last day of the twelfth month. Paragraph 1.6.10.2 requires the technical performance evaluation itself to use production hardware or specimens containing discontinuities, performed before the end of the second year of the cycle for anyone carrying out acceptance inspections.

Miss the annual oversight and paragraph 1.6.4.1 forces re-examination by a practical examination administered by the activity's own Examiner. Vision tests run annually under paragraph 1.6.7.1 against the J1 letters on the Jaeger chart at a distance between 12 and 16 inches, and they expire the same way, on the last day of the retest month. A firm with no Level III on the day one of those clocks runs out has an inspector who cannot sign.

sections.heading: Standing up a Puget Sound programme without a staff Level III
paragraphs: A programme begins with the written practice, because paragraph 1.6 makes it the controlling document and also requires a copy to be handed to the Government inspector on request. From there the sequence is fixed: method procedures with the certification statement signed by the Examiner under 1.7.1, procedure demonstrations under 1.7.2, general, specific and practical examinations, then the personnel records listed in 1.6.8, down to vision-test records covering the current and preceding certification period.

Third-party costs are published and belong in the budget from the start. ASNT lists the NDT Basic examination and the AE, ET, LT, RT and UT method examinations at $545 for members and $625 for non-members, and IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT at $525 and $605, with lower retake fees. Its Level III experience routes run from twelve months on a four-year engineering or science degree through to forty-eight months with no college study at all.

Atlantis places an ASNT Level III against Puget Sound scopes on whatever terms the work needs: remote for written-practice and procedure drafting, on site at Harbor Island, Ballard or Bremerton for demonstrations and practical examinations, and on the calendar for the annual oversight nobody remembers in December. Nuclear-adjacent scopes at Bremerton draw on our [NDT consulting for nuclear facilities](/consulting/nuclear-ndt-consulting). Firms facing this in the Navy's other West Coast repair hub should read the [San Diego maritime NDT page](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-san-diego). Quote on request.

faq.q: Does Atlantis supply the Level III Examiner named in our NAVSEA written practice?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis supplies an ASNT Level III who is delegated the Examiner role under paragraph 1.5.5, signs the certification statement on each method procedure under 1.7.1, and administers or oversees personnel examinations. Your activity keeps responsibility for programme adequacy under paragraph 1.6.3, which is why the delegation is written into the practice rather than assumed.

faq.q: We hold ISO 9001 and a class thickness-measurement certificate. Is that enough for Bremerton work?
faq.a: No. IACS UR Z17 approval covers services a class surveyor relies on, and its quality-system clause accepts ISO 9000 series certification. NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 is a separate regime with its own written practice, its own Examiner, its own procedure qualification and its own examinations. The two run in parallel and neither shortens the other.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a Seattle firm ready for its first NAVSEA job order?
faq.a: The pacing item is procedure qualification under paragraph 1.7.2, which demands physical demonstration on specimens containing discontinuities near the acceptance threshold, plus the examination cycle for each inspector. Drafting the written practice moves quickly. Booking bench time, the right test blocks and senior technicians during the November to January fishing surge does not.

faq.q: Our Level III just resigned. What breaks first?
faq.a: Procedure approvals and personnel certifications both require the cognizant Examiner's signature. New certifications stop immediately, expiring certifications cannot be renewed, and the annual oversight under 1.6.10.1 has nobody to perform it. Paragraph 1.6.4 offers no grace period past the last day of the recertification month, so bridge the role before that month closes.

faq.q: Do you train our technicians in Seattle, or only audit the programme?
faq.a: Both. Atlantis delivers Level I and Level II training written against the same practice it drafts, then administers the general, specific and practical examinations that practice requires. Training weeks are scheduled around the Alaska calendar so classroom time falls outside the November to January yard surge, when the fleet needs those technicians on the boats.

title: In San Diego, NDT Qualification Is a Bid Gate, Not an Audit
description: Six yards, 14,000 workers, 54 homeported ships. San Diego repair is quoted year-round, and NAVSEA Tech Pub 271 qualification decides who gets to quote at all.
h1: Outsourced ASNT Level III Support for San Diego Ship Repair Firms
answer: San Diego runs on repair, not build. Six shipyards on Port tidelands support 14,000 workers, and work arrives as competitively awarded availabilities on the roughly 54 ships homeported at Naval Base San Diego. NDT qualification under NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 travels with the job order, so a lapsed written practice takes a firm out of contention before anyone reads its proposal.
expansion: San Diego is a repair market that competes continuously. The Port of San Diego counts six shipyards on its tidelands, Austal USA, BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair, Continental Maritime, General Dynamics NASSCO, Marine Group Boat Works and Nielsen Beaumont Marine, together supporting 14,000 workers and a $1.25 billion annual payroll. Naval Base San Diego homeports roughly 54 ships across 13 piers and is the principal homeport of the Pacific Fleet. Southwest Regional Maintenance Center competes maintenance and Chief of Naval Operations availabilities off multiple-award contracts, so the same firms bid again and again across the year. NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 governs the NDT on nearly all of it, and its requirements are dated. An expired inspector certification or a missed annual oversight never surfaces at an audit here. It surfaces when the next task order is quoted without you.
source: Verified against NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Rev 1 (paragraphs 1.5.2, 1.5.3, 1.5.5, 1.6, 1.6.2, 1.6.2.1, 1.6.3, 1.6.4, 1.6.7.1, 1.6.9, 1.6.10, 1.7.1-1.7.4, 1.8.1-1.8.4); the Port of San Diego shipyards page listing six tidelands yards with 14,000 workers and a $1.25 billion payroll; Naval Base San Diego facility data on homeported ships, piers and personnel; General Dynamics NASSCO public programme reporting on the John Lewis-class T-AO fleet oilers through 2026; GAO bid-protest and Navy contract records naming BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair and Continental Maritime of San Diego on multiple-award amphibious maintenance contracts with Southwest Regional Maintenance Center as contracting activity; IACS Unified Requirement Z17 Rev.15 sections 5, 6 and Annex 1; and the ASNT published Level III examination fee schedule.

table.note: Paragraph 1.6.9 prohibits transferring NDT certifications between activities, and 1.7.4 prohibits transferring procedures without specific NAVSEA approval. A San Diego firm that wins its first availability by hiring certified technicians away from a competing yard still starts its own programme from zero.

facets.q: Who administers the specific examination for an outsourced Level III?
facets.a: Paragraph 1.6.2.1 requires a specific examination for each method covering the employer's products, equipment, techniques and procedures, plus administration of the employer's written practice. It then states that preparing, approving and administering that examination is the responsibility of the employing activity, independent of the Examiner being tested. A contracted Level III cannot write the exam he then sits.

facets.q: Does Southwest Regional Maintenance Center approve our NDT programme?
facets.a: SWRMC is the contracting activity for the multiple-award contracts covering complex emergent and continuous maintenance and CNO availabilities on San Diego-homeported amphibious ships. Under paragraph 1.5.2, the Government inspector at a naval repair facility, a category that includes Regional Maintenance Centers, is the commanding officer or a delegated representative. At a commercial shipyard it is the Supervisor of Shipbuilding.

facets.q: How large is the San Diego repair market a qualified firm bids into?
facets.a: The Port of San Diego counts six shipyards on its tidelands, Austal USA, BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair, Continental Maritime, General Dynamics NASSCO, Marine Group Boat Works and Nielsen Beaumont Marine, supporting 14,000 workers and a $1.25 billion annual payroll. Naval Base San Diego homeports roughly 54 ships across 13 piers with about 26,000 personnel.

facets.q: Does NASSCO commercial work run under the same NDT rules as its Navy work?
facets.a: No. NASSCO is the only new-construction shipyard on the US West Coast building large ocean-going commercial vessels, and that work is surveyed by a classification society. Any outside firm whose results the surveyor relies on is approved under IACS UR Z17. Navy and Military Sealift Command hulls in the next dock run on NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 instead.

facets.q: What expires and takes a San Diego firm out of contention?
facets.a: Under paragraph 1.6.4, inspector certifications expire at three years and Examiner certifications at five, on the last day of the month recertification is due. Paragraph 1.6.10.1 requires documented annual oversight every twelve months, by the last day of the twelfth month. Vision tests run annually under 1.6.7.1. Any one of those ends signing authority outright.

facets.q: Can one written practice cover a NASSCO subcontract and a BAE availability?
facets.a: One written practice covers one activity, defined by paragraph 1.5.3 as all sites under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan. A single firm working both yards is one activity and needs one practice. The procedures underneath it cannot be shared with a different activity, because paragraph 1.7.4 prohibits transfer without specific NAVSEA approval.

sections.heading: The largest repair cluster on the West Coast, and the fleet that feeds it
paragraphs: San Diego holds six shipyards on Port of San Diego tidelands: Austal USA, BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair, Continental Maritime, General Dynamics NASSCO, Marine Group Boat Works and Nielsen Beaumont Marine. Between them they support 14,000 workers and a $1.25 billion annual payroll, and the Port describes the cluster as the largest and most capable shipbuilding and repair industry on the West Coast. That is not a statement about tonnage launched. It is a statement about the density of repair capacity within a few miles of one naval base.

The base sets the demand. Naval Base San Diego homeports roughly 54 ships across 13 piers on 1,600 acres of land and 326 acres of water, with around 26,000 military, civilian and contract personnel. The mix runs to amphibious assault ships including Essex and Boxer, cruisers, destroyers including the Zumwalt class, 18 littoral combat ships, two Coast Guard cutters and eight Military Sealift Command hulls. It is the principal homeport of the Pacific Fleet and the second-largest surface ship base in the world.

Geography compresses the market further. BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair leases its yard from the Port, sits immediately north of the naval base near the Coronado Bridge, and maintains more than 50 Navy vessels homeported locally. A technician can cover a NASSCO building dock in the morning and a BAE pier in the afternoon. That proximity is why San Diego subcontractors chase several primes at once, and why one lapsed certification file costs more than one job.

sections.heading: NASSCO is the one yard here that still builds
paragraphs: General Dynamics NASSCO sits at 28th Street and Harbor Drive with a dry dock that takes vessels up to 840 feet. It is the only new-construction shipyard on the West Coast of the United States building large ocean-going commercial vessels, and it is simultaneously a Master Ship Repair contractor for the Navy. Both halves of that description matter to an inspection firm, because between them they invoke two separate acceptance regimes inside the same fence line.

The Navy side is busy. NASSCO is under contract for 17 ships of the Navy's 20-ship John Lewis-class fleet oiler programme. USNS Sojourner Truth, T-AO 210, completed integrated sea trials in May 2026 and was handed over in San Diego the following month. Keels were laid for USNS Ruth Bader Ginsburg, T-AO 212, in February 2026 and USNS Harriet Tubman, T-AO 213, in June. Steel was first cut for USNS Joshua L. Goldberg, T-AO 211, in July 2026. Each hull runs 742 feet and carries 162,000 barrels.

A yard reaching four separate oiler milestones inside seven months generates a steady stream of production radiography, ultrasonic testing of plate and weld, and magnetic particle inspection on structure. It also generates subcontract demand, because no prime staffs peak NDT internally. The firms that capture that demand are the ones whose written practice, procedures and personnel files were already current when the schedule tightened, not the ones assembling them after an award lands.

sections.heading: Work arrives as availabilities, and availabilities do not wait
paragraphs: Repair work in San Diego arrives as availabilities. BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair and Continental Maritime of San Diego hold indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity multiple-award contracts covering complex emergent and continuous maintenance and Chief of Naval Operations availabilities on amphibious ships homeported in San Diego. Southwest Regional Maintenance Center is the contracting activity. Individual awards are competed off those vehicles, repeatedly, throughout the year.

That structure reshapes the qualification problem compared with a new-construction market. There is no single annual audit to prepare for. There is a rolling series of task orders, and a firm's NDT credentials form part of what it puts forward each time. A written practice that expired last month does not fail an audit. It removes the firm from the list before anyone opens the technical proposal, and nobody sends a notification when that happens.

Emergent work compresses this further. A ship returning from deployment with cracked structure does not wait while a subcontractor qualifies a procedure and examines an inspector. The work goes to whoever already holds current certification in the right method. Readiness in San Diego is a commercial asset with a shelf life, and that shelf life is set by dates written into NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271.

sections.heading: What Tech Pub 271 asks of the subcontractor, not just the prime
paragraphs: Tech Pub 271 treats the subcontractor as an activity in its own right. Paragraph 1.6.3 places responsibility for the adequacy of the NDT programme and for the certification of all levels of NDT personnel squarely on the employing activity. A prime contractor's approval does not extend down the chain. The subcontractor certifies its own people against its own written practice and hands a copy to the Government inspector on request under paragraph 1.6.

Which inspector that is depends on where the work sits. Paragraph 1.5.2 names the Supervisor of Shipbuilding or a delegated representative for commercial shipyards, and the commanding officer or a delegate for naval repair facilities, a category the document expressly extends to Regional Maintenance Centers. San Diego repair work routinely runs through the second route, so technical scrutiny arrives from the maintenance centre rather than from a shipbuilding office across the bay.

The controlling document is identical under both routes. Paragraph 1.6 requires personnel to be certified in accordance with the activity's written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and states that SNT-TC-1A as modified is invoked as mandatory minimum requirements rather than recommendations or guidelines. [Written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) is therefore the first piece of work on any San Diego engagement, because every requirement downstream cites back to it.

sections.heading: The records a San Diego prime will ask to see
paragraphs: Paragraph 1.8.1 requires an inspection record for any NDT inspection called for by a specification, contract or order, containing at minimum the record requirements listed in the applicable method section of the document. Where the controlling specification for the work carries its own NDT record requirements, or states that records are not required, that specification governs instead. San Diego primes ask for these records package by package, and an incomplete record set stalls a ship's certification as effectively as a rejected weld does.

Paragraph 1.8.3 is the clause that catches digitised shops. When a signature is specified, the signature shall be written and shall be entered on each inspection record to which it applies, and the use of any system or process for completing inspection records that does not provide for written signatures requires NAVSEA approval. A tablet workflow capturing a typed name does not satisfy that on its own. The approval has to be sought rather than assumed.

Paragraph 1.8.2 offers the only shortcut available. Attributes that never change can sit in the inspection procedure rather than on every record, provided each record still carries the procedure identification, a description or unique identification of the items inspected, the date of inspection, the inspector's signature and the disposition of those items. Paragraph 1.8.4 holds records for the period the ship or fabrication specification sets, and 1.6.8 opens personnel records to an authorised NAVSEA representative on request.

sections.heading: The Examiner cannot write his own specific examination
paragraphs: There is one hard limit on how far an outsourced Level III can go, and San Diego firms meet it more often than most because they qualify Examiners frequently. Paragraph 1.6.2 permits Examiner personnel to be tested by examinations administered by the employing activity, by ASNT, or by another outside agency. That much is flexible, and it is the clause consultants tend to quote. Paragraph 1.6.2.1 is the one that constrains the arrangement.

It requires a specific examination for each NDT method covering the specifications, equipment, techniques and procedures applicable to the employer's products and methods, plus administration of the employer's written practice. Then it sets the condition that matters: it is the responsibility of the employing activity, independent of the Examiner being tested, to prepare, approve and administer that examination. A contracted Level III cannot sit an examination he authored himself.

In practice the work splits cleanly. Atlantis drafts the practice, writes and qualifies the procedures, and runs general, specific and practical examinations for Level I and Level II personnel, while the employer or a second independent Level III prepares and administers the Examiner's specific examination. What an [outside NDT Level 3 can and cannot do](/consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do) is worth reading before scoping, and [NDT Level 3 exam oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) is arranged so nobody grades their own paper.

sections.heading: Two acceptance regimes inside one San Diego shop
paragraphs: The second San Diego complication is that commercial and Navy work live in the same shop. NASSCO commercial hulls are surveyed by a classification society, and any outside firm whose results that surveyor relies on is approved under IACS Unified Requirement Z17. Z17 asks for a documented quality system, work procedures covering all services supplied, personnel records showing training and experience, and a supervisor with at least two years as an operator inside the activity being approved.

Its personnel bar is written to international schemes. For thickness measurement of structural material, Annex 1 requires the responsible supervisor to be qualified to a recognised standard such as ISO 9712 Level II, and operators to be certified at Level I with enough knowledge of ship structure to select representative measurement positions. Elsewhere in Annex 1, ISO 9712 and ASNT SNT-TC-1A are both named as acceptable certification schemes for supervisors and operators.

The certificates then renew on different clocks. A Z17 certificate of approval renews at intervals not exceeding five years, and three years for firms engaged in thickness measurement, with the society free to require shorter intervals and intermediate audits. Tech Pub 271 runs on three and five years for people. A firm serving both sides of San Diego Bay tracks two renewal calendars, which is why any [maritime NDT consulting](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting) engagement starts by mapping them onto one sheet.

sections.heading: The dated obligations that quietly take a firm off the list
paragraphs: Certification in this regime is a set of dates rather than a plaque. Paragraph 1.6.4 recertifies NDT personnel other than Examiners at intervals not greater than three years, and Examiners at intervals not greater than five, with expiry falling on the last day of the month recertification is due. Recertification by evidence of continuing satisfactory technical performance is not permitted, and neither is recertification on ASNT certifications granted without examination.

Paragraph 1.6.10.1 requires documented annual oversight: witnessing in-process inspections, reinspecting previously inspected product, or conducting a technical performance evaluation, at least one of the three, every twelve months, by the last day of the twelfth month. Paragraph 1.6.10.2 requires that technical performance evaluation to use production hardware or specimens containing discontinuities, before the end of the second year of the cycle for anyone performing acceptance inspections.

Miss the annual oversight and paragraph 1.6.4.1 forces a practical re-examination administered by the activity's own Examiner. Vision tests run annually under 1.6.7.1 against the J1 letters on a Jaeger chart at a distance between 12 and 16 inches, expiring on the last day of the retest month. In a market that competes new work every few weeks, a certification month closing on a Friday decides whether you quote the next availability.

sections.heading: How Atlantis covers the Examiner role in San Diego
paragraphs: Atlantis engages against the San Diego calendar rather than a generic checklist. The first pass maps every expiring certification, every annual oversight due date and every procedure lacking current demonstration data, then sequences the work so nothing lapses between availabilities. Written practice and procedure drafting run remotely. Demonstrations, practical examinations and oversight witnessing happen on site at the yard, on the pier, or in the shop where the specimens live.

Third-party fees belong in the plan and they are published. ASNT lists the NDT Basic examination and the AE, ET, LT, RT and UT method examinations at $545 for members and $625 for non-members, with IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT at $525 and $605 and lower retake fees. Its Level III experience routes run from twelve months with a four-year engineering or science degree through to forty-eight months without college study.

Firms new to Navy work start with [ASNT Level III consulting services](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) and add methods as the bid pipeline demands them, rather than certifying everything at once. Firms facing the same problem in the Navy's northern West Coast repair hub will recognise most of this on our [Seattle and Puget Sound maritime NDT page](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-seattle), with a very different seasonal calendar attached. Affordable, accessible, fully customizable, and quoted on request.

faq.q: Can Atlantis act as the Examiner named in our San Diego written practice?
faq.a: Yes. Paragraph 1.5.5 defines the Examiner as the individual to whom the activity delegates authority to examine and certify NDT personnel and to approve procedures and workmanship standards, and it does not require employment. The delegation is documented in the written practice, and your firm keeps responsibility for programme adequacy under paragraph 1.6.3.

faq.q: We subcontract to BAE and NASSCO. Does their approval cover us?
faq.a: No. Paragraph 1.6.3 places responsibility for the adequacy of the NDT programme and the certification of all levels of NDT personnel on the employing activity, which is your firm. You maintain your own written practice, your own qualified procedures and your own certified personnel, and you produce the practice for the Government inspector on request.

faq.q: How fast can a San Diego shop be ready to quote its first availability?
faq.a: Procedure qualification sets the pace. Paragraph 1.7.2 requires each procedure to be proven on discontinuities sized near the acceptance and rejection threshold, which means bench time and the right specimens. Written practice drafting and examination scheduling move faster. Sequencing matters more than raw duration when task orders land with short response windows.

faq.q: Does our ISO 9001 certificate help with NAVSEA work?
faq.a: It helps on the class side. IACS UR Z17 states that a documented quality system complying with the current ISO 9000 series would be considered acceptable for service supplier approval. NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 is a separate regime built on a written practice, a delegated Examiner, qualified procedures and dated personnel certification. The two run in parallel.

faq.q: Do you train Level I and Level II technicians in San Diego?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis delivers Level I and Level II training written against the same practice it drafts, then administers the general, specific and practical examinations that practice requires. Training is scheduled around availability start dates so classroom weeks do not collide with the periods when the yard needs those technicians on the deck plates.

title: Ingalls Is Outsourcing Hulls. Its Suppliers Need a Level III.
description: Ingalls is raising outsourced shipbuilding hours 30% in 2026. Partner yards inherit no Ingalls procedures and no Ingalls certifications, so they build their own.
h1: Outsourced ASNT Level III Support for Pascagoula Shipyards and Fabricators
answer: Ingalls Shipbuilding doubled its distributed shipbuilding workload last year and plans a further 30 per cent rise in outsourced hours in 2026, with six partner yards on destroyers and two on structural units for LPD 32. Those partner yards inherit no Ingalls certifications and no Ingalls procedures. Each stands up its own written practice and its own Level III Examiner.
expansion: Pascagoula is a single-prime town with a refinery attached. Ingalls Shipbuilding occupies roughly 800 acres on the Pascagoula River with about 11,500 employees, making it the largest manufacturing employer in Mississippi, and it is builder of record for the Arleigh Burke destroyers and America-class amphibious assault ships and sole builder of the San Antonio class. It is now deliberately pushing structural work outward: distributed shipbuilding workload doubled last year, six partner yards took early work on destroyers 135, 137 and 139, and two hold contracts for eight structural units on LPD 32. Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding builds the Coast Guard's Polar Security Cutter a few miles away, and Chevron runs its largest wholly owned refinery across the harbour. Every one of those buyers wants NDT records signed by somebody its own inspector will accept.
source: Verified against NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Rev 1 (paragraphs 1.1, 1.3, 1.5.2, 1.5.3, 1.5.5, 1.6, 1.6.1, 1.6.1.1, 1.6.3, 1.6.4, 1.6.6, 1.6.7.1, 1.6.8, 1.6.9, 1.6.10, 1.7.1-1.7.4); HII and trade reporting on Ingalls distributed construction, including the doubling of distributed workload, the planned 30 per cent rise in outsourced hours for 2026, six partner yards on DDGs 135, 137 and 139 and two partner yards holding eight structural units on LPD 32; 33 CFR 334.781, which establishes the naval restricted area for Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion and Repair Gulf Coast, Pascagoula, Mississippi; Navy statements that SUPSHIP Gulf Coast oversees six ship classes at private yards in Pascagoula, New Orleans and Mobile; USNI reporting on Polar Security Cutter progress at Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding in August 2026; Chevron and Energy Intelligence reporting on Pascagoula refinery capacity and the announced expansion; and the ASNT published Level III examination fee schedule.

table.note: Ingalls plans to raise outsourced shipbuilding hours by roughly 30 per cent in 2026 after doubling distributed workload the year before. Every hour that leaves the yard moves NDT acceptance responsibility onto a supplier whose written practice has to exist before the unit ships.

facets.q: Can a partner yard use Ingalls NDT procedures on Ingalls work?
facets.a: No. Paragraph 1.7.4 of NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 states procedures shall not be transferred from one activity to another without the specific approval of NAVSEA. Paragraph 1.5.3 defines an activity as all sites under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan. A partner yard is a separate activity and writes its own procedures from scratch.

facets.q: Who is the Government inspector for a Pascagoula supplier?
facets.a: For commercial shipyards, paragraph 1.5.2 names the Supervisor of Shipbuilding or a delegated representative. Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion and Repair Gulf Coast is headquartered in Pascagoula, recognised in federal regulation at 33 CFR 334.781, and oversees Navy ship classes at private shipyards in Pascagoula, New Orleans and Mobile. The written practice goes to that inspector on request under paragraph 1.6.

facets.q: How much work is Ingalls actually pushing out to suppliers?
facets.a: Ingalls doubled its distributed shipbuilding workload in the prior year and plans to raise outsourced hours by roughly 30 per cent in 2026, with amphibious ships carrying a significant share. Six partner yards took early work on destroyers 135, 137 and 139. Two partner yards hold contracts for eight structural units on LPD 32, already in early production.

facets.q: Does refinery NDT experience count toward a Navy written practice?
facets.a: An individual's hours count, because paragraph 1.6.1 adopts the ASNT SNT-TC-1A training and experience minimums for initial certification. The procedures do not carry across. Chevron's refinery accepts inspection against ASME construction and API in-service criteria; a Navy job order accepts it against the drawing and Tech Pub 271. That means two procedure libraries and one Examiner keeping them apart.

facets.q: What must be finished before the first structural unit ships to Pascagoula?
facets.a: A written practice under paragraph 1.6, method procedures each carrying a certification statement signed by the cognizant Examiner under 1.7.1, procedure qualification by demonstration under 1.7.2, certified operators and inspectors, and the personnel records listed in 1.6.8 including current vision tests. Missing any one of those makes the NDT records on that unit unusable to the inspector.

facets.q: What do the ASNT examinations behind a Gulf Coast Level III cost?
facets.a: ASNT charges $545 for members and $625 for non-members on the NDT Basic examination and on the AE, ET, LT, RT and UT method examinations, and $525 and $605 on IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT, with cheaper retakes. Its experience routes span twelve months with a four-year technical degree to forty-eight months without college.

sections.heading: One prime, one refinery, and a supplier base being built at speed
paragraphs: Ingalls Shipbuilding occupies roughly 800 acres along the Pascagoula River and employs about 11,500 people, which makes it the largest manufacturing employer in Mississippi and the state's largest private employer of any kind. It has been building ships on that site for more than 85 years. Ingalls is builder of record for the Arleigh Burke class destroyers and the America class large-deck amphibious assault ships, and the sole builder of the San Antonio class amphibious transport docks. The destroyer Ted Stevens was delivered recently, with further hulls in the water preparing for trials.

A few miles away, Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding, the yard formerly trading as VT Halter Marine, is building the Coast Guard's Polar Security Cutter. As of August 2026 the stern sections of the future USCGC Polar Sentinel stood almost four storeys high, positioned to be welded into place. Across the harbour, Chevron operates its largest wholly owned refinery, running around 330,000 barrels a day, with an announced project to lift capacity roughly ten per cent to about 394,000 barrels and to widen the crude slate it can process.

That combination produces a labour market unlike any other maritime metro in the United States. The same welders, radiographers and ultrasonic technicians move between Navy structural steel, Coast Guard icebreaker hull sections and refinery pressure boundary work inside a single county. What does not move between them is paperwork. Each of those three buyers accepts inspection under a different code, and each expects a qualified Level III who has signed against that specific code rather than a general one.

sections.heading: Distributed construction is why supplier qualification is urgent here
paragraphs: The commercially important fact in Pascagoula right now is that Ingalls is deliberately sending work out. The company doubled its distributed shipbuilding workload in the prior year and plans to raise outsourced shipbuilding hours by roughly 30 per cent in 2026, with amphibious ships accounting for a significant share of that increase. Partner yards build outfitted structural units at their own facilities and ship them to Pascagoula for final assembly and integration, freeing the main yard workforce for the complex integration only a major shipyard absorbs.

The named packages are already in production. Six partner yards across several states took early work on destroyers 135, 137 and 139, beginning with a pilot Ingalls ran alongside the Navy's Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Gulf Coast on the future USS Thad Cochran. Two partner yards now hold contracts for eight structural units on LPD 32, the future USS Philadelphia. Every one of those units carries welded structure that has to arrive in Pascagoula with acceptable NDT records attached to it.

For a Gulf Coast fabricator this is the opening it has waited for and a qualification problem it has never had to solve. Shipping a structural unit into a Navy programme means standing up an NDT programme a Government inspector will accept, in advance, on the fabricator's own paper. [Written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) is the entry ticket rather than the finishing touch, and the delivery date for the first unit does not move to accommodate a late start.

sections.heading: SUPSHIP Gulf Coast is the Government inspector, and it is local
paragraphs: The Government inspector for that work sits in the same town. Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion and Repair Gulf Coast is headquartered in Pascagoula, a status recognised in federal regulation through the naval restricted area established at 33 CFR 334.781, and it oversees the design and construction of six US Navy ship classes at private shipyards in Pascagoula, New Orleans and Mobile. Proximity means scrutiny arrives quickly, in person, and repeatedly across the life of a package.

Tech Pub 271 names that office explicitly. Paragraph 1.5.2 defines the Government inspector as, for commercial shipyards, the Supervisor of Shipbuilding or a delegated representative. Paragraph 1.6 requires a copy of the activity's written practice to be provided to that inspector on request. Paragraph 1.7.3 requires procedures to be provided for review on request and allows a demonstration to be demanded whenever there is reason to believe a procedure cannot deliver adequate results. Paragraph 1.6.6 extends the same reach to people, permitting a practical or written examination of any individual whose competence is in question.

sections.heading: Nothing from Ingalls transfers to a partner yard
paragraphs: Two clauses decide whether a partner yard can lean on the prime. Paragraph 1.7.4 states procedures shall not be transferred from one activity to another without the specific approval of NAVSEA. Paragraph 1.6.9 bars the transfer of NDT certifications to other activities outright, absent authorization from NAVSEA. A fabricator awarded a structural unit package inherits neither Ingalls procedures nor Ingalls-certified inspectors, whatever else the drawing and specification package contains.

Paragraph 1.5.3 draws the boundary. An activity is all sites of an organisation under the same quality assurance management using the same quality assurance plan. A yard in Mobile and a yard in Gulfport operating under separate QA management are two activities, each needing its own written practice, its own approved procedures and its own certified people. Shared corporate ownership does not merge them, and neither does a shared logo on the gate.

The procedures themselves carry a physical burden that surprises first-time Navy suppliers. Under paragraph 1.7.2 a procedure is qualified only by demonstrating that known discontinuities, natural or artificial, are reliably detected and evaluated, and those discontinuities have to sit near the accept-reject threshold. [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) at this level is bench work on real specimens, and it is the line item most often left off a first-time supplier's schedule.

sections.heading: What the Examiner signs before the first unit ships north
paragraphs: Paragraph 1.5.5 defines the Level III NDT Examiner as the individual to whom the activity delegates responsibility and authority to examine and certify NDT personnel, and the individual to whom the activity assigns responsibility for approving NDT procedures and workmanship standards. The Examiner is stated to be equivalent to the Level III in ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Nothing in the publication requires that person to be an employee. It requires the role to be delegated and the delegation to be recorded.

Before the first unit ships north, the Examiner has signed several distinct things. The written practice under paragraph 1.6. A certification statement inside every method procedure under 1.7.1. The certification statement on every operator and inspector record under 1.6.8d. Procedure approval under 1.7.3. Each is a separate signature with a separate consequence, and each has to be in place before the NDT records travelling with that structural unit mean anything to a Government inspector.

Paragraph 1.6.3 keeps the employing activity responsible for the adequacy of the NDT programme and the certification of all levels of NDT personnel, so the delegation belongs in the written practice rather than implied by a purchase order. Paragraph 1.6.1.1 gives useful relief to small suppliers: limited-scope certifications with fewer training hours are permitted where described in the written practice, subject to floors of fifteen general and ten specific examination questions.

sections.heading: Bollinger and the Polar Security Cutter add a second acquiring service
paragraphs: The Polar Security Cutter puts a second acquiring service in the county. Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding took the programme over when it acquired VT Halter Marine and renamed the Pascagoula yards, and construction is visibly advancing, with stern sections of the future USCGC Polar Sentinel standing almost four storeys as of August 2026. Heavy icebreaker plate carries demanding weld inspection, and the programme draws on the same regional supplier base that Ingalls is now expanding.

A supplier serving both Ingalls and Bollinger remains one activity under paragraph 1.5.3 provided it operates under one quality assurance management and one plan, so it maintains one written practice. What it maintains separately is a procedure library per programme, because paragraph 1.3 leaves acceptance standards to the applicable drawing, specification, contract or order rather than fixing them. Paragraph 1.1 says so outright: the publication does not contain acceptance criteria for NDT. It covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual testing as methods, and the criteria arrive with the drawing.

sections.heading: The refinery across the harbour runs a different acceptance code
paragraphs: Chevron's Pascagoula refinery is the county's other large inspection employer, and it runs on a different code entirely. It is Chevron's largest wholly owned refinery, processing around 330,000 barrels a day, with an announced project to raise capacity by roughly ten per cent to about 394,000 barrels and to broaden the crude slate it can handle. Capital work and turnarounds on that scale generate sustained demand for weld inspection and pressure boundary examination.

The acceptance path there runs through ASME construction codes, API in-service inspection practice and the owner's inspection organisation rather than through a Government inspector. A technician's hours count toward qualification either way, because paragraph 1.6.1 adopts the ASNT SNT-TC-1A training and experience minimums. The procedures do not cross over. Refinery procedures written to ASME acceptance criteria carry no standing on a Navy structural unit, and Navy procedures carry none on a refinery vessel.

Firms working both sides of Jackson County therefore run one written practice and two procedure libraries, with the Examiner accountable for keeping the acceptance criteria from bleeding across. Our [petrochemical NDT consulting](/consulting/petrochemical-ndt-consulting) work covers the refinery side of that split, including method procedures and Level III oversight on turnaround scopes. Atlantis does not provide API 510, 570 or 653 certification training, and no part of this engagement substitutes for it.

sections.heading: Dated obligations and published third-party costs
paragraphs: The dated obligations are identical to those in every other NAVSEA market and are the most common cause of a supplier quietly falling out of compliance. Paragraph 1.6.4 recertifies personnel other than Examiners at intervals not greater than three years and Examiners at not greater than five, with expiry on the last day of the month recertification is due. Recertification on the strength of continuing satisfactory technical performance is not permitted under that paragraph.

Paragraph 1.6.10.1 imposes an annual oversight duty that has to be documented. The activity witnesses in-process inspections, reinspects previously inspected product, or runs a technical performance evaluation, and at least one of those happens every twelve months, closing by the last day of the twelfth month. Paragraph 1.6.10.2 requires the technical performance evaluation to run on production hardware or specimens containing discontinuities, before the end of the second year, for anyone performing acceptance inspections. [NDT Level 3 exam oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) covers both obligations.

Third-party costs are published and belong in the plan. ASNT prices the NDT Basic examination, and the AE, ET, LT, RT and UT method examinations, at $545 for members and $625 for non-members; IR, MFL, MT, PT and VT sit at $525 and $605, and retakes cost less. Its Level III experience routes run from twelve months with a four-year engineering or science degree to forty-eight months with no college study. Vision tests run annually under paragraph 1.6.7.1.

sections.heading: How Atlantis covers the Examiner role in Jackson County
paragraphs: Atlantis builds Gulf Coast programmes in the order a Government inspector reads them: written practice first, then method procedures with their demonstration data, then examinations and personnel records, then the oversight calendar that keeps all of it live. Drafting runs remotely. Procedure demonstrations, practical examinations and oversight witnessing happen on site, in Pascagoula or at the partner yard wherever it sits along the Gulf, because specimens and production hardware do not travel.

The engagement is scoped to the packages actually in play. A fabricator quoting eight structural units on an amphibious hull needs different methods certified than a shop chasing icebreaker plate or refinery piping. [ASNT Level III consulting services](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) are configured method by method, so a supplier certifies what the award requires this year rather than paying to certify a full method set it will not use.

Firms working a comparable Navy repair market on the West Coast will find the same clauses wearing a different local shape on our [San Diego maritime NDT page](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-san-diego). For Pascagoula the deciding variable is the ship schedule. Outsourced hours climb through 2026, and the suppliers holding current paper are the ones who get the call. Affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a quote issued on request.

faq.q: We fabricate structural steel and have never done Navy work. Where do we start?
faq.a: With the written practice required by paragraph 1.6, because every other requirement cites back to it, and with a decision on which methods the award actually needs. Procedure qualification under 1.7.2 and the examination cycle follow. Starting with equipment purchases before the practice exists produces certified technicians with nothing valid to sign against.

faq.q: Can Atlantis act as the Examiner named in our written practice?
faq.a: Yes. Paragraph 1.5.5 defines the Examiner as the individual to whom the activity delegates authority to examine and certify NDT personnel and to approve procedures and workmanship standards, without requiring employment. The delegation is written into the practice, and your firm retains responsibility for programme adequacy under paragraph 1.6.3 and for certifying all levels of personnel.

faq.q: Does SUPSHIP Gulf Coast audit our shop, or only Ingalls?
faq.a: Paragraph 1.6 requires the written practice to be provided to the Government inspector on request, and 1.7.3 requires procedures for review on request with demonstrations available. Paragraph 1.6.6 permits examination of any individual whose competence is questioned. Those provisions attach to the activity performing the NDT, which on a distributed construction package is your shop.

faq.q: Our technicians hold refinery certifications. Do they need new ones for Ingalls work?
faq.a: They need certification against your written practice for the Navy work, under paragraph 1.6. Their accumulated training and experience hours count toward the ASNT SNT-TC-1A minimums adopted by 1.6.1, so the history is not wasted. The examinations, procedures and acceptance criteria are separate, and paragraph 1.6.9 blocks certifications transferring between activities.

faq.q: How does Atlantis schedule around a Gulf Coast turnaround season?
faq.a: Procedure demonstrations, practical examinations and annual oversight are booked outside refinery turnaround windows and outside the weeks a structural unit is closing out, because the same senior technicians are needed for all three. The oversight calendar under paragraph 1.6.10.1 has a hard monthly deadline, so it is placed first and the rest is sequenced around it.

title: Barge Hull Gauging Training for Gulf Coast Brown-Water Fleets
description: Gulf Coast maritime NDT training for barge fleets on Subchapter M, class tonnage under ESP, and Mobile/Pascagoula new build. On-site cohorts, no crew travel.
h1: Hull Gauging and Weld NDT Training Built Around Gulf Coast Drydock Windows
answer: Gulf Coast maritime NDT training splits three ways: inland barge fleets on Subchapter M drydock and internal structural exams, offshore service vessels under class survey, and new construction at Mobile and Pascagoula. Atlantis delivers cohort training at the yard or operator's facility so crews qualify without leaving the region during turnaround season.
expansion: The Gulf Coast is not one maritime market. Kirby Inland Marine alone runs 1,134 tank barges and 291 towboats across the Mississippi River System, the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and the Houston Ship Channel, and those hulls are inspected under 46 CFR Subchapter M rather than class rules — a drydock and internal structural exam once in five years for freshwater service, twice in five years for vessels in salt water more than six months of any twelve. Blue-water tonnage calling at Houston, Mobile and Pascagoula runs the Enhanced Survey Programme instead, with close-up survey and thickness measurement scope widening as the hull ages. New construction at Austal USA in Mobile and Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding in Pascagoula adds a third regime again — weld inspection to build specification under NAVSEA technical publications. A Gulf Coast technician who knows only one of the three is employable in one lane.
