facets.q: Does API QUTE still exist under that name?
facets.a: Partly. API consolidated QUTE, QUSE, QUPA and QUSE-PA into two programmes, QUTE (M) for manual and QUTE (PA) for phased array, and the four legacy schemes are being sunset. Existing holders keep their certificates to the end of the current period and must recertify into one of the two new programmes. New applicants cannot enter the legacy schemes.

facets.q: Is an ASNT NDT Level III qualified to perform the UT scan itself?
facets.a: The Level III credential is earned on written examinations, so it evidences method knowledge, procedure authority and interpretation depth. It does not evidence hand skill on a flawed weld, because no specimen is scanned to earn it. Many Level IIIs scan superbly. The certificate is simply silent on the question your contract is trying to answer, which is detection rate.

facets.q: What does a QUTE (PA) certificate actually prove about a technician?
facets.a: That on one 8-hour day, on carbon steel SMAW butt welds between 0.25 in and 1.00 in thick and 2 in to 12 in diameter pipe, totalling roughly 75 linear inches, the technician's missed detections, missed characterisations, flaw start and stop positions and false calls fell inside API's grading limits. It proves performance on that specimen set.

facets.q: Can we require QUTE (PA) on every UT scope in a turnaround contract?
facets.a: You can write it. You will waive it. API reports 77 QUTE (PA) holders and 17 QUTE (M) holders worldwide as of 30 April 2026, against 21,996 API 510 certifications. Performance demonstration sessions ran four times in 2026, in Houston, with roughly half the candidates failing. Reserve the requirement for scopes where the read drives a run-or-repair decision.

facets.q: What is the accepted precedent for a performance demonstration clause?
facets.a: Nuclear. ASME BPVC Section XI Mandatory Appendix VIII qualifies the whole examination system, personnel, procedure and equipment together, rather than the individual alone, and US utilities implement it through the EPRI-operated Performance Demonstration Initiative. Borrow the structure: qualify the system, name the specimen set, and state what happens when the qualified technician is replaced mid-job.

facets.q: Does holding ASNT Level III cover the QUTE prerequisite?
facets.a: Yes, and comfortably. API opens the ultrasonic examiner programmes to anyone holding Level II or above from ASNT, CGSB, PCN or any other ISO 9712 accredited scheme. A Level III in UT clears the gate with room to spare. The prerequisite is the cheap part; the performance demonstration in Houston is where candidates are actually lost.

sections.heading: What API QUTE is, and what API renamed it to
paragraphs: API's Qualification of Ultrasonic Testing Examiners programmes sit inside the same Individual Certification Programs portfolio as API 510 and API 570, but they work nothing like them. There is no written exam. A candidate spends one eight-hour day at the PRCI Technology Development Center on Langfield Road in Houston, scanning welded specimens whose flaws API knows and the candidate does not. The grade comes from four error classes: missed detections, missed characterisations, wrong flaw start and stop positions and total length, and false calls.

The structure changed in 2024. API revalidated QUTE, QUSE, QUPA and QUSE-PA, and by consensus agreement consolidated four programmes into two: QUTE (M) for manual ultrasonics and QUTE (PA) for phased array. The four legacy programmes are being sunset. Holders keep their certificates to the end of their current certification period and must recertify into one of the two survivors. QUTE-TM, the straight-beam thickness measurement programme covering metal from 0.160 in to 2.00 in, continues alongside them as a separate credential.

That matters to your contract before any technical argument does. A turnaround clause reading "API QUTE certified" now names a programme with no route in for new candidates. A bidder can satisfy the words with a legacy certificate that expires and cannot be renewed, and nobody notices until the next contract cycle. API's public programme-updates page carries the sunset notices for Tank Entry Supervisor and the Certified Auditor Program, but not this consolidation; it appears in the Individual Certification Programs status update presented at API's April 2026 annual meeting.

sections.heading: What an ASNT NDT Level III certificate actually attests
paragraphs: The ASNT NDT Level III credential is earned on written examinations: the NDT Basic exam plus at least one Method exam. ASNT publishes three entry routes, being a four-year engineering or physical science degree with twelve months of experience, two years of post-secondary engineering or science study with twenty-four months, or forty-eight months of experience with no college. The certificate runs five years and renews by method examination or by accumulated recertification points before expiry.

What it attests is knowledge and authority. The holder can write and approve procedures, establish techniques, interpret codes and acceptance standards, and train and examine Level I and Level II personnel. That is precisely what a UT scope needs sitting above the technician, and it is why the credential belongs in your contract at all. It is also, by design, not a statement about hand skill, because nothing in the examination requires the candidate to scan a flawed weld and call it.

The second thing to settle is who does the certifying. Under [SNT-TC-1A](/compliance/asnt-snt-tc-1a) the employer certifies its own personnel against its own written practice, and ASNT's Level III examination is a third-party test of knowledge that the employer then relies on. [ANSI/ASNT CP-189](/compliance/ansi-asnt-cp-189) tightens the same architecture into a standard rather than a recommended practice. If your clause says "ASNT Level III", decide whether you mean ASNT's certificate, the employer's Level III certification, or both. They are different documents and they fail audit differently.

sections.heading: Where the two credentials genuinely overlap
paragraphs: The overlap is at the entrance, not the outcome. API opens the ultrasonic examiner programmes to any applicant currently holding Level II or above from ASNT, CGSB, PCN or any other ISO 9712 accredited NDE certification. A UT Level III clears that gate without effort. So the credentials are not rivals in any procurement sense; one is the admission ticket to the other, and a QUTE (PA) holder is by definition already Level II or higher in ultrasonics.

They also share a scope problem. A Level III certificate names methods, not techniques, so a UT Level III is not automatically competent in phased array, time of flight diffraction or corrosion mapping, and the certificate will not tell you which. Working out where a given Level III's authority actually ends is the whole content of [method scope limitations](/consulting/level-iii-method-scope-limitations), and it is the same question QUTE answers narrowly and honestly for one weld geometry on one day.

sections.heading: What an owner is really buying by specifying QUTE
paragraphs: Strip the branding away and a QUTE requirement buys one thing: a measured false call rate and a measured miss rate, produced by an independent body on specimens the technician has never seen. That is a genuinely different purchase from a knowledge certificate. It is the same purchase the nuclear sector made when it stopped trusting prescriptive UT rules and built ASME Section XI Mandatory Appendix VIII, where personnel, procedure and equipment are qualified together as one examination system.

It also buys a specific, bounded population of welds. The QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) specimen set is carbon steel SMAW butt welds, 0.25 in to 1.00 in thick flat plate and 2 in to 12 in diameter pipe, roughly 75 linear inches of weld in total. If your turnaround scope is 2 in stainless socket welds, dissimilar metal welds, clad overlay or thick-wall coke drum shells, a QUTE (PA) certificate proves competence on something adjacent to your problem, not on your problem.

And it buys nothing at all about reporting. The technician who demonstrated on API's specimens still writes a report your integrity engineer has to act on, and the failure mode that actually costs owners money is a defensible read written up indefensibly. That gap is what [report validation](/report-validation/what-makes-an-ndt-report-defensible) closes, and it sits downstream of every credential in this article.

sections.heading: The supply problem your clause has to survive
paragraphs: The numbers are unforgiving. As of 30 April 2026 API records 17 QUTE (M) holders and 77 QUTE (PA) holders worldwide, plus 125 on legacy QUTE, 162 on QUPA, 14 on QUSE and 13 on QUSE-PA. Every one of those legacy certificates is on a countdown. Set against 21,996 API 510 certifications and 20,030 API 570 certifications, the entire performance-demonstrated ultrasonic population is a rounding error, and it is concentrated in a handful of specialist houses.

Throughput does not fix it. API scheduled four QUTE performance demonstration sessions in 2026, on 26 to 28 January, 16 to 18 March, 18 to 20 May and 20 to 22 July. Across the whole of 2025, 19 candidates sat QUTE (M) and four passed; QUTE (PA) took 60 candidates and passed 32. In the first three 2026 sessions QUTE (PA) passed 10 of 23. A single owner cannot buy its way out of that with a purchase order.

So write the clause knowing you are competing for a few dozen people against every other operator with the same clause. The realistic lever is not the certificate, it is the crew you retain and develop, which is why an honest UT strategy usually reads as ASNT method training plus a Level III who audits reads, rather than a procurement requirement nobody can meet.

sections.heading: The equivalency clause, written properly
paragraphs: Start by refusing the word "equivalent" on its own. An audit-proof equivalency clause states what the alternative must demonstrate, not what it must be called. Write the acceptance criteria into the contract: the specimen population, the flaw types, the maximum permitted false call rate, the sizing tolerance, and who witnesses the demonstration. Once those exist, a technician with a QUTE (PA) certificate satisfies them by presenting the certificate, and everyone else satisfies them by demonstrating.

Next, name the credential exactly as its issuer now names it. "API QUTE (PA), Qualification of Ultrasonic Testing Examiners (Phased Array)" leaves no argument. Add a line stating that a certificate issued under a superseded API programme is accepted until its stated expiry date and not renewable, which quietly handles every legacy QUPA holder on your site without a variation order.

Finally, separate the technician requirement from the oversight requirement. The technician demonstrates. The Level III owns the procedure, the technique sheet, the calibration blocks and the acceptance criteria, and signs the technique as fit for the geometry actually in front of the crew. Splitting those two lines is what makes the clause survive an audit, because the auditor can trace each obligation to a named person and a dated document.

sections.heading: Three clause patterns, and when each one is right
paragraphs: Pattern one, performance demonstration mandatory. Use it where the ultrasonic read alone decides whether equipment restarts: crack-like flaws in a hydrogen service vessel, weld overlay integrity, or any read feeding an API 579 assessment. Here the false call rate is worth the mobilisation pain, and the population of qualified technicians is small enough to name in the bid tab. Expect to book the technician months out and to pay for the scarcity.

Pattern two, tiered acceptance. Performance demonstration for a named list of critical welds, ASNT or ISO 9712 Level II under Level III oversight for the balance, with a written technique per geometry. This is the pattern that actually gets executed on a live turnaround, and it is the one most owners converge on after their first waived clause. The list of critical welds is the real negotiation; write it during scoping, not during execution.

Pattern three, verification instead of qualification. Accept Level II under Level III oversight, then buy independent review of the output, either as [third-party review or targeted re-inspection](/report-validation/third-party-review-vs-re-inspection). This works when your risk sits in interpretation and documentation rather than raw detection, and it is materially easier to resource than a demonstration requirement. It also produces evidence an auditor can read, which a certificate photocopy never does.

sections.heading: Verifying a credential before the crew mobilises
paragraphs: Ask for the certificate image, not the CV line, and read three fields: the exact programme name, the issue date and the expiry. API ultrasonic examiner certifications run three-year terms and require full retesting to renew, with recertification applications accepted from 90 days before expiry and a 90-day grace period carrying a late fee. Past that grace period the certification lapses and the holder starts again, so a certificate that expired four months ago is not a technicality.

For the ASNT side, ask for the certificate and the employer's written practice, and check that the methods and levels on the certificate match the methods and levels the written practice assigns to the work. A [programme audit or gap assessment](/consulting/ndt-program-audit-gap-assessment) does exactly this across a contractor's whole roster, and it routinely finds people working outside their certified method scope with entirely genuine certificates in the file.

sections.heading: What to do about legacy QUTE holders already on contract
paragraphs: Do nothing punitive. A legacy QUTE, QUSE, QUPA or QUSE-PA certificate is valid until it expires, and those technicians demonstrated on API specimens the same way the new cohort does. Treat them as qualified for the balance of their term and put a diary marker on each expiry date. What you must not do is renew a contract clause that assumes those holders can requalify into the programme named in the clause, because that route is closed.

Then have the conversation with the contractor early. A technician moving from QUPA to QUTE (PA) must sit the full performance demonstration again, in Houston, on a session date set by API. Between the four annual sessions and the observed pass rates, a contractor with six legacy holders needs roughly a year of planning to carry them across. Ask for that plan at bid stage and you will learn more about a bidder's technical depth than any capability statement gives you.

sections.heading: Where this leaves your turnaround scope
paragraphs: The honest position for an owner is that QUTE is worth specifying on a short, named list of welds and worth abandoning everywhere else. Hold the line where a missed crack ends a run; take Level II under credible Level III oversight everywhere else and buy independent scrutiny of the output. That combination is resourceable, auditable, and it survives the day the specified technician calls in sick.

Atlantis does not sell API certification training, and the QUTE performance demonstration is API's to administer. What we do is the layer around it: [ASNT method training](/training) for the Level I and Level II population you actually have to grow, [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) covering procedure ownership and method scope, and [independent report validation](/report-validation) on the reads that matter. If you are rewriting turnaround clause language this cycle, send us the draft clause and we will mark up what will hold. [Talk to us](/contact) for a demo or a quote on request. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

faq.q: Is API QUTE the same thing as an ASNT Level III in ultrasonics?
faq.a: No. ASNT NDT Level III is a written-examination credential covering method knowledge, procedure authority and interpretation, valid five years. API QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) are hands-on performance demonstrations, graded on missed detections, missed characterisations, flaw positions and false calls on API's own flawed specimens, valid three years with full retesting to renew.

faq.q: Can a technician hold QUTE (PA) without any ASNT certification?
faq.a: Not through ASNT alone, but there is more than one route in. API requires the applicant to hold Level II or above from ASNT, CGSB, PCN or another ISO 9712 accredited NDE certification scheme. A PCN or CGSB Level II ultrasonic certification satisfies the prerequisite exactly as an ASNT Level II does.

faq.q: How much does the QUTE performance demonstration cost?
faq.a: API's published ICP fee schedule lists initial certification for QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) at $750 for API members and $850 for non-members, with recertification at $700 and $800. QUTE-TM is listed at $700 and $800 initial, $650 and $750 to recertify. Travel to Houston and the technician's lost billable day sit on top of those figures.

faq.q: Where can I read API's own notice that QUTE was consolidated?
faq.a: In the Individual Certification Programs status update presented to API's annual meeting, breakdown as of 30 April 2026, which states that the QUTE, QUSE, QUPA and QUSE-PA programmes were revalidated, consolidated into QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) by consensus agreement, and sunset. The individual programme pages on api.org describe the two surviving programmes without narrating the transition.

faq.q: Does Atlantis deliver API QUTE or API 510 training?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not sell API certification training, and the QUTE performance demonstration can only be administered by API. Atlantis delivers ASNT method training to Level I, II and III, outsourced ASNT Level III consulting for procedure ownership and method scope, and independent NDT report validation. Demo or quote on request.

faq.q: Should the clause name RT instead, to avoid the problem entirely?
faq.a: Sometimes, and it is worth pricing. The trade between the two methods on weld work is not a preference argument, it is a flaw-orientation and access argument, laid out in [RT vs UT for weld inspection](/blog/rt-vs-ut-weld-inspection). Radiography carries its own qualification chain, source logistics and exclusion-zone cost, so the substitution is rarely free.

title: API 510 or a National Board Commission? The Midstream RFP Test
description: A National Board commission is issued to your employer and expires every 31 December. API 510 travels with the person. Which to name in a midstream RFP, and why.
h1: Jurisdictional authority and owner-user authority are not the same purchase
answer: Name both, on different lines. API 510 certifies an individual to run an owner-user in-service vessel programme and travels with them between employers. A National Board Inservice Inspector Commission authorises jurisdictional inspection and is issued only while the holder is exclusively employed by a jurisdiction, an Authorized Inspection Agency, or an accredited Owner-User Inspection Organization.
expansion: The tell in most midstream RFPs is a line saying the inspector shall be API 510 certified and National Board commissioned. Written that way it excludes almost every third-party inspection contractor in the country, because RCI-1 requires exclusive employment by a jurisdiction, an Authorized Inspection Agency, an Owner-User Inspection Organization, a non-member enforcement agency, or the National Board itself. A vendor cannot simply hire a commissioned inspector and bill you; the employer has to hold the accreditation, and the commission card carries the employer's name. Separate the two requirements. Ask for API 510 on the inspector performing and signing the in-service inspection, and ask for a National Board Inservice Inspector Commission with the R endorsement only where NBIC repair or alteration acceptance is in scope. Then ask the bidder for the accreditation certificate number, not the individual's card.
source: NB-263, RCI-1, Rules for Commissioned Inspectors, 2025 Edition, effective 1 January 2025 and mandatory from 1 July 2025; NB-371, Accreditation of Owner-User Inspection Organizations, Revision 11, approved 10 May 2025; the National Board Inspection Code NB-23, 2025 Edition; API Standard 510, 11th edition with Errata 1 (2023) and Errata 2 (2025); API 510 Body of Knowledge dated September 2025; API ICP status update as of 30 April 2026.

facets.q: Can a third-party inspection vendor supply a National Board commissioned inspector?
facets.a: Only if the vendor itself is an Authorized Inspection Agency, an accredited Owner-User Inspection Organization, a jurisdiction, a non-member enforcement agency, or the National Board. RCI-1 requires exclusive employment by one of those, and the commission card names the employer. An ordinary NDT or inspection contractor cannot hold commissions for hire, which is why this RFP line quietly disqualifies most bidders.

facets.q: Does API 510 count toward a National Board commission?
facets.a: Yes. RCI-1 Table 1 awards two of the five required credit points for certification as an API 510 or API 570 inspector, the same weight it gives an AWS Certified Welding Inspector. A bachelor's degree in engineering, technology, science or mathematics is worth three. Experience adds one point per year, capped at four, and education credit is capped at four.

facets.q: What is an Owner-User Inspection Organization?
facets.a: It is your own company, accredited by the National Board so that commissioned inspectors on your payroll may inspect equipment you own and operate. NB-371 requires a quality management system meeting NB-381, a National Board review of the facility, a supervisor holding an active Inservice Inspector Commission, and a separate Certificate of Accreditation for each jurisdiction. The certificate expires every three years.

facets.q: Who signs off a weld repair on an in-service vessel at a gas plant?
facets.a: Two signatures, not one. The repair organization works to NBIC Part 3 under a National Board R Certificate of Authorization, and the acceptance inspection is made by a Repair Inspector holding an Inservice or Authorized Inspector Commission plus the R endorsement. Your API 510 inspector owns the engineering evaluation, the repair plan, the re-rating decision and the acceptance of the vessel back into service.

facets.q: How much ultrasonics does an API 510 inspector actually get tested on?
facets.a: Less than most RFP writers assume. The API 510 body of knowledge dated September 2025 draws its ultrasonic content from ASME Section V Article 23, SE-797 only, which is manual pulse-echo contact thickness measurement. Shear wave flaw detection, sizing and phased array are outside the exam. An API 510 certificate is not evidence that the holder can judge a weld inspection read.

facets.q: What should the RFP ask bidders to produce?
facets.a: Four documents. The inspector's current API 510 certificate with its expiry. The commission card, showing the employer name and the 31 December expiry, where a commission is genuinely needed. The employer's Authorized Inspection Agency or Owner-User Inspection Organization Certificate of Accreditation, with the jurisdiction it covers. And the written practice under which the NDE examiners supporting the inspector were certified.

sections.heading: The two commissions the National Board issues
paragraphs: There are exactly two. The National Board Inservice Inspector Commission, designated IS, is issued to individuals qualified to perform installation and in-service inspections, meaning the jurisdictionally required periodic inspections of boilers and pressure vessels that are in operation. The National Board Authorized Inspector Commission, designated AI, is issued to individuals qualified to perform the inspections required by the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code during construction. For an operating midstream asset, IS is the one that matters and AI is the one people accidentally ask for.

Everything else in the system is an endorsement layered on top of a commission. N, I and C cover nuclear construction, nuclear in-service and nuclear concrete. R is the Repair Inspector endorsement, which is what unlocks acceptance inspections of repairs and alterations under the National Board Inspection Code. B and O are supervisor endorsements, B for an Authorized Inspector Supervisor and O for an Owner-User Inspector Supervisor. None of them stands alone.

The governing document is NB-263, RCI-1, Rules for Commissioned Inspectors. The 2025 Edition became effective 1 January 2025 and mandatory from 1 July 2025, and the National Board publishes a new edition every two years, with the next planned to take effect 1 January 2027. If your RFP template cites an older edition by year, it is already stale, and the auditor reading your file will notice.

sections.heading: The employment rule that decides your RFP
paragraphs: RCI-1 paragraph 1-1.1 is the clause that quietly rewrites your bidder list. A candidate for a National Board Commission shall be in the exclusive employment of a Jurisdictional Authority, an Authorized Inspection Agency, an Owner-User Inspection Organization, a Non-Member Enforcement Agency, or the National Board. The National Board's own guidance adds a Federal Inspection Agency to that list. There is no individual application route; the candidate and the employer apply jointly, and the commission card carries the employer's name.

The consequences run further than most RFP authors expect. Commissions expire annually on 31 December, and the employer renews them, documenting that the inspector completed the required continuing education for each commission and endorsement held. Change employer and the commission has to be transferred on an Application for Change of Employment, with continuing education completed in the twelve months before submittal. Let it lapse more than two years and reinstatement requires retaking the examination.

There is also an ethics rule with teeth. RCI-1 Part 7 requires Commissioned Inspectors to be independent from designing, manufacturing, supplying, installing, purchasing, owning or maintaining the items they inspect, and bars inspecting work performed by entities under the same corporate structure or contractual arrangement. Inspectors employed by an accredited Owner-User Inspection Organization may be exempt from those requirements. That single carve-out is the whole reason the owner-user route exists.

sections.heading: How a person gets a commission, and where API 510 counts
paragraphs: The default path is five credit points drawn from education and experience, with a minimum of one and a maximum of four from each side. Education credit includes three points for a bachelor's degree or higher in engineering, technology, science or mathematics, two for a two-year degree or an accredited apprenticeship, and two for an AWS Certified Welding Inspector certification. Certification as an API 510 or API 570 inspector is also worth two points. Eighty hours of classroom technical training in boiler, pressure vessel or piping inspection earns one.

Experience credit is one point per year in engineering or design review, manufacturing, high-pressure steam plant operation above 50,000 lb/hr, repairs and alterations, quality control systems, inspection of boilers or pressure vessels, or work as an NDE examiner meeting ASNT Level II or III by examination. Concurrent experience does not stack; two years as a QC manager who was simultaneously a Level II examiner is two years, not four.

There is a second route. RCI-1 paragraph 1-1.3 allows the National Board Inservice Inspector Training Program, described in NB-380, in place of the five credit points. It combines mentored on-the-job training with the classroom Inservice Inspector Commission Course, three online courses covering NBIC Part 1, NBIC Part 2 and RCI-1, and a minimum of 300 inspections carried out under the instruction of a National Board Commissioned Inspector. Partial credit is not granted. Either route ends at the same examination, which requires 70 percent to pass.

sections.heading: What the R endorsement adds, and when you need it
paragraphs: The R endorsement is the Repair Inspector qualification, and it is the one midstream RFPs most often omit and then need. It requires the National Board Repair Inspector Course plus an active IS or AI commission. A holder of an IS commission also needs eighty hours of diversified experience as a Repair Inspector trainee under direct supervision, of which up to forty hours may be credited from Authorized Inspector on-the-job training and up to eight hours from observing a joint review for a National Board Certificate of Authorization.

What the endorsement buys is the authority to make authorization, in-process and acceptance inspections for repairs and alterations to NBIC Part 3, and to sign the National Board report forms that follow. If a vessel at your gas plant needs a weld repair to a pressure boundary, that signature is a separate deliverable from your API 510 inspector's engineering evaluation, and it is the one that keeps the jurisdiction and the insurer satisfied.

So the practical RFP question is not which credential, it is which deliverables. In-service inspection and interval setting is API 510 work. Repair and alteration acceptance under the NBIC is R endorsement work. The two overlap on the same vessel in the same outage, and the bidder who cannot name who signs which form is telling you something. That reconciliation is exactly what an [API 510 programme audit](/consulting/api-510-program-audit) is for.

sections.heading: The Owner-User Inspection Organization route
paragraphs: NB-371, Revision 11, approved by the Board of Trustees on 10 May 2025, sets the rules for accrediting your own company. An OUIO Certificate of Accreditation allows National Board Commissioned Inspectors on your payroll to perform in-service inspection of items you own and operate, and the scope may be extended to repair and alteration inspections for NBIC compliance. It requires a written quality management system meeting NB-381, a National Board review and verification of implementation at your facility, and authorization from the jurisdictional authority.

Two details decide whether the route is worth it for a midstream operator. First, where the applicant has facilities in more than one jurisdiction, a separate Certificate of Accreditation is required for the facilities in each jurisdiction. A company with vessels in four states carries four accreditations, four QMS implementations, four reviews. Second, the certificate expires every three years, and each renewal repeats the review.

You also have to staff it. The OUIO must employ one or more owner-user inspector supervisors, each holding an active Inservice Inspector Commission and, where the scope includes repair and alteration inspections, the R endorsement. A provisional Certificate of Accreditation lets you employ inspectors and lets employees apply for commissions while accreditation is in progress, but no inspections may be performed until the commissions and the certificate are actually issued. Plan on quarters, not weeks.

sections.heading: What API 510 authorises that no commission does
paragraphs: API 510 is the code, not just the credential, and that is the point people miss. The 11th edition, carrying Errata 1 from 2023 and Errata 2 from 2025, governs in-service inspection, rating, repair and alteration for pressure vessels under an owner-user inspection programme. It gives the authorised inspector the machinery to set inspection intervals from corrosion rates and remaining life, to calculate remaining corrosion allowance, to accept a re-rate, and to accept the vessel back into service.

A National Board commission confers none of that. It confers authority to carry out a jurisdictionally required inspection and to report the result in the manner the jurisdiction prescribes. The two credentials answer different questions: the commission answers who is permitted to inspect on the jurisdiction's behalf, and API 510 answers how the owner decides what to inspect, when, and what to do about the answer. Interval logic and risk targeting sit on the API side, which is where [risk-based inspection programme design](/consulting/rbi-program-design) attaches.

For a US midstream operator there is a third pressure entirely. OSHA's process safety management standard requires mechanical integrity for covered process equipment, and API 510 is the recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice that most operators name to satisfy it. That obligation exists whether or not your state jurisdiction inspects unfired pressure vessels, and it is unpacked in [the NDT half of PSM mechanical integrity](/consulting/osha-psm-mechanical-integrity-ndt).

sections.heading: How deep API 510 goes on NDE, and where it stops
paragraphs: Read the body of knowledge and the boundary is unmistakable. The API 510 exam BOK dated September 2025, covering the September 2025, January 2026 and May 2026 windows, lists API 510, RP 571, RP 572 including Annex B, RP 576, RP 577 and RP 578, plus ASME Section V, Section VIII Division 1, Section IX and ASME PCC-2. On ultrasonics it covers ASME Section V Article 23, SE-797 only, the standard practice for measuring thickness by manual pulse-echo contact method.

That means the API 510 certificate tests thickness measurement, radiography, liquid penetrant and magnetic particle general requirements, and nothing about shear wave flaw detection, crack sizing or phased array. An API 510 inspector reviewing a phased array corrosion mapping report is working outside the knowledge the certificate attests. It does not make them wrong; it makes the certificate silent, which is a different thing to say in a bid evaluation.

The gap is filled from the ASNT side, by a Level III who owns the technique and reviews the reads. Naming that role explicitly in the RFP costs nothing and closes the loop, and it is what [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) exists to supply for operators who do not carry a Level III in house.

sections.heading: Writing the midstream RFP clause
paragraphs: Write four separate personnel lines rather than one compound one. Line one, the in-service inspection is performed and signed by an API 510 certified inspector, certificate current at the date of inspection. Line two, NDE is performed by examiners certified under a written practice that the bidder submits with the tender, and interpreted by a certified Level III in the applicable method. Line three, where NBIC repair or alteration acceptance falls in scope, that acceptance is made by a Repair Inspector holding an active National Board commission with the R endorsement.

Line four is the one that saves the tender. State that where a National Board commission is required, the bidder shall identify the employing Authorized Inspection Agency or Owner-User Inspection Organization and provide its Certificate of Accreditation number and the jurisdiction it covers. This makes the employment constraint visible at bid stage instead of at mobilisation, and it lets an honest contractor say plainly that they will subcontract the commissioned scope.

Then add the boring line everyone forgets: a personnel matrix listing each named individual, each certificate, the issuing body and the expiry date, refreshed monthly for the duration. Commissions expire on 31 December regardless of when they were issued, so a January outage inherits a cliff edge every year. Tracking that across a roster is precisely the problem [NDT personnel certification tracking](/erp/ndt-personnel-certification-tracking) solves.

sections.heading: Verification: what to ask a bidder to produce
paragraphs: Ask for images, not assertions. On the API side, the certificate shows the programme, the number and the expiry, and API's exam windows for 2026 ran 2 to 23 January, 8 to 29 May and 4 to 25 September for API 510, which tells you how long a lapsed inspector will take to get current. On the National Board side, the commission card names the employer, and the endorsements are printed on it, so an R endorsement that is claimed but not printed is not held.

Then ask one question that separates real capability from paperwork: which specific reports will each named person sign, and against which code. A bidder who answers cleanly has run this before. A bidder who answers with a capability statement has not. Where the answer looks thin, an independent read of a sample of their existing reports settles it faster than any interview, which is what [NDT report validation](/report-validation) is for.

sections.heading: Where Atlantis fits
paragraphs: Atlantis does not sell API 510, 570 or 653 certification training, and no private company can issue a National Board commission. What we do is the work that sits either side of those credentials for owner-operators: independent validation of the inspection reports your programme depends on, outsourced ASNT Level III coverage for procedure ownership and method scope, and programme audits that reconcile what your RFP asked for against what your files actually contain.

If you are rewriting a midstream inspection RFP this quarter, send us the personnel clause and the deliverables list. We will mark up the places where the commission requirement will exclude your preferred bidder and the places where the API 510 requirement leaves an NDE gap. [Get in touch](/contact) for a demo or a quote on request. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

faq.q: Is a National Board commission better than API 510?
faq.a: They are not ranked, they are scoped. A National Board Inservice Inspector Commission is authority delegated through an employer that the jurisdiction recognises. API 510 is individual certification to run an owner-user in-service programme for pressure vessels. A midstream facility with in-house vessels and NBIC repairs needs both functions covered, frequently by two different people.

faq.q: Can our own employees hold National Board commissions?
faq.a: Yes, if your company holds a National Board Owner-User Inspection Organization Certificate of Accreditation under NB-371. That accreditation requires a quality management system meeting NB-381, a National Board review of the facility, a supervisor holding an active Inservice Inspector Commission, and a separate certificate for each jurisdiction where you have facilities. It expires every three years.

faq.q: What edition of the NBIC applies right now?
faq.a: The National Board Inspection Code, NB-23, 2025 Edition, in four Parts: Part 1 Installation, Part 2 Inspection, Part 3 Repairs and Alterations, and Part 4 Pressure Relief Devices. The National Board publishes a new edition in July of odd-numbered years, so the 2027 Edition is next. Confirm which edition your jurisdiction has adopted, since adoption lags publication.

faq.q: How often do National Board commissions have to be renewed?
faq.a: Annually. RCI-1 states that commissions expire on 31 December, and each endorsement expires with the commission year. The employer makes the renewal and documents that the inspector completed the required continuing education course for each commission and endorsement held. Continuing education is not required in the year a commission or endorsement was first issued.

faq.q: Does Atlantis provide API 510 certification training?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not sell API 510, 570 or 653 certification training. Atlantis delivers ASNT method training to Level I, II and III, outsourced ASNT Level III consulting, independent NDT report validation, and inspection programme audits for owner-operators. Demo or quote on request.

faq.q: Is API 510 certification still worth sponsoring for our team?
faq.a: API reports 21,996 API 510 certifications held as of 30 April 2026, up from 17,709 five years earlier, so demand has not softened. Whether it pays back for a specific engineer depends on the deliverables they will sign, which is the argument worked through in [is API 510 certification worth it in 2026](/blog/api-510-certification-worth-it-2026).

title: API 510 or AMPP CIP Offshore? Read 30 CFR 250.919 First
description: BSEE's annual platform report asks for inspection type and a corrosion protection evaluation. API 510 answers one line, AMPP CIP the other. How to split the budget.
h1: Neither credential wins pre-qual, because pre-qual does not ask for either
answer: Split them by scope, not by prestige. API 510 certifies fixed-equipment integrity, covering separators, scrubbers and knock-out drums. AMPP's Coating Inspector Program certifies coatings and linings. BSEE's contractor selection rule names no certification at all; it asks for documented expertise per employee. Sponsor whichever credential your bid packages keep asking you to evidence.
expansion: The pre-qual question has a boring, verifiable answer. 30 CFR 250.1914 requires an operator to obtain and evaluate a contractor's safety record and environmental performance, to confirm the contractor has written safe work practices, and to document that each contracted employee is knowledgeable and experienced in the work practices needed to do the job safely. It names no certifying body. 30 CFR 250.1916 does the same for mechanical integrity: it demands a documented date, the name, position and signature of the person who performed the inspection, the equipment identifier, the description of the test and the result. So the certification never clears pre-qual by itself. What clears pre-qual is a contractor whose paperwork survives an operator audit, and whose people can produce a defensible record for the scope actually awarded. Both credentials help you get there; neither does it alone.
source: 30 CFR 250.1914 and 250.1916, Safety and Environmental Management Systems, current text; 30 CFR 250.919, as amended at 91 FR 35359, 10 June 2026; AMPP Coating Inspector Program pages and QP 5 accreditation page; AMPP Certification Renewal Guide, January 2023, version 2022.2; AMPP Exam and Re-take Fees schedule effective 1 July 2026; API ICP Schedules and Fees and the ICP status update as of 30 April 2026; Executive Order 14172 of 20 January 2025.

facets.q: Does BSEE require API 510 for offshore pressure vessels?
facets.a: No. 30 CFR 250.1916 sets criteria for mechanical integrity and names no code, no standard and no certifying body. It requires written procedures, inspection frequencies consistent with BSEE regulations and manufacturer recommendations, and documentation carrying a date, the person's name, position and signature, the equipment identifier, a description of the test and the result. API 510 enters as the operator's chosen practice.

facets.q: What has to be in the annual in-service inspection report to BSEE?
facets.a: Five things, submitted by 1 November each year to the Regional Supervisor. The list of fixed and floating platforms inspected in the preceding twelve months. The extent and area covered above water and underwater, plus mooring components for floating platforms. The inspection type employed, for example visual, magnetic particle or ultrasonic. The overall structural condition including a corrosion protection evaluation. And a summary of repairs needed.

facets.q: Did the offshore inspection interval rules change recently?
facets.a: Yes, on 10 June 2026. The amendment at 91 FR 35359 rewrote 30 CFR 250.919(d) to set in-service inspection intervals by Section 6.5.3 Table 3, the Default Inspection Program, of API Recommended Practice 2SIM, using the exposure category BSEE accepted under 250.920 and the survey level from Section 6.5. Compliance with Section 6.5.2.2, risk-based inspection intervals, is explicitly not required.

facets.q: Is AMPP CIP still called NACE CIP Level 1, 2 and 3?
facets.a: AMPP renamed them. Basic Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 1 and SSPC PCI 1, Certified Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 2 and PCI 2, and Senior Certified Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 3 and PCI 3. The old names survive in course titles and in almost every bid document. Write both names into your personnel matrix so a screener recognises either.

facets.q: Which sponsorship pays back faster for a small offshore group?
facets.a: Count the awarded scopes, not the credentials. Structural and coating survey work recurs on the 2SIM default interval and lands squarely on the corrosion protection line of the annual report, so a coatings inspector bills every cycle. Vessel and piping integrity work recurs on the operator's mechanical integrity schedule. Sponsor toward whichever of those two your last twelve months of awards was short of.

facets.q: Does the Gulf of America renaming change any technical requirement?
facets.a: It changes paperwork, nothing else. Executive Order 14172 of 20 January 2025 renamed the water body, and BOEM now titles its lease sales accordingly, from Big Beautiful Gulf 1 in December 2025 onward. The regulations at 30 CFR 250 are unchanged. Update report headers, procedure scopes and pre-qual submissions so a screener never sees a mismatch with the operator's own wording.

sections.heading: What the regulation actually asks a contractor for
paragraphs: Before comparing credentials, read the rule that governs whether you get on the operator's list at all. 30 CFR 250.1914 requires the operator's SEMS programme to document contractor selection criteria, and it is specific about what those criteria contain. When selecting a contractor, the operator must obtain and evaluate information regarding the contractor's safety record and environmental performance, must ensure contractors have their own written safe work practices, and must document an agreement on safety and environmental policies before the contractor begins work.

Paragraph (b) is the one that touches your certification budget. The operator must document that contracted employees are knowledgeable and experienced in the work practices necessary to perform their job in a safe and environmentally sound manner, and documentation of each contracted employee's expertise, together with a copy of the contractor's safety policies and procedures, must be made available to the operator and to BSEE on request. Expertise, evidenced per employee. No scheme is named.

Paragraph (d) then lists the activities the operator must verify contractor personnel can perform, including installation, maintenance or repair of equipment, construction and start-up, turnaround operations, major renovation and specialty work. Inspection sits inside specialty work. So the regulator's question is not which certificate your people hold, it is whether you can produce evidence, per named person, tied to the activity actually awarded.

sections.heading: The annual report that decides which credential you needed
paragraphs: 30 CFR 250.919 is where the two credential families quietly meet. Every operator must submit a comprehensive in-service inspection report annually, by 1 November, to the Regional Supervisor. It lists the fixed and floating platforms inspected in the preceding twelve months, the extent and area of inspection above water and underwater plus mooring components for floating platforms, the type of inspection employed, the overall structural condition of each platform including a corrosion protection evaluation, and a summary of what repairs were needed.

Read paragraph (a)(3) and (a)(4) side by side. The type of inspection employed is given as visual, magnetic particle, ultrasonic testing. That is NDT personnel work, certified under a written practice and interpreted by a Level III. The corrosion protection evaluation is coatings and cathodic protection work, and it is where an AMPP Coating Inspector Program credential earns its keep. One report, two workforces, and neither one substitutes for the other.

This is why the framing of the original question, which credential moves the needle more, gives the wrong answer. Both credentials populate the same regulatory deliverable, on different lines. An offshore inspection group that can only fill one of those lines will keep losing the packages that ask for the other, and the loss will read like a pricing problem when it is a scope-coverage problem.

sections.heading: What changed for offshore inspection intervals in June 2026
paragraphs: 30 CFR 250.919(d) was amended at 91 FR 35359 on 10 June 2026, and the change is worth knowing before your next bid. Operators must now perform in-service inspection of each platform according to the time intervals in Section 6.5.3 Table 3, the Default Inspection Program, of API Recommended Practice 2SIM. The applicable interval comes from Table 3 based on the exposure category BSEE has accepted under 250.920 and the platform's survey level established in accordance with Section 6.5.

There is an explicit carve-out that reads as an instruction. Operators are not required to comply with Section 6.5.2.2 of API RP 2SIM, risk-based inspection intervals. BSEE has, in effect, fixed the offshore structural inspection cadence to a default table rather than allowing it to be argued down by risk analysis. For a contractor, that is good news: the survey volume is predictable, scheduled and recurring rather than negotiable.

It also tells you where the recurring coatings work sits. Structural surveys under 2SIM generate above-water and splash-zone condition assessments cycle after cycle, and the corrosion protection evaluation reported under 250.919(a)(4) is the direct output. A coatings inspector attached to that programme has a defined annual calendar. A fixed-equipment inspector does not, because vessel work runs on the operator's mechanical integrity schedule instead.

sections.heading: What API 510 certifies, and what it does not touch
paragraphs: API 510 governs the in-service inspection, rating, repair and alteration of pressure vessels. Offshore that means separators, scrubbers, knock-out drums, filter vessels and heat exchangers on the production deck. The certification is a written examination, closed book plus open book, sat in scheduled windows. API's 2026 windows for API 510 ran 2 to 23 January, 8 to 29 May and 4 to 25 September, and its published fee schedule lists $875 for API members and $1,125 for non-members, with recertification at $745 and $855.

The body of knowledge dated September 2025 shows the scope precisely: API 510, RP 571, RP 572 including Annex B, RP 576, RP 577 and RP 578, plus ASME Section V, Section VIII Division 1, Section IX and ASME PCC-2. It is a fixed-equipment integrity credential end to end. It says nothing about surface preparation, dry film thickness, holiday detection, adhesion testing or cathodic protection potentials, and no reasonable reading of it suggests otherwise.

The credential is also demonstrably in demand. API records 21,996 API 510 certifications held as of 30 April 2026, against 17,709 five years earlier, inside a portfolio of 79,062 certifications held by 43,837 people in 135 countries. If your group's award mix is weighted toward vessels and piping, that is your sponsorship. If it is weighted toward structures and coatings, it is not, however impressive the letters look on a CV.

sections.heading: What AMPP CIP certifies now that NACE and SSPC have merged
paragraphs: AMPP is the body formed by the merger of NACE International and SSPC, and it has folded the NACE Coating Inspector Program and the SSPC Protective Coatings Inspector programme into a single ladder with new names. Basic Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 1 and PCI 1. Certified Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 2 and PCI 2. Senior Certified Coatings Inspector replaces CIP Level 3 and PCI 3. Seven specialties sit alongside, including Marine, Pipeline, Thermal Spray, Fireproofing, Nuclear, Bridge and Corrosion Under Insulation.

The requirements tighten as you climb. Basic runs on a five or six day in-person course worth 5.2 CEUs, with a written theory exam and a practical exam on the final day. Certified requires the Basic course and an active Basic certification, a five day course, written and practical exams, and two years of verifiable coatings-related work experience before the certificate issues. Senior requires five years of verifiable coatings experience with references, and the assessment is an oral peer review rather than a written paper.

Every level renews on a three-year cycle. AMPP's Certification Renewal Guide requires 1.5 years of work experience in the most recent three-year period, plus professional development of 8 hours for Basic, 12 for Certified and 20 for Senior across the cycle, and an ethics training requirement applies to certification and renewal alike. AMPP also refreshed the Level 2 course, with all public English deliveries transitioned to the updated version by 1 January 2026.

sections.heading: The company-level credential that moves pre-qual more than either
paragraphs: Individual certifications get evaluated on the technical bid. Company accreditations get evaluated at pre-qual, which is the stage the original question is actually about. AMPP QP 5 accredits inspection companies in the industrial coating and lining sector, and it examines exactly what an operator's procurement audit examines: management procedures, established inspection practices, quality control systems, internal audit and review procedures, standards for qualifying and training personnel, and complaint review and resolution. Application is by written submission, followed by an impartial on-site audit at the company's headquarters.

That is the shape of thing that clears an operator's contractor selection process, because it maps directly onto 250.1914's requirement to evaluate a contractor's practices and to confirm written safe work practices exist. An individual certificate cannot do that work. A QP 5 audit report can, and it travels across every operator you bid to rather than being re-argued each time.

The fixed-equipment side has no exact equivalent, which is a real asymmetry worth naming. What substitutes is a documented inspection programme with written procedures, a personnel qualification matrix, and evidence that reads and reports survive independent scrutiny. Building that evidence base is the point of an [NDT programme audit and gap assessment](/consulting/ndt-program-audit-gap-assessment), and it produces the same kind of artefact a pre-qual screener can actually read.

sections.heading: Cost and time, with third-party numbers
paragraphs: Compare the two sponsorships honestly. API 510 costs $875 for members or $1,125 for non-members in application fees, plus study time and a scheduled three-week exam window three times a year. There is no mandatory course, so a disciplined engineer can self-study. The recurring cost is $745 or $855 every three years. Prep courses from third-party providers add substantially on top, and market rates for a week-long API 510 prep course run well into four figures per seat.

AMPP CIP costs the other way round: the exam is cheap and the course is not. AMPP's Exam and Re-take Fees schedule effective 1 July 2026 folds the Basic and Certified Coatings Inspector exam fees into the course fee, and prices a separately purchased computer-based exam at $165. The course is the expenditure. RINA, an AMPP-approved provider, lists CIP Level 1 at $2,829 for AMPP members and $3,104 for non-members, plus VAT where applicable, covering course materials, reference documents and the certificate.

Then add the seat time, which is the number that actually hurts an offshore group. Basic is five or six days in person. Certified is another five days, and cannot be attempted until Basic is held. Reaching Certified is therefore roughly two working weeks off the roster per person, spread across at least two course cycles plus a two-year experience gate before the certificate issues. API 510 costs no classroom days at all if the candidate self-studies, only evenings.

sections.heading: How to split a fixed sponsorship budget across an offshore group
paragraphs: Start from your last twelve months of awarded scopes and lost bids, not from the credential names. Sort every line into two buckets: work that ends up on 250.919(a)(3) as an inspection method, and work that ends up on 250.919(a)(4) as a corrosion protection evaluation. The bucket with the higher value of lost or declined work is where the sponsorship goes. That test takes an afternoon and it beats every argument about which credential is more respected.

Then apply a depth rule to each bucket. On coatings, one Senior Certified Coatings Inspector who can own procedures, adjudicate disputes and sign off failure investigations is worth more than three additional Basic holders, because the Senior credential is the one that unlocks the specification-writing and dispute work. On fixed equipment, an API 510 inspector without a competent NDT layer underneath produces reads they cannot defend, so the second hire is usually a Level III, not a second API 510.

Finally, decide what you are not doing. An offshore group of a dozen people cannot cover structures, coatings, vessels, piping and rope access credibly, and operators can tell. Pick two lanes, be the obvious answer in both, and subcontract the rest. Where the fixed-equipment lane runs into remaining-life and run-or-repair arguments, that is [fitness-for-service under API 579](/consulting/fitness-for-service-api-579) territory and it is worth buying rather than building.

sections.heading: Gulf of America: what changed and what did not
paragraphs: Executive Order 14172 of 20 January 2025 renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, and the federal machinery followed. BOEM now titles its Outer Continental Shelf lease sales accordingly. Big Beautiful Gulf 1 opened bids on 10 December 2025 and drew $300,425,222 in high bids across 181 blocks. BBG2 followed on 11 March 2026 and BBG3 opened on 12 August 2026. Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, two Gulf of America sales are held each year from 2026 through 2039, by 15 March and 15 August.

For a contractor the operational meaning is a sustained, scheduled leasing pipeline rather than a technical change. Nothing in 30 CFR 250 shifted because of the renaming. The SEMS obligations, the mechanical integrity criteria and the annual in-service inspection report are exactly as they were, and the June 2026 amendment to 250.919(d) is a separate and more consequential change.

What does need attention is your document set. Procedure scopes, report headers, personnel matrices and pre-qual submissions that still say Gulf of Mexico will read as stale to a screener comparing them against an operator's own current wording. It is a find-and-replace exercise with a real scoring consequence, and it costs an afternoon.

sections.heading: Where Atlantis fits
paragraphs: Atlantis does not sell API 510 certification training and does not deliver the AMPP Coating Inspector Program; those belong to API and AMPP respectively. What Atlantis delivers is the layer that makes either credential produce evidence an operator will accept: ASNT method training for the UT, MT, PT and VT population your inspection reports depend on, outsourced ASNT Level III consulting for procedure ownership and technique approval, and independent validation of the reports themselves.

That last one is the direct answer to 250.1916(d), which requires each inspection record to carry the date, the name, position and signature of the person who performed it, the equipment identifier, a description of the test and the result. Reports that miss those fields fail an operator audit no matter who signed them, which is the case made in [what makes an NDT report defensible](/report-validation/what-makes-an-ndt-report-defensible).

If you are deciding where to put a fixed sponsorship budget across an offshore group this year, send us your award mix and your last three declined pre-quals. We will tell you which line of the annual report you are short on. [Contact us](/contact) for a demo or a quote on request. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

faq.q: Which credential do Gulf of America operators ask for in pre-qual?
faq.a: Neither, directly. Operator pre-qual under 30 CFR 250.1914 asks for a safety record, environmental performance, written safe work practices and documented per-employee expertise. Certifications appear later, in the technical bid package and its inspection and test plan, where the scope of work names them. Read the scope of work, not the pre-qual portal, to decide what to sponsor.

faq.q: Can one person hold both API 510 and AMPP CIP usefully?
faq.a: Yes, and offshore it is a genuinely strong combination, because a single person can then cover both the inspection-type line and the corrosion protection line of the annual report. The cost is time: API 510 needs a scheduled exam window and self-study, and reaching Certified Coatings Inspector needs roughly two working weeks of classroom plus a two-year experience gate.

faq.q: How long do these certifications last?
faq.a: API 510 runs a three-year cycle with a recertification fee of $745 for API members and $855 for non-members. Every AMPP professional certification recertifies every three years, requiring 1.5 years of work experience in the most recent three-year period, plus 8, 12 or 20 professional development hours per cycle for Basic, Certified and Senior Certified Coatings Inspector respectively.

faq.q: Does AMPP QP 5 accreditation help an inspection company win offshore work?
faq.a: It targets exactly the stage the operator scores. QP 5 evaluates an inspection company's management procedures, inspection practices, quality control, internal audit, personnel qualification standards and complaint resolution, verified by an on-site audit at the company's headquarters. That evidence maps directly onto what SEMS contractor selection requires an operator to obtain and evaluate.

faq.q: Does Atlantis offer API 510 or AMPP CIP training?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not sell API certification training and does not deliver AMPP's Coating Inspector Program. Atlantis delivers ASNT method training to Level I, II and III, outsourced ASNT Level III consulting, independent NDT report validation, and inspection programme audits. Demo or quote on request.

faq.q: Where does mechanical integrity documentation most often fail an operator audit?
faq.a: On the signature and identifier fields. 30 CFR 250.1916(d) requires each inspection or test record to carry the date, the name and position and signature of the person who performed it, the serial number or other identifier of the equipment, a description of what was performed, and the results. Missing equipment identifiers and unsigned reads are the two failures that recur, and both are addressed by [NDT report validation](/report-validation).

title: Required vs Preferred: Sequencing API ICP Spend for 2026 Bids
description: Operator packages separate hard award gates from preferred role credentials. How flow-down works, what 2026 API and AWS fees are, and what to fund first.
h1: How to sequence certification spend against real bid eligibility
answer: Operator pre-qualification packages set two different bars. Contract-award gates are hard: platform score thresholds, OSHA rates, insurance, and PHMSA operator qualification where 49 CFR applies. Named certifications like API 510, 570, 653 and AWS CWI usually attach to individual role slots inside the scope of work, not to company eligibility. Fund the gate first, then the roles you will actually staff.
expansion: The confusion in 2026 comes from reading a scope of work as if it were an eligibility list. It is two documents stapled together. The first part is the commercial and safety gate, and it is genuinely binary: a contractor-management platform score above the operator's threshold, current insurance, an experience modification rate inside the band, and where the asset is a DOT-regulated pipeline, operator qualification records under 49 CFR. Miss any of those and the bid is never scored. The second part lists inspection and NDT roles, each with a credential attached. Those credentials bind the person assigned to the slot, not the company. A contractor with one API 570 holder can bid piping work that needs one API 570 holder. Sequencing spend means funding the gate to completion first, then buying exactly the role credentials the scopes you actually chase name, and treating everything else as [training](/training) you defer.
source: API ICP Schedules & Fees, ICP Examinations and programme pages (api.org); API 510 Eleventh Edition, October 2022, Annex B; AWS Certified Welding Inspector programme page (aws.org); ASNT NDT Level III examination and recertification pages (certification.asnt.org); 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart N and Part 195 Subpart G (eCFR) with PHMSA Operator Qualification guidance; published documentation for ISNetworld, Avetta and Veriforce. All web sources checked August 2026.
